title: ACLED Ukraine Conflict Monitor
machine_readable: Documented REST API returning JSON/CSV event records with latitude/longitude and geo-precision codes. NOTE the legacy host api.acleddata.com is DEAD (does not resolve, verified 2026-08-19) - use OAuth against acleddata.com/api/acled/read, or the key-free HDX mirror.
reliability_notes: Academically coded event data with an explicit geo_precision field, but coordinates are frequently snapped to the nearest named settlement and releases come out weekly, so it is not a live tracker.
description: Curated event dataset and dashboard of battles, shelling, drone/missile strikes and control changes in Ukraine, each geocoded with a stated precision level. The most citable structured event feed for statistical work on where fighting is concentrated.

title: armedconflicts.org Russia-Ukraine War Map
reliability_notes: Aggregator that re-renders third-party control data (primarily DeepState/ISW-derived) with an editorial layer; adds no independent verification and lags its upstream sources.
description: A free live front-line map with settlement labels and daily change notes aimed at a general audience. Useful mainly as a lightweight, ad-free viewer of the consensus line.

title: GeoConfirmed - Ukraine Verified OSINT Map
machine_readable: REST JSON/CSV, no auth. Spec at /openapi/v1.json (NOT /swagger/). GET /api/Placemark/{conflict}/geojson -> 59,359 dated Point features (2014-03-03..2026-08-19); GET /api/Map/export/{conflict}/csv -> 59,337 rows semicolon-delimited UTF-8 BOM with Date;Name;Faction;Origin;Latitude;Longitude;PlusCode;Description;Source;Geolocation;Equipment;Units;OrbatUnits;Id; GET /api/Placemark/detail/{id}; GET /api/Conflict lists 20 conflicts (Ukraine=UKR); POST /api/Placemark/filter for server-side paging.
reliability_notes: Volunteer-verified geolocations to building precision, each row carrying a source URL plus unit/ORBAT attribution - the richest machine-readable event feed found. CAVEAT: /api/placemark/Ukraine (lowercase, no suffix) returns only the icon taxonomy, not data. Coverage is event-driven, so absence of points is not absence of fighting.
description: Volunteer-verified database of precisely geolocated conflict media in Ukraine, each pin carrying coordinates, date and source link. The best source for defensible point coordinates of individual strikes and clashes; the QGIS plugin gives filtered bulk access.

title: Global Conflict Awareness - Ukraine Live Map
reliability_notes: Another 2026 auto-aggregated entrant claiming a five-minute refresh across thousands of events in 17 languages; no published methodology or verification chain, and events are recycled from news feeds, so precision and de-duplication are unverified.
description: Multilingual live event map of missile/drone strikes, frontline incidents and deep strikes into Russia. Included for completeness as a recent entrant; verify anything it shows against GeoConfirmed or DeepState.

title: International Crisis Group - Ukraine War Map: Tracking the Frontlines
machine_readable: None of its own (it embeds DeepState data automatically)
reliability_notes: Explicitly a re-presentation of DeepState's live layer inside a Crisis Group frame, so it carries DeepState's Ukrainian-aligned biases while adding Crisis Group's neutral framing; auto-updates with the upstream source.
description: Crisis Group's zoomable visual explainer of shifting front lines, fed automatically from the DeepState project, with a full-screen mode. Convenient institutional-citable wrapper around DeepState geometry.

title: Liveuamap (Ukraine)
language: English, Ukrainian, Russian, German, Spanish, and 10+ more
machine_readable: Commercial JSON/GeoJSON API sold separately; public site is scrapeable HTML with per-region feeds
reliability_notes: Crowd-sourced newswire pinned to coordinates; fast but pin placement is often approximate to the nearest settlement and unverified items do appear; near real-time (minutes).
description: Live event map that geolocates news reports, strikes, clashes and claims across Ukraine with source links per pin. Best used for 'where did this event happen' rather than for the control line itself.

title: Project Mariupol / OSINT for Ukraine Map
reliability_notes: Volunteer documentation project focused on evidencing damage and alleged war crimes in specific occupied cities; coverage is deep but narrow and updates are project-phase driven rather than continuous.
description: Geolocated evidence map of destruction and incidents in Mariupol and other occupied areas, each point tied to imagery. Useful for micro-geography of occupied cities rather than for the moving contact line.

title: Suriyak - Russian-Ukrainian War Map (Google My Maps)
machine_readable: KML export via Google My Maps (?mid=... on the /maps/d/kml endpoint)
reliability_notes: Prolific single-analyst project covering many conflicts; frontline shapes are hand-drawn and generally credible but sometimes lean toward Russian-claimed positions, and there is no published methodology; updated within hours of major changes.
description: Hand-maintained Google My Maps layer of control polygons and axis-of-advance annotations for Ukraine, mirrored as image maps on Telegram and X. The Google My Maps backing means you can pull the whole layer as KML.

title: Ukraine Control Map (UAControlMap)
machine_readable: None documented; a public data viewer page renders unit/position records as HTML (scrapeable)
reliability_notes: Community-maintained aggregation of frontlines, geolocated clips, unit positions and equipment losses cross-checked against both sides' claims and satellite imagery; quality varies by contributor and the viewer endpoint is intermittently broken.
description: Layered map combining a control line, a Suriyak overlay, custom KML imports and clickable geolocation dots that link back to original source media. Useful for tracing an individual claim to the video it came from.

title: Ukraine Frontline Map (themonstar)
machine_readable: Client-side web app that consumes DeepState, UAControlMap and ukrdailyupdate layers; hosted on GitHub Pages so the front-end source is inspectable
reliability_notes: Hobbyist aggregator with no independent verification: its value is the tooling, not the data, and it is only as fresh as the upstream DeepState/UAControlMap layers it pulls.
description: Free tactical map viewer that overlays the DeepState control layer and third-party event layers on Mapbox/OSM/ESRI/NASA basemaps, adding line-of-sight, terrain, air-defence-range and measurement tools. Useful for analysts who want frontline data plus terrain reasoning in one place.

title: War Monitor (warmonit.com) Ukraine War Map
machine_readable: None documented; ingests ACLED and GDELT feeds upstream
reliability_notes: 2026 aggregator that machine-combines ACLED event data, GDELT news signals and third-party frontline layers with AI-generated briefings; the AI summaries are unverified and the underlying control line is not independently sourced, so treat as a convenience viewer only.
description: Auto-updating conflict map layering strikes, frontline events and news-derived incidents with generated intelligence briefs. Useful for discovery and for its ACLED/GDELT mashup, not for adjudicating control.

title: WarSpotting (Ukraine equipment losses map)
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML per-loss pages with coordinates (site is behind bot protection, so automated access is blocked without a browser-like client)
reliability_notes: Photo/video-confirmed loss database with per-item geolocation where available; more balanced than LostArmour but incomplete, and a large 'unknown location' bucket limits mapping coverage; the site returns HTTP 403 to plain scrapers.
description: Catalogued and partly geolocated Russian and Ukrainian equipment losses with dated evidence, browsable on a map. Useful for corroborating that fighting occurred at a specific coordinate on a specific date.

title: Wikipedia Template:Russo-Ukrainian War detailed map
machine_readable: Wikipedia/Wikimedia REST and MediaWiki APIs expose the template wikitext and the underlying settlement control lists; the SVG/map file is downloadable from Commons
handle_or_feed: https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php (action=parse on the template); see also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_control_during_the_Russo-Ukrainian_war
reliability_notes: Consensus-edited from ISW, DeepState and both sides' claims, so it is usually a reasonable middle estimate, but it is subject to edit wars and typically trails specialist maps by a day or more.
description: The zoomable detailed control map embedded across Wikipedia's Russo-Ukrainian War articles, with a per-settlement control legend and citations. Handy as a neutral, freely licensed baseline and for reconciling conflicting claims about a specific village.

title: LostArmour Map
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML (map markers link to per-item pages with photo evidence)
reliability_notes: Pro-Russian equipment-loss database that only counts photo/video-confirmed items; its evidence handling is reasonably conservative but its coverage is heavily skewed toward Ukrainian losses, so it must be paired with Ukrainian/neutral trackers.
description: Interactive map of documented destroyed and captured vehicles with photo evidence per marker, giving coordinates for where armour was actually hit. Useful as a Russian-side geolocated incident layer and for identifying active assault corridors.

title: Rybar Map (map.rybar.ru)
handle_or_feed: Telegram https://t.me/rybar ; https://t.me/s/rybar for the web mirror
reliability_notes: Well-resourced pro-Kremlin milblogger project: cartography is competent and often fast, but it systematically overstates Russian control and advances and is used for information operations; the map itself now sits behind registration plus a paid subscription.
description: Rybar's interactive conflict map with user-submitted events and its own frontline rendering, covering Ukraine and other theatres. Worth consulting only as the Russian-claim upper bound to bracket Ukrainian and Western estimates.

title: Air Alarm Map of Ukraine (alerts.in.ua)
machine_readable: Documented JSON API with oblast and hromada-level alert states plus history; official Python/JS clients
reliability_notes: Mirrors official Ukrainian civil-defence alert declarations, so it is authoritative about alerts but says nothing directly about the frontline; alert granularity is oblast/raion, and a raid alert covers a whole region rather than a target.
description: Real-time map and API of active air-raid alerts by region and hromada across Ukraine, including artillery-threat states for frontline raions. The frontline-adjacent raion alert types are a cheap proxy for which areas are within tube-artillery range.

title: DeepStateMap.Live
machine_readable: Public JSON/GeoJSON API, no auth (verified 2026-08-19): full historical frontline time series retrievable.
handle_or_feed: GET /api/history/public (index of 1732 snapshots 2022-04-03..2026-08-19, fields id/description/descriptionEn/updatedAt/datetime/createdAt); GET /api/history/last ({id,map:FeatureCollection} ~628KB); GET /api/history/{id}/geojson (any past snapshot). NOTE /api/history 401, /api/history/last/geojson 404.
reliability_notes: Ukrainian volunteer team (DeepStateUA) with contacts inside the Ukrainian military; the most granular public control layer but Ukrainian-aligned and criticised for sometimes optimistic grey-zone rendering; typically hours behind events, occasionally a day on quiet sectors.
description: The de-facto reference interactive map of territorial control in Ukraine, with occupied/liberated/grey-zone polygons, dated history slider and point markers for strikes and clashes. Its undocumented GeoJSON history endpoint makes it the single best machine-readable source for 'where is the line'.

title: Frontelligence Insight
machine_readable: RSS for posts; geospatial products are published as annotated images, no data export
reliability_notes: Ukrainian-led analytical team whose geospatial vehicle-loss and frontline reports are detailed and well-sourced, but the perspective is pro-Ukrainian and much in-depth output sits behind a paid tier; cadence is weekly-to-irregular rather than live.
description: Publishes geospatial analyses such as vehicle-loss heat maps by sector and frontline assessments of specific axes. Useful for understanding why a sector is moving, and for loss geography that pure control maps omit.

title: National Mine Action Platform (demine.gov.ua)
machine_readable: Portions published as open data on Ukraine's open-data portal; no documented public GeoJSON API for hazardous-area polygons
reliability_notes: Official Ministry of Economy platform, so authoritative on survey and clearance status, but hazardous-area geometry is restricted/partial and reporting lags clearance work; roughly 139,000-144,000 sq km is only 'potentially contaminated', not confirmed mined.
description: Ukraine's official mine-action portal with maps of surveyed, hazardous and cleared land plus operator activity by region. Its deoccupied-area contamination layer is the best public indicator of where the front recently was.

title: SaveEcoBot Fire Map (Ukraine, NASA FIRMS)
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML map; upstream data is the NASA FIRMS API, which is the better programmatic route
reliability_notes: Repackages NASA FIRMS detections hourly for Ukraine with wind overlays; inherits all FIRMS false-positive caveats (crop burning, wildfires) and adds no verification of its own.
description: Ukraine-focused rendering of NASA FIRMS thermal hotspots with wind direction and 24-hour filtering, clipped to Ukrainian oblasts. Convenient shortcut for spotting frontline heat-signature clusters without querying FIRMS directly.

title: Texty.org.ua 'Under Fire' Shelling Map
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML/embedded dataset in the visualisation
reliability_notes: Aggregated from official Ukrainian reporting rather than independent verification, so it reflects what authorities announced; coverage is retrospective and updates are project-driven, not continuous.
description: Filterable interactive map of where and when Russian shelling, missile and drone strikes were reported, broken down by weapon type over time. Good for mapping strike geography and intensity by region.

title: Texty.org.ua Combat Operations Map
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML/embedded JSON in the visualisation
reliability_notes: Built strictly from General Staff communiques and oblast military administration statements, so it marks only officially named settlements and explicitly avoids asserting exact positions; manual updates make cadence uneven, and the team warns it must not be used for evacuation decisions.
description: Ukrainian data-journalism map of combat activity keyed to officially mentioned settlements, with the reporting source behind each point. Useful as an official-statement-only cross-check against OSINT-drawn frontlines.

title: Black Bird Group Map
reliability_notes: Finnish OSINT collective with an explicitly relativist definition of control (whoever dominates an area more) and unusually candid methodology write-ups; smaller team means fewer sectors updated per day than DeepState.
description: Frontline map and accompanying situation assessments from the Black Bird Group analysts, focused on operational-level dynamics and encirclement risk. Valuable as a methodologically explicit Western alternative to both ISW and Ukrainian maps.

title: Brady Africk - Russian Field Fortifications in Ukraine
machine_readable: None documented on the newsletter; the same fortification polylines are published as an ArcGIS feature layer used in ISW web maps
reliability_notes: Each point links to the satellite image it was derived from, so individual features are verifiable, but the author states the map is explicitly not exhaustive and does not distinguish trenches from barriers or dragon's teeth; updated as new imagery arrives.
description: Interactive map of Russian trenches, barriers and prepared defensive lines in and around Ukraine, digitised from Sentinel-2, Planet, Airbus and Maxar imagery. Essential for understanding where the defensive lines behind the contact line actually run.

title: Def Mon Operational Map Ukraine (ScribbleMaps)
machine_readable: ScribbleMaps supports KML/GeoJSON export of a public map from its own UI (no documented API)
reliability_notes: Widely respected pro-Ukrainian analyst known for careful annotation of Russian assault waves and artillery, but the author has publicly cut back time spent on the map, so freshness is inconsistent; verify the last-edited date before citing.
description: Detailed ScribbleMaps overlay of frontline positions, strongpoints and assault directions with a legend, used as the base for Def Mon's frontline-change threads. Good for tactical-level detail on active sectors when recently updated.

title: Eyes on Russia Map (Centre for Information Resilience)
machine_readable: None public; researchers can request database access from CIR
reliability_notes: CIR verifies each entry before publication and states its confidence, so accuracy is good, but the verification pipeline introduces days of lag and the map is event-based, not a control layer.
description: CIR's verified database and map of videos, photos and satellite imagery of the war, covering strikes, damage and troop movements with source links. Strong for building an auditable incident record at specific coordinates.

title: ISW / CTP Interactive Map: Russia's Invasion of Ukraine
machine_readable: Public ArcGIS REST FeatureServer layers behind the story map (queryable as JSON/GeoJSON via f=geojson)
reliability_notes: ISW/CTP is deliberately conservative: it maps only 'assessed' control it can corroborate, so it usually lags DeepState by days and under-reports Russian gains, but it is the most methodologically transparent Western baseline.
description: ISW and AEI's Critical Threats Project daily control-of-terrain map with layers for assessed Russian control, assessed advances in the past 24h, claimed Russian territory, claimed Ukrainian counteroffensives and Russian field fortifications. The underlying ArcGIS feature services are open and directly consumable.

title: ISW Interactive Time-lapse: Russia's War in Ukraine
machine_readable: None (rendered story map; underlying layers are in the ISW ArcGIS org)
reliability_notes: Built from ISW's own conservative assessments and refreshed roughly monthly, so it is a retrospective product, not a current-situation tool.
description: Animated month-by-month time-lapse of assessed control changes since February 2022. Useful for measuring rate-of-advance and for sanity-checking claims about how fast a sector actually moved.

title: ISW Map Room
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML index; links out to ArcGIS story maps and static campaign-assessment maps (PNG)
reliability_notes: Authoritative but conservative and slower than Ukrainian OSINT; the index page is the reliable entry point because ISW has repeatedly changed individual map URLs.
description: ISW's canonical hub listing every current interactive and static map product, filterable to the Russia-Ukraine portfolio. Use it to discover ISW map URLs rather than hard-coding deep links that rot.

title: NOELREPORTS Live Ukraine War Map
machine_readable: None documented yet (Leaflet front end; product still in pre-launch)
reliability_notes: Long-established pro-Ukrainian OSINT news account, but the map product itself was still labelled pre-launch/test mode as of August 2026, so layers and uptime are unproven and advance/recapture markers should be cross-checked.
description: A 2026 entrant: dashboard-style live map promising 12+ layers including frontline changes, verified OSINT events, thermal hotspots and air-raid alerts. Worth tracking as it matures but not yet a dependable primary source.

title: NZZ Ukraine Front Line Interactive Map
reliability_notes: High-quality newsroom cartography built on ISW/OSINT inputs with explicit caveats that no official side confirms control; editorially updated, so it can trail specialist maps by a day and is subject to the publisher's paywall metering.
description: Neue Zurcher Zeitung's continuously updated interactive front-line map with historical comparison views and change annotations. A good, well-annotated general-reader reference for the current line.

title: Poulet Volant frontline sector maps
machine_readable: None (image maps; posts available via X/Mastodon feeds)
reliability_notes: Highly regarded for careful, conservatively drawn sector maps with explicit uncertainty caveats; output is raster images rather than data, and coverage is sector-by-sector rather than whole-front.
description: Daily per-sector frontline maps (Pokrovsk, Kupiansk, Kostiantynivka, etc.) with timestamped change annotations, also feeding the War Mapper Telegram channel. Useful as an independent second opinion on contested settlements.

title: UA Map (map.ukrdailyupdate.com) - Andrew Perpetua
machine_readable: None documented; the operators explicitly ask users not to embed the live map to limit server load
reliability_notes: Run by Andrew Perpetua, whose daily geolocation of loss and strike footage is respected for volume and for separating confirmed from claimed items; it is pro-Ukrainian in framing and coverage depends on how much footage surfaces each day.
description: Andrew Perpetua's interactive map of daily geolocated strikes, equipment losses and frontline positions, refreshed roughly hourly with measurement and line-drawing tools. One of the best sources for intensity-by-location on a given day.

title: Ukraine Invasion Interactive Web Map (ISW ArcGIS layers)
machine_readable: ArcGIS REST FeatureServer endpoints for each layer; supports f=json / f=geojson queries, attribute filters and pagination
reliability_notes: This particular web map is a third-party remix of ISW's official web map, but it points at ISW's own live public feature services, which are the actual authoritative data; layer IDs have changed historically so enumerate the service directory rather than hard-coding.
description: An ArcGIS web map that exposes ISW's control-of-terrain, 24-hour-gains and Russian-fortification feature layers as directly queryable REST services. This is the practical way for a developer to pull ISW frontline polygons as GeoJSON.

title: War Mapper
machine_readable: None (Substack RSS available for the posts, not the geometry)
reliability_notes: One of the longest-running territorial-control accounts; deliberately conservative monthly/periodic net-change accounting rather than live tracking, so it is a good cross-check on gain/loss arithmetic but never current.
description: Publishes periodic Ukraine control maps and square-kilometre net territorial-change statistics, co-produced with Poulet Volant. Best used to quantify how much ground actually changed hands over a month.

title: awesome-osint (jivoi)
reliability_notes: Broad OSINT tool index, not Ukraine-specific; many links rot.
description: Long-running curated index of OSINT tools and databases, including geolocation and mapping resources usable for frontline work.

title: Awesome-OSINT-List (Astrosp)
reliability_notes: General-purpose OSINT list with a War/Military Conflict section; quality varies by entry.
description: Curated OSINT tool collection containing a dedicated war and military-conflict category relevant to Ukraine tracking.

title: OSINT War Room (Hue-Jhan)
machine_readable: Open-source Python dashboard; wires GDELT, Overpass, OpenSky, AISStream, t.me/s scrapes, RSS
reliability_notes: Hobby project, not authoritative, but its source wiring is a working reference implementation for an aggregator.
description: Open-source tactical dashboard that aggregates conflict OSINT feeds into one map; valuable as a blueprint for which feeds are practically ingestable and how.

title: OSINT Guide: Tracking the Ukraine War (Ukraine War Analytics)
reliability_notes: Introductory methodology overview; names only the best-known sources, no milbloggers.
description: Beginner-to-intermediate guide to Ukraine war OSINT method, naming core tools (ISW, Oryx, DeepState, Liveuamap, Copernicus, Flightradar24).

title: Clash Report
reliability_notes: Turkish-run conflict-news outlet (~110K on Telegram, larger on X). Fast global war feed covering Ukraine among other conflicts; captions are often thin and location claims are inherited from source channels, with occasional mislabelled footage.
description: Rapid English-language conflict footage and event reporting across Ukraine and other theatres.

title: Conflicts Tracker (Telegram)
machine_readable: t.me/s HTML scrape / Telegram Bot API
reliability_notes: Aggregates from other channels without independent verification.
description: English-language multi-conflict tracking channel that reposts Ukraine frontline and strike reports.

title: Monitor The Situation (Telegram aggregator)
machine_readable: t.me/s HTML scrape / Telegram Bot API
reliability_notes: Fast global conflict aggregator with low verification standards; treat as a lead generator, not evidence.
description: High-volume English-language breaking-news aggregator covering Ukraine strikes and frontline claims.

title: OSINT Warfare (Telegram)
machine_readable: t.me/s HTML scrape / Telegram Bot API
reliability_notes: Mixed sourcing, occasional geolocation; verify independently.
description: English OSINT channel posting combat footage and strike reports, sometimes with geolocation.

title: Status-6
reliability_notes: Long-running conflict-news account (also YouTube @archer83able). Broad, fast coverage of strike and drone footage with reasonable sourcing; leans pro-Ukrainian, and location detail is often only 'near <settlement>'.
description: OSINT-driven coverage of strikes, drone warfare and equipment losses in Ukraine and elsewhere.

title: Telegago (Google CSE for Telegram)
reliability_notes: Community-maintained Google Custom Search across t.me previews and Telegram directories; the fastest way to find a channel's current slug or to full-text search milblogger posts that Google has indexed. Coverage is limited to what Google has crawled, so absence proves nothing.
description: Search engine over public Telegram channels, groups and post previews.

title: Telegram Bot API / MTProto client APIs
reliability_notes: Official APIs; MTProto clients (Telethon/TDLib) can read full channel history including preview-disabled channels, which the Bot API cannot. Requires a phone-number-bound account, and mass scraping risks account bans - the standard practical constraint on building a milblogger corpus.
description: Official programmatic access to Telegram channel content and history for automated collection.

title: Telegram public channel previews (t.me/s/)
reliability_notes: The core ingestion mechanism for this whole category: any public channel that has not disabled preview renders its last ~20 posts as static HTML with ISO timestamps, permalinks and media URLs. Caveat: channels can disable preview (verified: @grey_zone, @rsotmdivision, @donbassdevushka, @vchkogpu), pagination needs the ?before= parameter, and there is no rate-limit guarantee.
description: Web-readable mirror of any public Telegram channel's recent posts, usable for scraping without an account.

title: Telemetr.me
reliability_notes: Alternative Telegram analytics service with strong coverage of Ukrainian and Russian channels, useful for resolving renamed or migrated handles and for tracking whether a channel is still active. Paywalled beyond basic profile data.
description: Channel discovery, subscriber/post analytics and historical handle tracking for Telegram.

title: TGStat
reliability_notes: Russian-based Telegram analytics with the most complete index of Russian- and Ukrainian-language war channels, including handle history, subscriber trends and full-text search. Being Russian-hosted, coverage of Ukrainian channels can be uneven and metrics are inflated by view-farming; it is a discovery tool, not an evidence source.
description: Search, ranking and analytics for Telegram channels, plus an API for post-level data collection.

title: Andrei Marochko (LPR)
reliability_notes: LPR 'people's militia' officer and TASS-quoted commentator (~15K subs but very widely republished). The single most prolific source of premature Russian advance claims on the Kupiansk/Lyman/Siversk axes; his statements are routinely repeated by Russian state media and should be treated as claims, not observations.
description: Daily claims about Russian progress on the Luhansk-direction axes and Ukrainian losses.

title: ANNA News
reliability_notes: ~237K subs; long-standing pro-Russian war-media outlet (Abkhazian Network News Agency) with embedded crews. Openly propagandistic, historically inaccurate on capture claims; footage can still be useful for dating Russian presence.
description: Embedded Russian frontline video reports and axis claims.

title: Archangel Spetsnaz Z (@rusich_army) - semi-dormant
reliability_notes: VDV-linked Z-channel historically among Russia's top military channels; the public preview now shows only sporadic posts (latest 5 Jul 2026, ~11.6K subs), suggesting a migration or restriction - verify before relying on it. Content when active is nationalist and unverified.
description: Airborne-forces-adjacent frontline content, tactical clips and pro-war commentary.

title: Colonelcassad (Boris Rozhin)
reliability_notes: ~743K subs; Crimea-based analyst at the CIGR, one of ISW's most-cited Russian milbloggers. Aggregates and comments on all Russian axes with relatively sober tone by Z-channel standards, but is firmly pro-Kremlin, repeats MoD framing and amplifies unverified capture claims.
description: Aggregated Russian frontline claims, strike reports and commentary on Russian military politics.

title: Conflict Intelligence Team (CIT)
reliability_notes: Exiled Russian investigative OSINT group (~89K subs; citeam.org, English on x.com/CITeam_en). Methodologically strict, publishes evidence and admits uncertainty; anti-Kremlin but critical of both sides' claims. Slower than milbloggers and not a continuous frontline mapper.
description: Verification of strike and loss claims, Russian unit/mobilisation research, weekly war summaries.

title: Dimitriev (Russkiy Orientalist)
reliability_notes: ~129K subs; pro-Kremlin analyst frequently cited by ISW for elite-adjacent commentary. Analytical tone, no geolocation, and consistently frames events to Russian advantage.
description: Political-military analysis of the war and Russian internal debates.

title: Donbass Devushka
reliability_notes: English-language pro-Russian channel run by a US-based operator exposed in 2023 (linked to leaked-documents amplification). Deliberate disinformation vehicle aimed at Western audiences; web preview disabled. No evidentiary value.
description: English-language pro-Russian war content, claims and commentary for Western audiences.

title: Donbass reshaet (Donbass Decides)
reliability_notes: ~43K subs; Donbas-based pro-Russian frontline channel. Local detail on Donetsk-axis fighting but wholly partisan and unverified.
description: Donbas frontline video and claims, occupation-area local news.

title: Fighterbomber
reliability_notes: ~519K subs; the authoritative Russian VKS-insider channel (note: the older @fighter_bomber handle is now only a backup pointer). Genuinely well-informed on Russian aviation losses, glide-bomb and Shahed employment and often admits Russian aircraft losses before officials do; strongly pro-war and hostile to Ukraine, with no geolocation.
description: Russian air-force insider reporting: aircraft/UAV losses, weapons employment, aircrew news.

title: Geroman
reliability_notes: Pro-Russian mapper/aggregator producing frontline graphics and casualty claims. Consistently maximalist about Russian gains and Ukrainian losses; maps derive from Russian claims rather than geolocated evidence.
description: Russian-perspective frontline maps, strike claims and war statistics.

title: GREY ZONE
machine_readable: None (web preview disabled; requires Telegram client/API)
reliability_notes: Wagner-descended hardline channel, historically ~500K subs, still active post-2023 but with web preview disabled so t.me/s scraping fails - ingestion needs an authenticated Telegram client. Highly aggressive nationalist content, hostile to the Russian MoD, and unreliable on specifics.
description: Wagner-aligned frontline claims, assault-unit content and attacks on Russian military leadership.

title: Idi i smotri (Go and See)
reliability_notes: ~129K subs; graphic Z-channel combat-footage feed. Almost no verification or location metadata; footage frequently re-dated or misattributed.
description: Russian combat and drone-strike video with nationalist captions.

title: Igor Girkin/Strelkov
reliability_notes: Channel of the imprisoned ex-'DPR defence minister'; historically the loudest ultranationalist critic of the Russian MoD and thus a useful signal when Russian operations are going badly. Frequently exaggerates in the pessimistic direction and posts no geolocated evidence; content is now proxy-managed. (The lookalike @strelkov_info is a squatter.)
description: Hardline critique of Russian military performance and command, with front-wide commentary.

title: Khroniki Geraney (Chronicles of Geraniums)
reliability_notes: Pro-Russian channel tracking Shahed/Geran and missile strike waves against Ukraine, often naming target cities and facilities in near real time. Useful for reconstructing strike packages, but it publishes Russian target claims (including 'confirmed hits' that were intercepts) and celebrates strikes on civilian-adjacent infrastructure.
description: Real-time tracking and claimed results of Russian long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukraine.

title: Kotsnews (Aleksandr Kots)
reliability_notes: ~476K subs; Komsomolskaya Pravda war correspondent and member of Russia's Human Rights Council. Embedded reporting with heavy Kremlin framing; frequently first to claim Russian entry into a settlement, often before it is verifiable.
description: Embedded reports, interviews and claims from Russian axes of advance.

title: Legitimniy (Легитимный)
reliability_notes: Companion of the same anonymous 'insider' network as @rezident_ua; treated by Ukrainian and Western analysts as Russian-aligned influence content. Do not use as evidence for anything factual.
description: Anonymous claims about Ukrainian political and military decision-making.

title: LOSTARMOUR
reliability_notes: ~88K subs; the pro-Russian counterpart to Oryx, cataloguing destroyed equipment with photo evidence (lostarmour.info). Documentation is comparatively systematic but asymmetric: Ukrainian losses are catalogued far more diligently than Russian ones, and captions carry Russian framing.
description: Photo-documented equipment-loss cataloguing and strike-video archiving from the Russian side.

title: Mash
reliability_notes: ~3.1M subs; Kremlin-adjacent tabloid with fast access to Russian emergency-services sources. The most useful Russian channel for early reporting of Ukrainian deep-strike impacts inside Russia (refineries, airbases), though details are often wrong initially and downplay damage.
description: Breaking incident reporting inside Russia, including drone-strike impacts and emergency-services footage.

title: Michael Nacke (Maikl Naki)
reliability_notes: Exiled Russian anti-war journalist (YouTube channel UCgpSieplNxXxLXYAzJLLpng, 2M+ subs); prosecuted in absentia in Russia. Analytical daily war reviews built on OSINT and DeepState/ISW products, not original geolocation; strongly anti-Kremlin framing and occasionally over-optimistic about Ukrainian prospects.
description: Daily Russian-language video/text war analysis for a Russian-speaking anti-war audience.

title: MIG Rossii (MIG of Russia)
reliability_notes: ~475K subs; nationalist commentary channel often cited by ISW as a milblogger voice. Aggregation plus opinion, no geolocation, routinely amplifies unverified frontline claims.
description: Pro-war commentary and aggregation of Russian frontline and political claims.

title: Military Chronicle (@milchronicles) - dormant
reliability_notes: Formerly a widely ISW-cited, relatively analytical Russian channel; verified as effectively dead - the last post on the public preview is 23 Jan 2025 and the subscriber count has collapsed to ~1.1K. Retain only for historical corpus work.
description: Historical archive of analytical Russian-perspective frontline assessments.

title: Narodnaya militsiya DNR
reliability_notes: Official DPR 'people's militia' channel. Pure occupation-authority messaging: shelling accusations against Ukraine and advance claims, systematically unverified.
description: DPR official claims on shelling, casualties and frontline activity in Donetsk oblast.

title: Neofitsialnyi Bezsonov 'Z' (Daniil Bezsonov)
reliability_notes: ~246K subs; former DPR official turned milblogger, regularly cited by ISW. Pro-Russian and quick to assert advances; occasional internal criticism of Russian command.
description: Donbas-focused commentary on Russian operations and occupation politics.

title: Nikolaevskiy Vanek
reliability_notes: Pro-Russian informer channel focused on Mykolaiv/Kherson, publishing claimed Ukrainian troop and equipment locations. Functions partly as a targeting/informant channel: claims are unverified, sometimes fabricated, and its 'geolocations' are hostile intelligence claims rather than OSINT verification.
description: Claimed Ukrainian positions, movements and strike results in the Mykolaiv/Kherson area.

title: Novosti SVO, Rossii i mira
reliability_notes: Huge-volume pro-Russian war-news aggregator (400K+ posts). No verification and heavy repetition of MoD and milblogger claims; usable only as a bulk corpus for narrative tracking.
description: Continuous aggregation of Russian war news, frontline claims and strike reports.

title: Operation Z: Voenkory Russkoy Vesny
reliability_notes: ~1.46M subs; the 'Operation Z' aggregator of Russian war correspondents. Very fast and very unreliable: mass-reposts capture and casualty claims with no verification and a strong triumphalist slant.
description: Aggregated Russian war-correspondent claims, strike reports and frontline video.

title: Orchestra W (Wagner fan channel)
reliability_notes: Wagner-fandom channel; preview disabled so not web-scrapeable. Purely promotional/propagandistic, no geolocation, and claims about Wagner-successor deployments are often speculative.
description: Wagner-related news, recruitment material and glorification content.

title: Philologist in Ambush (Filolog v zasade)
reliability_notes: ~60K subs; frequently ISW-cited milblogger with a more analytical register and willingness to describe Russian problems. Still committed pro-war advocacy; no geolocation and prone to accepting Russian capture claims.
description: Essays and situation commentary on Russian operations and military reform debates.

title: Povyornutye na voine (Voenacher)
reliability_notes: ~668K subs; popular Z-channel with frontline footage and analysis. Nationalist, quick to claim advances, and mixes genuine unit video with unsourced aggregation.
description: Russian frontline video, strike claims and pro-war commentary.

title: Reverse Side of the Medal (RSOTM, Rusich-linked)
reliability_notes: Wagner/Rusich-associated channel; web preview is disabled (t.me/s returns no posts), so it cannot be scraped without a Telegram client. Extremist content, no verification value; relevant mainly for tracking assault-detachment and Wagner-successor activity.
description: Wagner-successor and Rusich-adjacent unit content, recruitment and frontline claims.

title: Rezident (Резидент)
reliability_notes: Anonymous channel posing as a Ukrainian insider source; widely assessed as a Russian influence operation aimed at Ukrainian audiences. Fabricated 'insider' claims about Ukrainian command and politics; zero verification value, useful only for mapping disinformation.
description: Purported insider leaks about Ukrainian leadership, mobilisation and frontline collapse.

title: Romanov Light
reliability_notes: ~152K subs; ISW-cited milblogger giving daily axis summaries. Pro-Russian and consistently optimistic about Russian progress; occasionally admits stalls, which makes those admissions informative.
description: Daily Russian-perspective summaries of fighting on each axis with commentary.

title: Ruslan Leviev (CIT founder)
reliability_notes: Personal channel of CIT's founder; same evidentiary standards as CIT but more commentary and personal analysis. Anti-Kremlin perspective, designated/prosecuted in Russia.
description: Commentary on Russian military developments, CIT findings and war-crime investigations.

title: Rybar (Mikhail Zvinchuk)
reliability_notes: The largest Russian-language military-analysis channel (~1.55M subs) run by ex-Russian MoD press officer Mikhail Zvinchuk; US-sanctioned. Cartography is genuinely high quality and often ahead of Ukrainian maps on Russian advances, but it is MoD-adjacent and systematically marks Russian gains early, understates Russian losses, and pushes information operations; treat maps as a Russian-claim layer to be intersected with Ukrainian-side maps.
description: Multiple daily mapped situation reports for every axis, strike claims and geopolitical commentary.

title: Rybar in English
reliability_notes: Official English mirror of Rybar (~80K subs) carrying the same maps and the same systematic pro-Russian bias and early-advance claims; useful for non-Russian-reading pipelines.
description: English translations of Rybar's mapped frontline summaries and strike claims.

title: SILOVIKI
reliability_notes: ~185K subs; security-services-adjacent pro-war aggregator. Mixes real leaks with rumour and disinformation, no verification, no coordinates.
description: Pro-Kremlin security/military news aggregation and frontline claims.

title: Sladkov+ (Aleksandr Sladkov)
reliability_notes: ~700K subs; VGTRK state-TV war correspondent. Effectively state messaging with frontline colour; useful only for reading the official Russian line, minimal verifiable geographic detail.
description: State-TV-aligned frontline reportage and commentary on Russian forces.

title: SolovievLive
reliability_notes: ~1.1M subs; Vladimir Solovyov's state-TV ecosystem channel. Pure propaganda and escalation rhetoric; no verification, no location value, but a good index of official Russian narrative.
description: State-TV war commentary, frontline claim amplification and political messaging.

title: Svodki opolcheniya Novorossii (Z.O.V.)
reliability_notes: ~223K subs and ~289K photos; enormous archive of Donbas 'militia' summaries dating to 2014. Volume is its value; reliability is poor, with heavy recycling of old footage and separatist propaganda framing.
description: Continuous Russian/separatist frontline summaries, video and strike claims.

title: Tot samyi Olen (@trueolen)
reliability_notes: Kremlin-adjacent 'insider' commentary channel; last public post observed 18 May 2026, so treat as low-activity. Political rather than operational, no geolocation.
description: Anonymous elite-adjacent commentary on Russian war policy and personnel.

title: Two Majors (Dva Majora)
reliability_notes: ~1.16M subs; anonymous serving-officer channel heavily cited by ISW. Often has genuine unit-level detail and criticises Russian command failures, which makes it a useful negative indicator; still nationalist propaganda, frequently premature on captures and hostile to any Ukrainian success reporting.
description: Axis-by-axis Russian frontline summaries, criticism of Russian command and fundraising for units.

title: VChK-OGPU
reliability_notes: Anonymous channel claiming Russian security-service sources; web preview disabled. Mixed record: some genuine leaks about Russian MoD/FSB affairs later corroborated, plus a lot of unverifiable or planted material. Never treat as a location source.
description: Alleged insider leaks on Russian security services, MoD corruption and casualties.

title: Vladimir Rogov
reliability_notes: ~100K subs; Russian occupation official for Zaporizhzhia (Public Chamber commission chair). Source of Russian occupation-authority claims about Zaporizhzhia axis and ZNPP; heavily propagandistic and repeatedly wrong or premature on Russian advances.
description: Occupation-administration claims on the Zaporizhzhia front, strikes and the Zaporizhzhia NPP.

title: Voenkor Kotenok (Yuri Kotenok)
reliability_notes: ~315K subs; veteran Russian war correspondent. Nationalist commentary with occasional insider criticism of the MoD; low geolocation value and prone to alarmist or triumphalist claims depending on the day.
description: Commentary and claims on Russian operations, strikes and military-political disputes.

title: Voennaya khronika (voenhronika.ru)
reliability_notes: Active pro-Russian war-video channel tied to voenhronika.ru, covering Ukraine since 2014. Propagandistic captions, no geolocation discipline. Note: the better-known analytic 'Voennaya Khronika' handle @milchronicles has been dormant since January 2025.
description: Russian-side war video archive and daily frontline claim summaries.

title: Voennyi Osvedomitel (Military Informant)
reliability_notes: ~615K subs, 115K photos; among the most technically competent Russian channels for equipment identification and loss documentation, and it does publish Russian losses. Still pro-Russian in framing and selective, but its identification work is comparatively trustworthy.
description: Weapons/vehicle identification, documented losses on both sides and technical war analysis.

title: Vypuskayte Krakena (RLZ the Kraken)
reliability_notes: ~505K subs; high-volume Z-channel mixing frontline video with hardline nationalist agitation. Very low verification standard, frequent recycled or mislabelled footage; treat all locations as unconfirmed.
description: Russian frontline and strike video with nationalist commentary.

title: War on Fakes (Voina s feikami)
reliability_notes: ~387K subs; Kremlin-aligned 'fact-checking' operation created to rebut Ukrainian and Western reporting. Documented disinformation vehicle: its 'debunkings' regularly invert verified events (e.g. strike attribution). Include only to track Russian narrative moves, never as verification.
description: Pro-Russian 'debunking' of Ukrainian and Western war claims.

title: WarGonzo (Semyon Pegov)
reliability_notes: ~749K subs; state-decorated war correspondent embedded with Russian units. Real on-the-ground presence, so his datelines indicate where Russian forces actually are, but reporting is openly propagandistic, routinely announces the 'capture' of settlements days-to-weeks early, and never publishes coordinates.
description: Embedded video reporting from Russian units, interviews and claims of advances by axis.

title: Yevgeny Poddubny (Poddubny ZOV)
reliability_notes: ~573K subs; VGTRK state correspondent, EU-sanctioned. Reports from Russian-held areas so his locations show Russian presence, but content is state propaganda: exaggerated Ukrainian losses, early capture claims, no independent verification.
description: State-television frontline video and claims from Russian-controlled sectors.

title: Yurii Podolyaka
reliability_notes: ~2.68M subs, one of the biggest war channels: Ukrainian-born (Sumy) pro-Russian commentator producing daily mapped video reviews. Systematically over-claims Russian progress and predicts Ukrainian collapse; maps are illustrative, not evidence-based.
description: Daily mapped video/text analyses of every front from a pro-Russian standpoint.

title: Z komitet + karta SVO
reliability_notes: ~68K subs; publishes Russian-side campaign maps. Maps are drawn to maximise Russian control, showing claimed rather than verified gains; useful only as a Russian-claim layer.
description: Russian-perspective frontline maps and axis summaries.

title: Zakhar Prilepin
reliability_notes: ~227K subs; writer, ex-Donbas fighter and ultranationalist politician. Ideological rather than operational; effectively no verifiable geographic content.
description: Nationalist political and war commentary with occasional frontline anecdotes.

title: ZAPISKI VETERANA (Zapiski Veterana)
reliability_notes: ~296K subs; ISW-cited veteran milblogger writing 'from the trenches'. Sometimes candid about Russian shortcomings, which is its analytic value; otherwise pro-war advocacy with fundraising, no coordinates, and unverifiable first-person claims.
description: Subjective frontline notes, complaints about Russian logistics/command and unit fundraising.

title: Andrii Tsaplienko
reliability_notes: ~323K subs; veteran TV war correspondent (1+1). Reliable on the fact that an event happened but aggregates heavily from other channels; patriotic framing, minimal geolocation discipline, occasional unverified early claims.
description: Frontline video reports, strike aftermath footage and Ukrainian military news commentary.

title: Anton Gerashchenko (Pravda Gerashchenko)
reliability_notes: ~325K subs; ex-adviser to Ukraine's Interior Minister and a prolific information-war amplifier. Reliable for what Ukrainian officialdom is messaging, but has repeatedly amplified unverified or false viral clips; not a geolocation source.
description: Curated war video, official Ukrainian messaging and English-language commentary.

title: DeepState (DeepStateUA)
reliability_notes: The single most-cited Ukrainian frontline mapping team (~765K subs, posting continuously as of 19 Aug 2026); pairs its Telegram commentary with the deepstatemap.live polygon map. Pro-Ukrainian but unusually willing to publish bad news and to mark Russian gains before the General Staff admits them; occasionally criticised for grey-zone shading that is more pessimistic than DeepStateMap competitors, and it does not always publish the geolocated source video behind a change.
description: Daily narrative updates on each axis (Pokrovsk, Kupiansk, Huliaipole etc.) tied to concrete settlements plus map-change announcements and drone/strike footage.

title: Dmytro Putiata (kriegsforscherD)
reliability_notes: Serving Ukrainian drone-warfare officer (SOF, 36th Marine Bde, 20th Unmanned Systems Bde background); credible practitioner detail on unmanned systems. Insider perspective means selective disclosure and OPSEC-driven vagueness on exact positions; do not confuse with @OSINTua.
description: Practitioner analysis of drone warfare, kill-zone dynamics and unmanned-systems force structure.

title: Dnipro Operatyvnyi
reliability_notes: City/oblast-level Dnipropetrovsk channel; fastest source on strike impacts in Dnipro and Kamianske but crowd-sourced and unverified, with frequent early errors on what was hit.
description: Local strike, air-alert and impact reporting for Dnipropetrovsk oblast.

title: INSIDER UA
reliability_notes: ~2.18M subs. Very high-volume Ukrainian news aggregator; useful as a tripwire for breaking strikes but low analytical value, no geolocation, and frequent unsourced 'insider' claims.
description: Breaking-news feed on strikes, alerts and war politics for a mass Ukrainian audience.

title: Kriegsforscher (OSINTua)
reliability_notes: Long-running pseudonymous Ukrainian volunteer/analyst account known as Kriegsforscher; blunt trench-level insight into drone and infantry realities. Partisan, profane, sometimes deliberately vague about locations for OPSEC reasons; posting is episodic.
description: Commentary on Ukrainian drone/infantry tactics, equipment problems and frontline conditions.

title: Lachen pyshe (Oleksandr Lachen)
reliability_notes: Popular Ukrainian volunteer/fundraiser channel with frontline sourcing through supplied units. Opinionated, sometimes engages in intra-Ukrainian political fights; claims about specific positions should be corroborated.
description: Frontline situation commentary, fundraising for units, criticism of Ukrainian procurement.

title: Necro Mancer
reliability_notes: Anonymous Donetsk-based researcher active since 2014; maintains a named database of Russian and collaborator casualties from social media. Deliberately aggressive/propagandistic in tone (posts graphic material) but the underlying identification work is heavily used by media and researchers.
description: Documentation of Russian personnel losses by name/unit, plus local reports from occupied Donetsk.

title: Operatyvnyi ZSU (Operational AFU)
reliability_notes: ~370K subs, near-continuous posting. Fast unofficial aggregator of General Staff statements, alerts and frontline clips; it is not an original-source or geolocating channel and it recycles claims from other Telegram channels, so cross-check before treating any location as confirmed.
description: Rapid aggregation of Ukrainian military statements, air-raid/strike alerts and frontline video.

title: Osint Ukraine (@ukraine_osint)
reliability_notes: Long-running pro-Ukrainian OSINT aggregator on X. Reposts frontline and strike footage quickly with settlement-level captions but does little original geolocation, so locations should be treated as claimed until matched to terrain by a verifier such as @Danspiun or @moklasen.
description: Aggregated frontline video, strike documentation and Ukrainian-side situation updates in English.

title: Roman Sheremeta
reliability_notes: Ukrainian-American economics professor and advocate; useful for Ukrainian macro/mobilisation framing and official messaging, but he is an advocate rather than an OSINT verifier and repeats claims without independent checking.
description: Commentary on Ukraine's war economy, aid and political developments plus amplification of Ukrainian reporting.

title: Serhii Beskrestnov 'Flash'
reliability_notes: ~166K subs; Ukraine's best-known radio/EW specialist (also known as 'Sergiy Flash'). Highly technical and credible on Shahed corridors, jamming, drone control links and Russian EW hardware; not a frontline mapper, and his Shahed route/altitude observations are indicative rather than precise geolocation.
description: Technical analysis of Russian drone/EW systems, Shahed flight-corridor and radio-frequency observations, advice to Ukrainian drone units.

title: Serhii Bratchuk
reliability_notes: ~173K subs; former Odesa oblast administration spokesman, now UWC-affiliated commentator. Useful for southern/Odesa strike reporting; strongly propagandistic tone, no coordinates, and past record of premature or morale-driven claims.
description: Southern-Ukraine strike and air-defence reporting plus general war commentary.

title: Serhii Sternenko
reliability_notes: ~890K subs; activist/fundraiser (Sternenko Community Foundation) rather than analyst. Publishes very large volumes of FPV strike video from units he funds, usually with the unit and rough area named; the videos are genuine but framing is promotional and geolocation is loose, so treat locations as claimed until independently placed.
description: FPV/drone strike footage from funded units, fundraising campaigns, commentary on drone and EW procurement.

title: Special Kherson Cat
reliability_notes: Kherson-based high-volume video aggregator (also on Bluesky). Excellent early source for southern/Kherson footage; captions are partisan and locations are usually as-claimed by the posting unit rather than independently verified.
description: Frontline and strike video, especially from Kherson and the southern axis.

title: Tatarigami_UA / Frontelligence Insight
reliability_notes: Ukrainian reserve officer leading the Frontelligence Insight team (Telegram mirror t.me/s/tatarigami_UA, reports at frontelligence.substack.com). Analytically careful, publishes methodology and admits Ukrainian problems; pro-Ukrainian in framing and slower/periodic rather than a live map.
description: Medium-form analytical reports on Russian force generation, sector assessments and satellite/geospatial studies.

title: TRUKHA Ukraine
reliability_notes: One of Ukraine's largest news channels. High speed, low verification: has repeatedly published mislabelled or recycled strike video, and is a known vector for panic content. Use only as an early-warning tripwire.
description: Mass-audience breaking news on strikes, alerts and war developments.

title: Ukraine Battle Map
reliability_notes: Posts settlement-by-settlement control updates and map graphics. Convenient summary format but sourcing is often not shown and changes sometimes trail geolocated evidence; treat as a secondary aggregation of DeepState/other maps.
description: Daily control-change posts naming captured/contested settlements with map images.

title: Ukraine NOW
reliability_notes: ~417K subs; originated as a semi-official information channel in 2022. Mostly reposts official and media content; no independent geolocation, patriotic framing.
description: General war news, strike reports and official announcements.

title: Yurii Butusov (Butusov Plus)
reliability_notes: Censor.NET editor-in-chief, ~348K subs, extremely well sourced inside the Ukrainian General Staff and brigades; frequently first to report unit collapses, command failures and casualty problems that officials deny. Strongly opinionated and polemical against Ukrainian command, sometimes publishes operational detail early; names settlements but rarely coordinates.
description: Investigative frontline reporting, brigade-level accounts of specific battles, criticism of Ukrainian force generation and command decisions.

title: Zvizdets Manhustu (Zvиздец Мангусту)
reliability_notes: ~69K subs; run by serving Ukrainian drone/artillery personnel. Strong primary-source strike footage from specific sectors, but sardonic, partisan and inconsistent about naming exact locations; treat unit claims as one-sided.
description: First-person drone and artillery strike video, trench-level commentary on specific sectors.

title: Andrew Perpetua
reliability_notes: Runs the longest-standing crowd-verified equipment-loss and geolocation lists; rigorous about coordinates and refuses claims lacking imagery. Pro-Ukrainian and often abrasive; his loss counts undercount Russian losses in areas with little footage rather than overstating them.
description: Daily geolocated lists of confirmed vehicle/equipment losses and strike locations for both sides.

title: Black Bird Group
reliability_notes: Finnish OSINT team behind blackbirdgroup.fi and its interactive frontline map; publishes multiple updates a day with documented mapping conventions. One of the few teams that explains why a line moved, making it a good cross-check against DeepState.
description: Team account for frontline map changes, sector assessments and geospatial analysis.

title: Chuck Pfarrer
reliability_notes: Former US Navy SEAL who posts hand-drawn 'Indications & Warnings' situation maps. Popular and readable, but treat with caution: his maps and casualty figures are loosely sourced, optimistic about Ukrainian performance, and have repeatedly lagged or contradicted geolocated evidence.
description: Daily sector situation maps with narrative assessments of Russian attacks and Ukrainian defence.

title: Dan (Danspiun)
reliability_notes: Careful geolocator of strike and combat footage, frequently cited by larger accounts and journalists; pro-Ukrainian alignment but places footage on the basis of terrain matching rather than claims.
description: Coordinate-level geolocation of Ukraine-war video and identification of struck targets.

title: Def Mon
reliability_notes: Widely trusted Scandinavian mapper of the Pokrovsk/Bakhmut axes; maintains a detailed Scribble Maps frontline map and is explicit about confidence levels. Pro-Ukrainian but conservative about accepting Russian gains only on geolocated evidence. Note: his Telegram mirror @defmon3war has been dormant since 2023, so use X.
description: Frontline map updates, sector analysis threads and assessment of claimed advances.

title: Emil Kastehelmi (Black Bird Group)
reliability_notes: Finnish analyst and Black Bird Group co-founder; one of the most methodologically explicit frontline mappers, publishing visualisation rules and confidence caveats. Western/pro-Ukrainian outlook but frequently corrects both Ukrainian and Russian exaggerations.
description: Frontline situation updates with the Black Bird Group interactive map and threaded sector analysis.

title: John Helin (Black Bird Group)
reliability_notes: Black Bird Group co-founder; same methodology and caveats as the group's map. Reliable, non-sensational, Western perspective.
description: Frontline analysis threads and Black Bird Group map updates.

title: Jomini of the West
reliability_notes: Retired US Army officer (Ivan Torres), senior Russian-forces analyst at Rochan Consulting. Doctrinally literate operational analysis with clearly labelled assessments; Western/pro-Ukrainian perspective, aggregates OSINT rather than doing his own geolocation.
description: Operational-level assessments of Russian and Ukrainian campaigns, force-ratio and sustainment analysis.

title: Konrad Muzyka (Rochan Consulting)
reliability_notes: Independent defence analyst covering Russia and Belarus; Rochan Consulting (rochan-consulting.com) sells subscription Ukraine Conflict Monitor reports with maps. Track record is strong and sober, incorporates both sides' claims; the detailed sector mapping sits behind a paywall.
description: Paid periodic conflict-monitor reports with sector maps, plus free daily commentary on Russian/Belarusian forces.

title: M0nstas
reliability_notes: Maintains a detailed multi-layer Ukraine war map (unit positions, competing frontline layers, strike data, fortifications). Data-forward and sourced, but a one-person effort with uneven update latency across sectors.
description: Interactive multi-layer war map combining frontline, unit and infrastructure data, plus update posts.

title: Mark Krutov (RFE/RL)
reliability_notes: RFE/RL Russian Service correspondent doing rigorous OSINT investigations (satellite imagery, Russian document leaks). High reliability with published evidence; investigative cadence rather than live frontline tracking.
description: OSINT investigations into Russian strikes, units, elites and losses, often with satellite imagery.

title: Michael Kofman
reliability_notes: Carnegie Endowment senior fellow; high-credibility strategic/operational analysis based on repeated front-line research trips with Rob Lee and Konrad Muzyka. Deliberately avoids day-to-day map claims, so useless for pinpointing events but excellent for interpreting them.
description: Strategic and operational assessments of the war, Russian military reconstitution and force-quality trends.

title: Michael MacKay
reliability_notes: Canadian chronicler who systematically transcribes Ukrainian General Staff operational reports into English, direction by direction (also on Bluesky). Valuable as a structured English mirror of official Ukrainian claims; strongly pro-Ukrainian and it inherits the General Staff's biases wholesale.
description: English renderings of AFU General Staff situation reports naming settlements per direction, plus advocacy commentary.

title: MilitaryLand.net
reliability_notes: Czech-run unit database and daily frontline reports (militaryland.net/maps). Best open source for Ukrainian and Russian unit locations and orders of battle; the map is coarser than DeepState's and the Telegram channel blocks web preview, so scrape the website instead.
description: Daily frontline situation reports by direction plus a maintained database of Ukrainian and Russian units and their sectors.

title: Moklasen
reliability_notes: Strong geolocation practitioner: establishes coordinates for strikes and identifies Russian systems from reconnaissance-drone footage. Pro-Ukrainian, but publishes the imagery and reasoning behind each placement.
description: Geolocation of strike video, identification of Russian air-defence/EW/artillery systems in occupied areas.

title: Naalsio (Naalsio26)
reliability_notes: Specialist in visually-confirmed equipment losses and Russian unit identification; contributor to Oryx and WarSpotting. Rigorous coordinate-level work with per-item evidence; counts are conservative by design (visual confirmation only).
description: Geolocated equipment-loss tallies by offensive/sector and unit attribution work.

title: NOELREPORTS
reliability_notes: Belgian-run pro-Ukrainian OSINT feed (~35K on Telegram, larger on X as @NOELreports; also noelreports.com). Mostly aggregates and translates Ukrainian sources with a positive slant; geolocation is inherited from others rather than done in-house, so verify claimed positions.
description: English-language aggregation of frontline video, strike reports and Ukrainian claims, plus a map dashboard.

title: OSINTdefender
reliability_notes: Very large fast-breaking military-news account. Low reliability relative to its reach: repeatedly amplified unverified or wrong claims early in events, no geolocation, and frequently reposts other channels without attribution. Use only as a tripwire, never as evidence.
description: Rapid breaking claims on strikes, escalation and military movements across Ukraine and other conflicts.

title: OSINTtechnical
reliability_notes: Large, well-established Western OSINT account with good weapons-identification track record. Pro-Ukrainian; posts footage quickly with light verification, and its Telegram mirror @osinttechnical has been dormant since 2022, so use X.
description: Weapons identification, strike footage and equipment-loss documentation.

title: Pasi Paroinen (Black Bird Group)
reliability_notes: Black Bird Group analyst; detailed force-grouping and terrain analysis, much of it in Finnish. Careful and evidence-led, willing to state that Ukrainian positions are deteriorating; language is a barrier for automated ingestion.
description: Sector situation reviews, Russian grouping estimates and mapping commentary.

title: Playfra0
reliability_notes: Produces fortification and terrain-focused Ukraine mapping with topographic layers. Strong on engineering/fortification geospatial detail; not a daily frontline tracker.
description: Mapping of Russian and Ukrainian fortification lines, terrain analysis and visualisation layers.

title: Rob Lee
reliability_notes: FPRI senior fellow; among the most reliable Western commentators on Russian military affairs, travels repeatedly to Ukraine and sources from Ukrainian units. Careful about uncertainty and openly reports Ukrainian setbacks; not a mapper and gives no coordinates.
description: Analysis of Russian and Ukrainian force employment, drone/artillery trends and campaign trajectory, with curated frontline video.

title: Rochan Consulting - Ukraine Conflict Monitor
reliability_notes: Konrad Muzyka's subscription monitor with mapped sector assessments; among the most professional non-think-tank products and used by defence institutions. Paywalled and weekly, and it aggregates OSINT rather than generating original geolocation.
description: Subscription reports with frontline maps and assessments of Russian and Ukrainian operations.

title: Russian milblogger corpus (2022-2023 academic dataset)
reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed data paper publishing a curated corpus of posts from 21 leading Russian milblogger channels (Rybar, WarGonzo, Sladkov+, Colonelcassad, Strelkov, Kotsnews, Grey Zone, Voennyi Osvedomitel, MIG Rossii, Kotenok, Bezsonov, ANNA News, Prilepin and others). Static 2022-2023 snapshot - use it to validate channel identities and for NLP baselines, not for current events.
description: Academic dataset and channel list for the main Russian pro-war Telegram ecosystem.

title: Ukraine Control Map
reliability_notes: Independent control-mapping project (uacontrolmap.com) publishing periodic front-change maps and area-change statistics. Reasonably rigorous and quantitative; smaller team means slower updates than DeepState.
description: Front-line control maps, monthly/weekly territorial-change quantification and sector graphics.

title: Ukraine Weapons Tracker
reliability_notes: Specialised in identifying weapons and vehicles in footage from both sides and attributing losses; strong technical accuracy. Pro-Ukrainian; the Telegram backup @UAWeapons has not posted since 2023, so X is the live feed.
description: Identification and cataloguing of destroyed/captured equipment with location context where available.

title: WarTranslated (Dmitri)
reliability_notes: Translation-focused project (also x.com/wartranslated). Translations are accurate and clearly attributed to the original channel, which makes it valuable for reading Russian milblogger claims; it does no independent verification, so the underlying claim can still be propaganda.
description: English translations of Russian and Ukrainian soldier/milblogger material, interviews and intercepts.

title: Al Jazeera — Ukraine maps and war coverage
reliability_notes: Qatari-funded international broadcaster; its interactive/Sanad verification unit sources maps to ISW and dates them clearly.
description: Publishes recurring free-to-read mapped explainers of Russian attacks and territorial gains, plus a long-running maps-and-charts live tracker. Free site-wide RSS and free access make it a practical Western-style map source for aggregation.

title: NEXTA
reliability_notes: Belarusian-founded exile media project; very fast aggregator with pro-Ukrainian framing and inconsistent verification of the footage it republishes.
description: Extremely high-volume aggregation of strike and frontline video from both sides, useful as a discovery firehose for clips to geolocate independently.

title: Agentstvo (agents.media)
reliability_notes: Russian exile news project focused on debunking Russian official narratives; concise, sources every claim.
description: Rapid fact-checking of Russian MoD territorial claims against OSINT mapping — useful as a corrective on Russian-side capture announcements. RSS at agents.media/feed/ (the agentstvo.media/.press domains do not resolve).

title: ASTRA
reliability_notes: Russian exile investigative Telegram outlet; frequently first with strike-damage geolocation inside Russia, generally reliable but Telegram-native and lightly edited.
description: Telegram-first outlet reporting drone and missile impacts inside Russia and occupied territory with addresses, coordinates and resident video. Web preview at t.me/s/astrapress is scrapeable; no website RSS.

title: Baza (Telegram)
reliability_notes: Russian incident-reporting Telegram outlet with security-services sourcing; fast and often accurate on locations but state-adjacent and prone to unverified claims.
description: Reports drone impacts, explosions and casualties inside Russia and occupied areas with addresses and eyewitness video, often minutes ahead of official confirmation.

title: Interfax Russia
reliability_notes: Russian commercial wire operating under Russian censorship law; factual agency style within permitted bounds.
description: Fast wire copy on Russian MoD statements and regional emergency reports useful for cross-referencing strike locations inside Russia. Live RSS.

title: IStories (Important Stories / Vazhnye Istorii)
reliability_notes: Russian exile investigative outlet designated 'undesirable'; document- and data-driven, high verification standards.
description: Data investigations into Russian military production, casualties and occupied-territory governance. Both language RSS feeds live (~30 items); note /rss/ returns 403 while /rss/all.xml works.

title: Kommersant
reliability_notes: Russian business daily, now operating within Russian wartime censorship; more measured than state agencies but constrained.
description: Russian domestic reporting including regional-governor statements about drone strikes on Russian territory. Live RSS.

title: Mediazona (Zona.media)
reliability_notes: Russian independent outlet, banned in Russia; best-in-class quantitative methodology, publishes source data and code.
description: Runs the continuously updated confirmed-Russian-military-deaths count (https://en.zona.media/article/.../casualties_eng) built from open obituaries and probate records — a rare newsroom dataset, with repos on GitHub. RSS returns ~50 items.

title: Meduza — Ukraine war coverage
reliability_notes: Latvia-based Russian exile outlet, designated 'undesirable' by Russia; rigorous, explicitly labels unverified Russian and Ukrainian claims.
description: Daily war digests that cross-check Russian MoD, Ukrainian General Staff and OSINT claims, plus investigations into strike attribution. Both language RSS feeds return ~30 items; Telegram @meduzalive is the fastest channel.

title: Novaya Gazeta Europe
reliability_notes: Exile continuation of Novaya Gazeta after its Russian suspension; investigative, strongly anti-war, careful attribution.
description: Investigations into Russian strike units, occupied-territory administration and casualty data, plus daily war news. RSS at /feed/rss returns ~100 items (note: /rss and /rss.xml fail).

title: Readovka
reliability_notes: Pro-Kremlin Russian Telegram-first outlet; nationalist framing and frequently unverified frontline claims — a Russian-narrative sample, not a source of truth.
description: Aggregates Russian-side frontline claims and strike reports; valuable for tracking what the Russian information space asserts about specific settlements. Website readovka.news blocks bots (403).

title: RIA Novosti
reliability_notes: Russian state-owned agency under Rossiya Segodnya — propaganda; claims require independent verification.
description: High-volume Russian-side reporting of MoD claims, 'liberated' settlement announcements and occupied-territory administration. Archive RSS is live and fast.

title: SHOT (Telegram)
reliability_notes: Russian tabloid-style incident Telegram channel with siloviki sourcing; high speed, low verification, occasional deliberate disinformation.
description: Rapid geolocated reports of strikes and air-defence activity inside Russia. Useful as an early-warning tripwire that must be corroborated before use.

title: Sirena (Telegram)
reliability_notes: Independent Russian-language Telegram news project, anti-war; aggregates and cross-checks local Russian reports.
description: Aggregates locally sourced reports of strikes and explosions in Russian regions and occupied territory, often with location detail.

title: TASS
reliability_notes: Russian state news agency — propaganda outlet; use strictly as a record of official Russian claims, never as verification.
description: Carries Russian MoD daily briefings and settlement-capture announcements, essential for logging the Russian-claim side of contested locations. Clean RSS in both languages.

title: The Insider (theins.ru / theins.press)
reliability_notes: Russian exile investigative outlet, Bellingcat partner; strong on identification of Russian officers and missile-strike attribution.
description: Investigations that name the Russian units and individuals behind specific geolocated strikes, alongside daily war news. Use /feed (returns ~50 items); /rss returns HTML.

title: Verstka (Vyorstka)
reliability_notes: Russian exile outlet with unusually good access to Russian military families and regional sources; anti-war stance.
description: Reporting on Russian units, mobilisation and losses that occasionally pins formations to specific frontline sectors. RSS at /feed (~10 items).

title: 0629.com.ua (Mariupol)
reliability_notes: City-portal network outlet for occupied Mariupol, run in exile; mixes resident reports and occupation-media monitoring, so individual items need corroboration.
description: One of very few continuing sources on events inside occupied Mariupol at street level. Live RSS; part of a wider 0XXX city-portal network with equivalents for other frontline cities.

title: ArmyInform
reliability_notes: Information agency of Ukraine's Ministry of Defence — official military voice, not independent.
description: Publishes General Staff operational updates, sector-by-sector combat-clash tallies and named-axis reporting (Pokrovsk, Lyman, Kupiansk axes). Working WordPress RSS makes the daily official frontline breakdown machine-readable.

title: Babel (babel.ua)
reliability_notes: Independent Ukrainian outlet with a plain-language, explicitly fact-checked house style and clear separation of claim from confirmation.
description: Daily war news and explainers, including day-by-day frontline summaries. Its RSS at /rss.xml is unusually deep (170+ items per pull), useful for backfilling.

title: Censor.NET — war news
reliability_notes: Run by Yurii Butusov; aggressively critical of Ukrainian command and fast to publish frontline video, but sometimes ahead of confirmation.
description: High-volume war news with frontline video and named-settlement claims, often earlier than official statements. Both the site and its RSS return 403 to non-browser clients, so use Telegram @censor_net or Butusov's own @ButusovPlus.

title: Ekonomichna Pravda (Ukrainska Pravda group)
reliability_notes: Business arm of Ukrainska Pravda; reliable on infrastructure and energy-strike damage with named facilities.
description: Valuable for locating strikes on energy and industrial infrastructure, which are often reported by facility name rather than settlement. Live RSS.

title: Espreso.TV
reliability_notes: Ukrainian TV news channel; patriotic framing, hosts frequent military-expert commentary of varying rigour.
description: Continuous war news feed and frontline video segments, plus daily military-expert map explainers on YouTube. RSS live with ~40 items.

title: Gwara Media (Kharkiv)
reliability_notes: Kharkiv-based independent outlet that also runs the Perevirka fact-checking bot; verification-oriented.
description: Local frontline oblast coverage of shelling and strikes in Kharkiv region, typically naming villages and districts. Live RSS plus a fact-checking arm that debunks fake geolocated claims.

title: Hromadske
reliability_notes: Public-interest independent Ukrainian broadcaster/outlet with a documentary and human-rights bent; careful attribution.
description: Frontline and occupied-territory reporting, deportation and war-crimes documentation with settlement-level detail. No working RSS found (all common paths 404) — scrape HTML or use Telegram @hromadske.

title: Hromadske Radio
reliability_notes: Independent Ukrainian public-interest radio; interview-led, careful sourcing.
description: Frontline-community and displaced-persons reporting, plus interviews with local officials that surface settlement-level detail. Live RSS (~20 items).

title: Interfax-Ukraine
reliability_notes: Commercial Ukrainian wire; sober, attribution-heavy agency copy, premium terminal products behind paywall.
description: Wire reporting on military and regional-administration statements, useful as a second attribution for strike and frontline claims. No RSS endpoint found; free web feed is scrapeable, full agency product is paid.

title: Kyiv Post
reliability_notes: Ukraine's oldest English-language paper; relaunched under new ownership in 2022 with a more opinionated line than pre-war.
description: English-language war reporting and frontline analysis columns. Its edge server returns HTTP 400 to all non-browser clients including /feed and /rss, so no reliable machine-readable ingest was found.

title: LIGA.net
reliability_notes: Established Ukrainian business-and-politics outlet; mainstream, reasonably rigorous, pro-Ukrainian.
