description: Politics/security news desk covering strikes and frontline developments with oblast and settlement naming. Per-vertical RSS feeds (news, biz, tech, finance) are all live.

title: Militarnyi (mil.in.ua)
reliability_notes: Specialist Ukrainian defence-industry and military outlet; technically literate, sources OSINT footage and identifies weapon systems, pro-Ukrainian framing.
description: Weapons-identification and frontline-technology reporting that pins strikes and equipment losses to named locations. WordPress RSS feeds exist for both languages though item counts are thin; Telegram @militarniy is the fuller stream.

title: Nakypilo (Kharkiv)
reliability_notes: Kharkiv independent media hub; local reporting on strikes with municipal-authority attribution.
description: Street- and district-level reporting of strikes on Kharkiv city and border-area settlements. Live RSS; note the domain moved from nakipelo.ua to nakypilo.ua.

title: NikVesti (Mykolaiv)
reliability_notes: Mykolaiv-region independent outlet; solid local sourcing on strikes and southern-axis events.
description: Local coverage of strikes on Mykolaiv and Kinburn/Ochakiv-area events with settlement naming. RSS at /rss.xml.

title: Novosti Donbassa
reliability_notes: Displaced Donetsk-region independent outlet; focuses on occupied territory, relies on resident sources and occupation-administration monitoring.
description: Reports on strikes, mobilisation and administration in occupied Donbas settlements, complementing Ukrainian-side frontline reporting. RSS at /feed/ (also reachable via /rss).

title: Novynarnia
reliability_notes: Small Ukrainian military-affairs outlet staffed by veteran defence correspondents; well-sourced inside the armed forces.
description: Unit-level and axis-level frontline reporting, brigade identifications and equipment losses tied to named settlements. Live WordPress RSS.

title: NV (Novoye Vremya / New Voice of Ukraine)
reliability_notes: Mainstream Ukrainian news magazine; reliable mainstream reporting, some analysis behind subscription.
description: Rolling war coverage plus commentary; the English edition (english.nv.ua) is widely syndicated. Site-wide RSS is live and returns ~40 items; English subdomain blocks bots.

title: OstroV (ostro.org) — Donbas
reliability_notes: Long-running Donbas-focused Ukrainian outlet covering both government-held and occupied areas; sources include occupied-territory residents.
description: One of the few outlets systematically covering occupied Donetsk/Luhansk settlements, useful for events behind the line. Multiple language-specific RSS feeds.

title: RBC-Ukraine
reliability_notes: Large commercial Ukrainian news agency; fast aggregation of official and Telegram sources, moderate verification.
description: Very high-volume news feed covering strikes, air alerts and frontline claims by oblast. Its all-news RSS returns hundreds of items per pull, making it good bulk-ingest material.

title: Realna Viina (Real War)
reliability_notes: Popular Ukrainian war-news Telegram channel; aggregates official and OSINT claims with pro-Ukrainian framing and light verification.
description: Rapid frontline and strike reporting keyed to named settlements and axes; useful as a cross-check on other Ukrainian Telegram aggregators.

title: Slidstvo.Info
reliability_notes: Ukrainian investigative journalism agency; documents-and-geolocation methodology, partners with international investigative consortia.
description: Investigative war-crimes and strike-attribution work, frequently geolocating specific attack sites and identifying Russian units. Live RSS.

title: Suspilne — War section and regional frontline newsrooms
reliability_notes: Ukraine's public broadcaster; editorially cautious, attributes to local authorities and its own regional correspondents, generally the best local-authority-level source.
description: National public broadcaster with 24 regional newsrooms that post shelling/strike reports at settlement and even street level, including frontline oblasts. Website and RSS are hard-blocked to non-browser clients (HTTP 403), so scrape the Telegram channels instead.

title: Texty.org.ua
reliability_notes: Ukraine's leading data-journalism nonprofit; methodology-transparent, publishes datasets and code alongside stories.
description: Data-journalism desk producing mapped investigations — damage to infrastructure, occupied-territory analysis, disinformation mapping — often with downloadable data. RSS at /feed.xml (not /rss/); Telegram @textyorgua.

title: The Kyiv Independent — War coverage
reliability_notes: English-language Ukrainian outlet founded by ex-Kyiv Post staff; strong sourcing discipline, names settlements and cites General Staff/DeepState/ISW for territorial claims.
description: Rolling war desk with named-settlement reporting, on-the-ground frontline dispatches and daily General Staff summaries. Working RSS at /news-archive/rss/ plus Telegram mirror @kyivindependent_official; some longform is member-only.

title: TRUKHA Ukraine
reliability_notes: Very large Ukrainian Telegram news aggregator; extremely fast but minimal verification and has repeatedly carried false claims — corroborate everything.
description: Firehose of air-alert, strike and frontline reports usually naming the oblast or city within minutes, useful as a discovery layer only.

title: Ukrainska Pravda — War section
reliability_notes: Ukraine's leading independent daily; fast but frequently republishes official/military claims, attributed rather than independently verified.
description: High-volume feed of strikes, casualties and frontline movement, usually naming the settlement and oblast. Multiple working RSS endpoints (news, publications, EN) plus Telegram @ukrpravda_news; HTML pages are Cloudflare-protected against bots.

title: Ukrinform — ATO/war rubric
language: Ukrainian; English; Russian; German; Spanish; French; Chinese; Japanese
reliability_notes: Ukraine's state news agency — official perspective; reliable for what officials said, not an independent check on it.
description: Dedicated ATO/war rubric carrying General Staff and regional-administration statements naming oblasts and settlements. Clean per-rubric RSS in several languages makes it one of the easiest official-claim feeds to ingest.

title: UNIAN
reliability_notes: Major commercial Ukrainian agency; very fast, aggregates heavily from Telegram and officials with light verification.
description: Bulk war news volume including air-alert, strike and frontline-claim items by oblast. Separate live RSS endpoints per language on rss.unian.net.

title: United24 Media
reliability_notes: Media arm connected to Ukraine's United24 state fundraising platform — treat as Ukrainian government-aligned messaging.
description: English-language war news and frontline explainers aimed at international audiences. No RSS found (/feed 404s).

title: Vgoru (Kherson)
reliability_notes: Kherson-region independent outlet reporting from both banks of the Dnipro; local-authority sourcing.
description: Daily shelling and drone-strike reporting for Kherson city districts and left-bank occupied settlements. RSS at /rss-google.xml (plain /feed 404s).

title: Zaborona
reliability_notes: Formerly a respected independent Ukrainian investigative outlet; as of August 2026 the site displays 'Seven Years of Journalism was Deleted' and its archive is gone.
description: DEAD/ARCHIVED: the live archive has been removed and the RSS feed returns HTML, so only Web Archive copies of its occupied-territory and war-crimes investigations remain usable.

title: Agence France-Presse (AFP) and AFP Fact Check
reliability_notes: Global wire; AFP Fact Check maintains a dedicated debunking operation for miscaptioned and mislocated war footage.
description: AFP frontline reporting is distributed to subscribers rather than published openly, so its value here is via clients and via AFP Fact Check debunks of geolocated fakes (factcheck.afp.com blocks bots with 403).

title: Associated Press — Russia-Ukraine war hub
reliability_notes: Non-profit wire with rigorous standards and its own frontline photographers/videographers; explicit about unverifiable battlefield claims.
description: Continuous wire coverage plus datelined dispatches from frontline cities, valuable for independent confirmation of events at named settlements. The hub page resolves but all AP RSS endpoints tested (apnews.com/index.rss, feeds.apnews.com) now fail.

title: BBC Russian
reliability_notes: BBC World Service Russian service, blocked inside Russia; independent verification of both sides' claims.
description: Russian-language war reporting with regular OSINT-based frontline pieces and geolocation of contested settlements. Live RSS plus Telegram.

title: BBC Ukrainian
reliability_notes: BBC World Service language service; same editorial standards, closer local sourcing than the English service.
description: Ukrainian-language war coverage including frontline explainers and map-based analyses of Russian advances. Live RSS (~17 items) plus Telegram mirror.

title: BBC — War in Ukraine and BBC Verify
reliability_notes: Publicly funded UK broadcaster with a formal editorial-standards regime; BBC Verify shows its geolocation and satellite-imagery working.
description: BBC Verify (bbc.co.uk/news/bbcverify) publishes step-by-step OSINT verification of strike sites, satellite comparisons and frontline claims. Europe RSS is live; there is no dedicated Ukraine-topic RSS.

title: CNN — Ukraine
reliability_notes: US broadcaster with correspondents in Ukraine; generally careful, labels unverified footage.
description: Rolling coverage and live updates from frontline cities. Section page resolves; the legacy rss.cnn.com feeds no longer resolve.

title: Current Time TV (Nastoyashcheye Vremya)
reliability_notes: RFE/RL and VOA Russian-language TV network; independent of the Kremlin, US-funded, verification-oriented.
description: Russian-language war video journalism including verified strike footage and frontline reports. RSS endpoint live.

title: Deutsche Welle — war in Ukraine (EN and UK)
reliability_notes: German public international broadcaster; institutionally cautious with battlefield claims, distinguishes claim from confirmation.
description: Dedicated Ukrainian-language 'Russia's war against Ukraine' topic page plus English coverage and analysis of frontline shifts. Language-wide RSS feeds are live; per-topic feeds are not exposed.

title: Financial Times — war in Ukraine and FT visual/data journalism
reliability_notes: FT's visual-and-data team publishes methodology notes and sources its frontline geometry to ISW/DeepState; high analytic quality.
description: Recurring Ukraine frontline and territorial-change maps and charts quantifying monthly Russian gains. Hard paywall and Cloudflare 403 to bots; the older ig.ft.com/ukraine-tracker/ standalone tracker is now dead (404).

title: France 24 — Ukraine
reliability_notes: French public international broadcaster; its Observers/Truth-or-Fake unit debunks mislocated war footage.
description: Europe desk coverage of the war plus Truth-or-Fake segments verifying and geolocating viral footage. Europe RSS is live; the /en/tag/ukraine/ page 403s to bots.

title: Krym.Realii (RFE/RL Crimea service)
reliability_notes: RFE/RL project focused on occupied Crimea; relies on resident networks and OSINT, generally reliable with claims attributed.
description: The most systematic open source on events in occupied Crimea — explosions at airbases, air-defence activity, Russian military movements, usually located to a named town or facility. RSS endpoint resolves but returned no items in testing; Telegram is the reliable channel.

title: Le Monde — Ukraine (English edition)
reliability_notes: French paper of record with its own war correspondents and a video-verification desk; careful attribution.
description: Frontline reporting and mapped analyses of Russian advances. Returns HTTP 402 Payment Required to unauthenticated clients — hard paywall, no usable feed.

title: POLITICO Europe — Defense
reliability_notes: Brussels-focused policy outlet; well-sourced on Western policy and intelligence assessments, not a battlefield-mapping source.
description: Useful for Western intelligence assessments of frontline trends and weapons deliveries rather than event geolocation. The /tag/ukraine/ path 404s; use /section/defense/.

title: Radio Svoboda (RFE/RL Ukrainian Service) and Skhemy
reliability_notes: RFE/RL's Ukrainian service; Skhemy is a leading investigative unit using satellite imagery and geolocation, with methodology published.
description: Ukrainian-language frontline and occupied-territory reporting plus Skhemy (radiosvoboda.org/skhemy) investigations that geolocate Russian bases and strike origins. RSS endpoint live with ~20 items.

title: Reuters — Ukraine coverage and graphics desk
reliability_notes: Global wire with the strictest verification standards in the category; frontline maps are explicitly sourced to ISW/DeepState with dating.
description: Wire reporting plus a graphics desk that publishes recurring Ukraine frontline and strike maps built on ISW/Institute data. reuters.com/world/ukraine/ returns 401 and the UKRAINE-CRISIS graphics paths return 403 to bots; the graphics landing page resolves. Metered paywall.

title: RFE/RL — Ukraine
reliability_notes: US Congress-funded broadcaster with a firewalled newsroom and a large in-country correspondent network; strong verification, explicit funding disclosure.
description: Ukraine desk with frontline dispatches and its own OSINT/verification work. The /api/zrqiteuuir RSS endpoint resolves for rferl.org but returned zero items in testing — verify per-section feed IDs before relying on it.

title: The Economist — Ukraine war fires tracker and war-fire model
reliability_notes: Unusually transparent newsroom modelling — code and data published openly, with stated uncertainty; the underlying satellite fire data is NASA FIRMS.
description: Continuously updated tracker inferring frontline activity from NASA satellite fire detections, plus monthly territorial-change estimates. The model code and derived data are on GitHub — one of the very few newsroom-published machine-readable conflict datasets. Article paywalled; repo free.

title: The Guardian — Ukraine
reliability_notes: Free-to-read UK paper with its own Kyiv correspondents; runs a near-daily Ukraine live blog with sourcing labelled.
description: Rolling live-blog coverage that timestamps and attributes strike and frontline claims to Ukrainian and Russian officials. Section RSS is live and free — one of the easiest Western feeds to ingest.

title: The New York Times — Ukraine war news event and Visual Investigations
reliability_notes: Leading US paper; its Visual Investigations unit is a gold standard for forensic geolocation of individual strikes, with published methodology.
description: The news-event hub carries the rolling Ukraine maps (updated territorial-control graphics), while nytimes.com/spotlight/visual-investigations holds frame-by-frame forensic reconstructions of specific attacks with coordinates. Hard paywall; article pages 403 to bots.

title: The Times (UK) — Russia-Ukraine war
reliability_notes: UK paper with embedded frontline correspondents; reporting is strong but analysis is opinionated and paywalled.
description: Datelined frontline dispatches naming specific settlements and units. Section page resolves; content behind a hard paywall.

title: The Washington Post — Ukraine war and visual forensics
reliability_notes: Major US paper with a strong visual-forensics team; verification-heavy, publishes satellite and video analysis of strike sites.
description: Publishes forensic reconstructions of individual strikes and periodic frontline/counteroffensive maps. Fully bot-blocked in this environment (connection refused / 403 via WebFetch) and behind a hard paywall — browser access required.

title: Airwars - Russian military in Ukraine
reliability_notes: Conservative, source-counted casualty methodology with published confidence gradings; focuses on civilian harm from strikes, not on ground control, and coverage of Ukraine is narrower than its Middle East work.
description: Incident-by-incident archive of alleged civilian-harm strikes with locations, dates and archived sources - a disciplined dataset for where strikes landed.

title: Amnesty International Citizen Evidence Lab
reliability_notes: Amnesty's verification methodology hub; its 2022 Ukraine reporting drew public criticism over framing, so read conclusions with that controversy in mind.
description: Publishes Amnesty's digital-verification methodology and worked examples plus the Digital Verification Corps' output - both a training resource and a source of verified Ukraine incident analysis.

title: Bellingcat - Ukraine investigations
reliability_notes: Publishes full methodology and archived source material, the field's de-facto standard; investigation-led rather than continuous, so coverage is deep but sparse.
description: Forensic geolocation and chronolocation of specific strikes and atrocities in Ukraine, including named-perpetrator work. The methodology write-ups double as teaching material for locating footage yourself.

title: Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations (UN OHCHR)
reliability_notes: A normative standard, not an evidence source; adherence by volunteer geolocators in the Ukraine community is uneven.
description: The reference methodology for conducting and documenting digital open-source investigations, defining how a frontline video should be collected, verified, geolocated and preserved to evidentiary standard.

title: Forensic Architecture - Ukraine investigations
reliability_notes: Goldsmiths-based research agency with court-grade spatial methodology; each investigation takes months, so it is retrospective rather than current.
description: Builds 3D spatial and temporal reconstructions of specific incidents in Ukraine from videos, photos and satellite imagery - the gold standard for pinning an event to an exact location and time.

title: Human Rights Watch - Digital Investigations Lab
reliability_notes: Combines field interviews with satellite and open-source analysis and documents its harm-mitigation policy; publishes on an investigation timetable, not continuously.
description: Geospatially verified investigations of strikes, cluster-munition use and destruction in Ukraine, with coordinates and satellite before/after comparisons in the reports.

title: SITU Research
reliability_notes: Design-practice research arm working with ICC and prosecutors; publishes selectively because much work is under legal confidentiality.
description: Spatial and visual evidence reconstruction of attacks including in Ukraine, producing georeferenced incident models used in accountability proceedings.

title: Conflict Intelligence Team (CIT)
reliability_notes: Exiled Russian OSINT team, designated 'undesirable' by Russia; publishes verification chains and geolocation reasoning but is a small team with limited coverage breadth.
description: Russian-language OSINT collective that geolocates strike and combat footage, tracks Russian unit deployments and debunks both sides' claims - unusually valuable for reading Russian-source material critically.

title: Detector Media
reliability_notes: Ukrainian media-monitoring NGO; strong on Russian Telegram narrative tracking, explicitly Ukrainian-aligned, and does little geolocation itself.
description: Monitors and debunks Russian information operations including fabricated frontline claims and Telegram narrative campaigns, helping assess source reliability.

title: InformNapalm
reliability_notes: Volunteer Ukrainian OSINT network active since 2014, explicitly aligned with Ukraine; hacked-material sourcing and identification work should be treated with care.
description: Long-running volunteer identification of Russian units and equipment deployed in Ukraine, often tying specific formations to specific frontline sectors.

title: Molfar (Ukrainian OSINT agency)
reliability_notes: Commercial Ukrainian OSINT firm that has openly passed target geolocations to Ukrainian forces, so it is a participant rather than a neutral observer; published cases are a curated subset of its work.
description: Publishes worked geolocation and chronolocation case studies (identifying Russian positions from soldiers' social media) plus the Molfar Intelligence Institute's investigations - strong practical methodology for locating frontline units.

title: StopFake
reliability_notes: Ukrainian fact-checking project founded 2014; has faced criticism over some editorial choices and is explicitly counter-Russian-disinformation in mission.
description: Debunks Russian disinformation including false claims about captured settlements and frontline breakthroughs - a filter for weeding out fabricated positional claims.

title: Truth Hounds
reliability_notes: Ukrainian documentation NGO doing field investigation plus OSINT for legal accountability; Ukrainian-aligned and incident-focused.
description: Documents and geolocates attacks and occupation-related crimes in frontline and de-occupied areas, with detailed location and date reconstruction in its reports.

title: VoxCheck (VoxUkraine)
reliability_notes: IFCN-adjacent Ukrainian fact-checking with published verdict methodology; Ukrainian perspective and mostly focused on information rather than geospatial verification.
description: Fact-checks war-related claims including Russian and Ukrainian statements about frontline progress; useful for adjudicating disputed advance claims.

title: C4ADS
reliability_notes: Data-heavy investigative nonprofit; reports are methodologically strong but slow and focused on networks rather than the contact line.
description: Investigations using satellite, shipping and procurement data on Russian logistics, sanctions evasion and grain theft from occupied Ukraine - useful for locating rear-area and occupation infrastructure.

title: Centre for Information Resilience - Eyes on Russia project
reliability_notes: Each entry is individually verified and archived by CIR staff; UK/US government-funded, and the dataset is incident-driven rather than a control-line assessment.
description: The Eyes on Russia project verifies and geolocates videos and images of the war and publishes the underlying incident database with source links - a primary evidence layer for where events happened.

title: DFRLab Digital Sherlocks / 360 Open Summit training programme
reliability_notes: A training pipeline rather than an evidence source; quality of alumni output varies and curricula are not fully public.
description: Trains and networks the volunteer verification community that produces much of the geolocated Ukraine footage, and publishes the methodology it teaches.

title: OSINT for Ukraine
reliability_notes: A student and early-career volunteer collective; enthusiastic and transparent but with limited institutional review and irregular output.
description: Volunteer collective documenting and geolocating alleged war crimes and strike incidents in Ukraine, publishing verification reports with source archives.

title: UC Berkeley Human Rights Center Investigations Lab
reliability_notes: Student-staffed under academic supervision; co-authored the Berkeley Protocol, so methodology is exemplary but throughput is limited and semester-bound.
description: Academic open-source investigation lab that verifies conflict footage including from Ukraine and sets the professional standards used by the wider verification community.

title: GLIDE - GLobal IDEntifier Number database
reliability_notes: A disaster-event identifier registry, not an incident feed; conflict events in Ukraine are sparsely registered compared with natural hazards.
description: ADRC/UN-maintained registry assigning canonical GLIDE identifiers to disaster events including Ukraine complex-emergency and flood entries. Useful for joining datasets that reference events by GLIDE code.

title: IAEA - Ukraine nuclear safety updates
reliability_notes: Live but bot-blocked (HTTP 403 from datacenter IPs); the IAEA reports what its on-site teams observe and pointedly declines to attribute attacks, which limits it as evidence of who struck what.
description: Numbered IAEA Director General updates on Zaporizhzhia, South Ukraine, Khmelnytskyi, Rivne and Chornobyl sites, including drone impacts, shelling heard nearby and power-line losses. The only neutral on-site observer reporting at named nuclear facilities.

title: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix - Ukraine
reliability_notes: Live but bot-blocked (HTTP 403 from datacenter IPs); survey-based with multi-week lag and oblast/raion resolution, so it is a lagging indicator of frontline change rather than an event source.
description: IOM general population surveys and area baseline assessments giving IDP and returnee counts by oblast and raion with downloadable datasets. Displacement spikes corroborate where the front moved.

title: OHCHR Ukraine country page
reliability_notes: Live but bot-blocked (HTTP 403 from datacenter IPs); aggregate figures only, no incident coordinates.
description: OHCHR hub for Ukraine casualty updates, Commission of Inquiry material and press briefings. Use HRMMU's own site for the detailed reports.

title: OSCE - Ukraine
reliability_notes: OSCE lost its in-country monitoring capability in 2022, so current output is statements and Moscow Mechanism reports rather than observed incident data; consensus rules make it slow.
description: OSCE Ukraine portal with Moscow Mechanism expert reports, Chairpersonship statements and Support Programme material. Now a documentary rather than observational source.

title: OSCE Special Monitoring Mission to Ukraine (SMM) - archive
reliability_notes: Mandate ended in 2022 so the data stops there, but it remains the only large body of neutral, on-the-ground, coordinate-bearing ceasefire-violation observations for the Donbas contact line.
description: Archive of SMM daily and spot reports (2014-2022) recording explosions, ceasefire violations and crater analyses with locations and often coordinates. Essential historical baseline for the pre-2022 contact line.

title: Register of Damage for Ukraine (Council of Europe)
reliability_notes: An international claims register, not a monitoring service: individual claim data is confidential and no public geodataset is released, so value is documentary and statistical only.
description: Council of Europe international register recording claims of damage, loss and injury caused by the Russian aggression, with category-by-category claim statistics. Authoritative confirmation that damage in given categories and areas has been formally documented.

title: ReliefWeb - Ukraine
reliability_notes: Aggregator rather than primary source, so quality varies by contributing agency; the v1 API is decommissioned (HTTP 410) and v2 rejects unapproved appnames (HTTP 403), so registration is required.
description: OCHA-run repository of every humanitarian report, map and assessment on Ukraine, with a full JSON API. The most efficient single entry point to official and NGO documents including maps with settlement detail.

title: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU/OHCHR)
reliability_notes: The most methodologically careful casualty source, but it counts only verified civilian casualties and therefore always undercounts; verification lag is weeks and it does not map military positions.
description: HRMMU periodic reports and monthly civilian-casualty updates with oblast breakdowns and named-incident case studies. The reference dataset for verified civilian harm by region.

title: UN OCHA Ukraine
reliability_notes: Humanitarian rather than military framing; reports name affected settlements and frontline hromadas but deliberately avoid describing military control, and figures are consolidated from partners with lag.
description: OCHA situation reports and flash updates on humanitarian impact, naming affected oblasts, hromadas and evacuation areas. Good for corroborating that a named settlement came under sustained attack.

title: UNESCO - damaged cultural sites in Ukraine
reliability_notes: Verified but narrow in scope (cultural property only) and slow, with verification lag of months; no attribution of responsibility per site.
description: UNESCO's verified list of damaged cultural sites in Ukraine broken down by oblast and site type, updated periodically. Gives independently confirmed, named-location damage records.

title: UNHCR Operational Data Portal - Ukraine situation
reliability_notes: Cross-border and IDP aggregates only; no incident-level geography and country-of-asylum figures depend on host-state reporting.
description: UNHCR's data portal for refugee and IDP figures across the Ukraine situation with downloadable time series. Useful contextual layer for population movement away from active fronts.

title: UNITAR maps and geospatial products
reliability_notes: Same episodic-coverage caveat as UNOSAT; products are static PDFs plus occasional shapefiles rather than a live feed.
description: UNITAR's catalogue of analysis maps including Ukraine damage assessments and flood/impact products. Search here for downloadable geodata behind UNOSAT reports.

title: UNOSAT (UNITAR) - satellite damage assessments
reliability_notes: Genuinely independent and geospatially rigorous, but activation-driven and episodic, so coverage is patchy in time and concentrated on major urban areas; damage points reflect imagery date, not the strike date.
description: UN satellite-imagery damage assessments for Ukrainian cities with per-building damage points, maps and downloadable datasets. One of the few neutral sources giving true coordinates for war damage.

title: WHO Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care (SSA)
reliability_notes: Verified and conservative, covering only health-facility and health-worker attacks and only where WHO could confirm them, so it undercounts; attribution is deliberately not assigned.
description: WHO's verified database of attacks on health care with date, oblast, facility type and impact for each Ukraine incident, downloadable as structured data. One of the few neutral, per-incident, location-tagged official datasets.

title: Alexander Gusev - Governor of Voronezh Oblast, Russia
reliability_notes: Deliberately vague: usually reports only "UAVs downed over the region" without naming the district, which limits geolocation value compared with Belgorod.
description: Voronezh Oblast governor's confirmations of drone attacks and air-defence activity. Confirms that a deep strike occurred in the region even when the exact target is withheld.

title: Alexander Khinshtein - Governor of Kursk Oblast, Russia
reliability_notes: Names settlements and districts in the border zone but is silent on Russian military dispositions and selective about incursion or border-fighting details.
description: Kursk Oblast governor's reporting on drone and artillery strikes and border-district incidents by named settlement. Important for the Sumy-Kursk cross-border sector.

title: Denis Pushilin - Russian-installed head of occupied Donetsk Oblast
reliability_notes: Occupation leadership channel: strike claims against Donetsk city are location-specific but casualty and culpability claims are propaganda, and advance announcements are often premature.
description: Claims of Ukrainian shelling of Donetsk, Horlivka and Makiivka with district-level detail, plus commentary on Russian advances toward named towns. A key official source for the occupied Donbas interior.

title: Kursk Oblast Administration - Telegram
reliability_notes: Institutional occupation-adjacent regional feed; location-specific for civilian impacts, opaque about military matters.
description: Kursk regional government channel with damage, evacuation and restoration reporting by named settlement. Complements the governor's personal channel.

title: Mikhail Razvozhaev - Russian-installed governor of Sevastopol
reliability_notes: Reports attacks on Sevastopol quickly and by district but downplays Black Sea Fleet damage; treat effect claims as unreliable.
description: Sevastopol-specific official channel announcing air-defence activity and attacks by city district. Highest-frequency official source for Black Sea Fleet base area events.

title: National Anti-Terrorism Committee of Russia (NAC) - Telegram
reliability_notes: Official framing labels Ukrainian strikes as terrorist attacks and minimises damage; place names are usually specific and accurate.
description: NAC statements on drone and sabotage incidents inside Russia, generally naming the region and facility. Complements MChS for locating strikes on Russian territory.

title: Rosatom - Telegram
reliability_notes: Russian operator's account of Zaporizhzhia NPP conditions; directly contradicts Ukrainian statements and both sides blame each other for shelling near the plant.
description: Rosatom communications on the occupied Zaporizhzhia NPP including claimed drone strikes on site and power-line status. Necessary counterpart to Energoatom and IAEA reporting for ZNPP events.

title: Russian Ministry of Defence - mil.ru
reliability_notes: Live inside Russia but unreachable from many Western networks (connection refused/timeout in testing) and intermittently geoblocked, so the Telegram mirrors are the practical access route; content carries the same unverifiable-claims problem.
description: Official Russian MoD site hosting the archive of daily special-military-operation briefings. Valuable as the citable primary record when accessible, e.g. via a Russian-routed proxy or web archive.

title: Russian Ministry of Defence - Telegram
reliability_notes: The mirror image of the Ukrainian General Staff: loss figures and "liberation" claims are unverifiable and routinely inflated, and settlement-capture announcements are often premature by days or weeks, yet the named settlements themselves are the key signal of where Russia is attacking.
description: Daily Russian MoD operational briefings naming captured settlements, claimed Ukrainian losses and grouping-by-grouping activity (Sever, Zapad, Yug, Tsentr, Vostok, Dnepr). The settlement names are essential input for frontline mapping even when the capture claim is false.

title: Russian Ministry of Defence - Telegram (English)
reliability_notes: Same unverifiable-claims caveat as the Russian original; transliteration of settlement names is inconsistent, which complicates automated matching to gazetteers.
description: English translations of Russian MoD daily briefings and grouping reports. Convenient for pipelines that cannot process Russian, with a name-normalisation step required.

title: Russian Ministry of Defence - X/Twitter
reliability_notes: Propaganda outlet with the same unverifiable claims; posting is less complete than Telegram.
description: English-language Russian MoD account carrying briefing highlights and claimed captures. Secondary to the Telegram channels.

title: Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) - Telegram
reliability_notes: Reliable that an incident occurred at a named place but systematically silent or euphemistic about military causes and about damage to military and refinery targets.
description: Russian emergency-service reporting on fires and damage in border and interior regions, naming settlements. Useful for corroborating Ukrainian deep-strike claims inside Russia.

title: Sergey Aksyonov - Russian-installed head of occupied Crimea
reliability_notes: Consistently minimises damage from Ukrainian strikes and often attributes visible smoke to "debris" or drills; place naming is usually accurate even when damage claims are not.
description: First official acknowledgements of drone, missile and naval-drone attacks on named Crimean locations including Sevastopol area, Feodosia and Dzhankoi. Useful timestamp and location anchor for Crimean strike events.

title: Veniamin Kondratyev - Governor of Krasnodar Krai, Russia
reliability_notes: Confirms strikes on named towns and sometimes refineries and port facilities, while minimising the scale of damage.
description: Krasnodar Krai governor's acknowledgements of drone strikes on Novorossiysk, Tuapse, Slavyansk-on-Kuban and Afipsky refinery areas. Primary official confirmation source for Black Sea coast energy-target strikes.

title: Vladimir Saldo - Russian-appointed head of occupied Kherson Oblast
reliability_notes: Occupation-administration propaganda with strong incentive to exaggerate Ukrainian shelling of civilians and to conceal military damage; nevertheless the named left-bank settlements are the main official window into that area.
description: Daily claims of Ukrainian strikes on named left-bank Kherson settlements (Nova Kakhovka, Oleshky, Hola Prystan) with casualty assertions. Effectively the only routine official reporting on occupied Kherson.

title: Vyacheslav Gladkov - Governor of Belgorod Oblast, Russia
reliability_notes: The single most location-precise Russian official channel: he routinely names individual villages, streets and house numbers hit in Belgorod Oblast, though attribution and casualty details are one-sided.
description: Multiple daily reports of shelling, FPV and drone strikes in Belgorod Oblast down to named village and street level, plus evacuation notices. Indispensable for mapping cross-border strikes on Russian territory.

title: Yevgeny Balitsky - Russian-appointed head of occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast
reliability_notes: Occupation official whose claims about Ukrainian strikes and about Russian advances are unverifiable and politically motivated; he has repeatedly announced captures before Russian MoD did.
description: Reporting on strikes in occupied Melitopol, Enerhodar, Tokmak and Berdiansk plus claims about the southern front. Useful for detecting Ukrainian deep strikes behind the southern line.

title: Yuri Slyusar - Governor of Rostov Oblast, Russia
reliability_notes: Names districts and towns for drone damage but avoids identifying military and refinery targets; claims of "no casualties" are routinely repeated.
description: Rostov Oblast governor's reports on drone strikes affecting Taganrog, Morozovsk, Kamensk and Rostov-on-Don areas. Key for Ukrainian deep strikes on southern Russian logistics and airbases.

title: Air Force Command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine - Facebook
reliability_notes: Slower than the Telegram channel and omits most in-flight tracking posts; interception figures are unverifiable official claims.
description: Facebook home of the Air Force daily air-attack summaries and infographics. Best used as the citable, permalinked version of the nightly launch/interception tallies.

title: Air Force Command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine - Telegram
reliability_notes: The single best official near-real-time source for locating incoming air threats; it names oblasts, raions and often individual settlements and vectors of drone/missile movement, though post-strike results and interception totals are official claims only.
description: Live threat-tracking posts ("Shahed group heading toward X, course on Y") plus a morning summary of the night's air attack giving launch counts, weapon types and the oblasts hit. Combined with timestamps this is the highest-resolution official feed for geolocating air attacks.

title: Air Force Command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine - X/Twitter
reliability_notes: Partial mirror; in-flight tracking alerts are generally not reposted here, so do not rely on it for real-time geolocation.
description: Daily air-attack summary posts and infographics. Useful only as a secondary confirmation feed.

title: Armed Forces of Ukraine - zsu.gov.ua
reliability_notes: Live but returns HTTP 403 to datacenter/bot IPs (Cloudflare protection), so automated scraping needs a residential proxy or browser headers; content duplicates General Staff output.
description: Official AFU portal republishing General Staff reports and command-level announcements. Value is as an authoritative web-permalink copy of reports that otherwise only exist on Telegram/Facebook.

title: Center for Countering Disinformation (Ukraine NSDC)
reliability_notes: A Ukrainian state information-operations body: its debunks are useful but it is itself a partisan actor and should not be used as a neutral arbiter.
description: NSDC-subordinate centre publishing rebuttals of Russian claims, including claimed captures of specific settlements. Valuable precisely because it reacts to Russian MoD settlement-capture announcements.

title: Center for Countering Disinformation - Telegram
reliability_notes: Partisan Ukrainian government channel; treat its denials of Russian advances with the same scepticism as the claims they answer.
description: Fast Ukrainian official denials and contextualisation of Russian claims about captured villages and strike results. Good for building a paired claim/counter-claim dataset per settlement.

title: Chernihiv Oblast Military Administration
reliability_notes: Border-zone reporting is settlement-specific; casualty figures preliminary.
description: Chernihiv OVA channel reporting cross-border shelling and drone strikes in Novhorod-Siverskyi and Semenivka areas plus energy-infrastructure damage. Covers the northern border axis.

title: Chernivtsi Oblast Military Administration
reliability_notes: Deep-rear oblast; rarely reports impacts, mostly alerts and drone transits, so low event density.
description: Chernivtsi OVA channel, representative of western-oblast administrations that report occasional deep drone strikes and alert activity. Useful for completeness of nationwide coverage.

title: Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration
reliability_notes: Names hromadas and districts (Nikopol, Marhanets, Synelnykove) reliably; deliberately vague about hits on industrial and military-adjacent facilities.
description: Dnipropetrovsk OVA channel logging Nikopol-area shelling from the left bank and drone/missile strikes on Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad. Now also covers fighting on the oblast's eastern edge.

title: Donetsk Oblast Administration - official channel
reliability_notes: Institutional companion to the governor's channel; location detail is settlement-level and reliable, coverage is civilian-impact only.
description: Donetsk OVA institutional channel with daily damage and evacuation reports naming affected settlements and hromadas. Useful for evacuation-order geography, which tracks the advancing front.

title: Donetsk Oblast Military Administration - head Vadym Filashkin
reliability_notes: One of the best official sources for exact strike locations because he names the specific settlement and often the street or facility; he does not report frontline movement and stops covering places once they fall.
description: Daily posts from the Donetsk OVA head listing shelling and strike casualties by named settlement across Kramatorsk, Sloviansk, Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka districts. Effectively a per-settlement civilian-impact log for the hottest oblast.

title: DSNS Kyiv City - Telegram (regional DSNS pattern)
reliability_notes: Representative of a family of per-oblast DSNS channels; each is location-precise for incidents in its own region only.
description: Kyiv city DSNS channel giving district-level and address-level detail on strike fires and rescue operations. Template for harvesting equivalent per-oblast DSNS channels.

title: Energoatom - Telegram
reliability_notes: Ukrainian operator's view of nuclear-site incidents, including at Russian-held Zaporizhzhia NPP where it has no on-site access, so ZNPP claims are second-hand and contested by Russia.
description: Energoatom reporting on strikes near nuclear plants, switchyard and power-line damage, and ZNPP status. Names specific plants and substations, making it useful for high-value target events.

title: eRecovery / Damaged and destroyed property register (damaged.in.ua)
reliability_notes: Live but bot-blocked (HTTP 403 from datacenter IPs); it is a citizen-claim intake system, so individual records are private and only aggregates are published, and coverage excludes occupied areas.
description: Ukraine's official register for reporting property damaged or destroyed by the war, feeding the eRecovery compensation programme. Aggregate outputs indicate which settlements have the heaviest verified building damage.

title: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine - Facebook
reliability_notes: Same content and same unverifiable-claims caveat as the Telegram channel; Facebook posts are often the canonical version cited by media, and an English translation is usually posted alongside.
description: Canonical Facebook home of the twice-daily General Staff operational report, including per-direction clash counts and settlement name lists. Useful as a stable archive because Facebook posts are permalinked and dated.

title: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine - Telegram
reliability_notes: Primary Ukrainian military source but claims (Russian losses, "attacks repelled") are unverifiable and it names axes/directions (Pokrovsk, Lyman, Huliaipole) plus lists of settlements near which clashes occurred rather than control changes; it systematically under-reports Ukrainian withdrawals.
description: Twice-daily operational report (morning/evening) listing combat clashes per direction with the settlements adjacent to each engagement, plus daily strike/air-defence summaries. The settlement lists are the standard raw input for inferring where fighting is active.

title: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine - X/Twitter
reliability_notes: English-language mirror that abbreviates the full report, so settlement lists are sometimes dropped; same unverifiable loss-claim caveat as the parent channel.
description: English summaries of General Staff operational reports and equipment-loss tallies. Convenient for quick monitoring but less complete than the Telegram/Facebook originals.

title: Joint Forces Task Force (Uhrupovannia Obiednanykh Syl) - Telegram
reliability_notes: Operational-grouping-level channel covering the north-eastern sector; reporting is axis-level and selectively silent about setbacks, so treat as one-sided.
description: Official grouping-level channel for the north-east (Kharkiv/Sumy/Kupiansk sectors) with situation notes and combat video. Provides sector detail the central General Staff report compresses.

title: Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov - Telegram
reliability_notes: City-level official who typically names the exact city district and sometimes the street within minutes; scope limited to Kharkiv city.
description: The Kharkiv mayor's channel giving district-level (Kyivskyi, Slobidskyi, Shevchenkivskyi) and often street-level detail on strikes in Ukraine's second city. One of the fastest and most precise municipal sources.

title: Kharkiv Oblast Military Administration - head Oleh Syniehubov
reliability_notes: Names exact settlements, streets and facility types for strikes; casualty counts are preliminary and he avoids commenting on Russian tactical gains.
description: The Kharkiv OVA head's channel reporting KAB, MLRS and drone strikes by named settlement across Kharkiv, Chuhuiv, Kupiansk and Izium districts. Primary official source for Kharkiv Oblast strike geolocation.

title: Kharkiv Oblast Military Administration - institutional channel
reliability_notes: Same reliability profile as the governor's channel; slightly more administrative content and fewer immediate incident flashes.
description: Kharkiv OVA institutional feed with morning damage digests naming settlements, plus evacuation and utility-restoration notices. Good structured daily summary for the oblast.

title: Kherson Oblast Administration - institutional channel
reliability_notes: Companion institutional feed; same settlement-level precision, same one-sided perspective.
description: Kherson OVA channel with daily shelling summaries, evacuation notices and named-settlement damage reports. Useful backup when the governor's channel is terse.

title: Kherson Oblast Military Administration - head Oleksandr Prokudin
reliability_notes: Extremely location-specific (names Kherson city districts and individual right-bank villages) and publishes daily aggregate shell counts; figures are official and unverified.
description: Daily Kherson OVA head reporting on artillery, mortar and FPV attacks across the right bank plus casualty lists by settlement and district. Among the highest-resolution official strike logs in Ukraine.

title: Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR/GUR) of Ukraine - Telegram
reliability_notes: Fastest HUR outlet but explicitly an information-warfare instrument; individual claims should never be treated as confirmed without independent imagery.
description: Rapid HUR claims of strikes on named Russian refineries, airbases and depots, often with attributed video. Frequently the first official naming of a specific struck facility.

title: Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR/GUR) of Ukraine - website
reliability_notes: Intelligence-service publicity arm; claims about Russian losses, sabotage and deep-strike results are inherently unverifiable and sometimes serve information-operation goals.
description: HUR news releases, named deep-strike and sabotage claims inside Russia and occupied territory, and intercepted-communication publications. Useful for identifying claimed target facilities by exact name and city.

title: Ministry of Defence of Ukraine - official website
reliability_notes: Official policy and communications channel; frontline detail is thinner than the General Staff and framing is uniformly favourable to Ukraine.
description: Ministry news, statements and occasional strike-confirmation releases in Ukrainian and English. Useful for corroborating officially acknowledged deep-strike operations and named targets.

title: Ministry of Defence of Ukraine - X/Twitter (@DefenceU)
reliability_notes: Communications-led account with strong messaging function; treat claimed effects of Ukrainian strikes as unverified until imagery confirms.
description: Fast English-language MoD posts including strike confirmations, equipment-loss infographics and named target announcements. Handy for time-stamping when Ukraine officially claims a deep strike.

title: Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine (MVS) - Telegram
reliability_notes: Consolidates police/DSNS/Guard reporting; casualty figures are preliminary and revised, but place names are generally accurate and specific.
description: MVS consolidated reporting on strike consequences, casualties and rescue operations, usually naming the exact settlement or city district affected.

title: Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine - website
reliability_notes: Official and reasonably precise on locations; casualty numbers are initial estimates.
description: MVS news portal aggregating incident reports from police, DSNS and the National Guard with named settlements. Good permalinked source for civilian-impact events.

title: Mykolaiv Oblast Military Administration
reliability_notes: Settlement-level and generally accurate; port and military-object damage is described euphemistically as "infrastructure".
description: Mykolaiv OVA channel with daily reports on drone and artillery attacks by named hromada, especially in Ochakiv and Kutsurub near the Dnipro estuary.

title: National Police of Ukraine
reliability_notes: Regional police units are among the most location-precise Ukrainian official sources (street addresses are common), but they report only civilian-impact events, never frontline positions.
description: National Police portal with regional-directorate reports on shelling damage, casualties and war-crime documentation, often down to street and house level. Excellent for point-geolocating strikes in rear and near-front cities.

title: Odesa Oblast Military Administration
reliability_notes: Names districts and settlements for civilian damage but withholds specifics on port and energy targets under wartime restrictions.
description: Odesa OVA channel reporting Shahed and missile strikes on Odesa city districts, Izmail and the Danube ports. Key for the south-western maritime axis.

title: Office of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine - War Crimes portal
reliability_notes: Legally framed, evidence-based and location-specific, but covers only alleged Russian crimes and lags events by days to months.
description: Ukrainian prosecution service portal documenting alleged war crimes with dates, oblasts and settlements, plus aggregate child-casualty counts. Strong for retrospective, well-located incident records.

title: Poltava Oblast Military Administration
reliability_notes: Rear-area oblast so events are strike-only; refinery and gas-infrastructure hits are described vaguely as "an infrastructure object".
description: Poltava OVA channel reporting deep-strike drone and missile attacks on Kremenchuk and Myrhorod areas. Important for tracking Russian strikes on rear energy and airbase targets.

title: Recovery.gov.ua - Ukraine recovery and reconstruction portal
reliability_notes: Reconstruction-focused and promotional; damage figures are official Ukrainian estimates and geography is oblast/hromada level.
description: Ukrainian government recovery portal with damage and reconstruction statistics by region and sector. Secondary indicator of where destruction is concentrated in liberated and rear areas.

title: Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) - Telegram
reliability_notes: Claims of SBU drone/naval-drone operations name specific installations but are self-reported and unverifiable; counter-intelligence posts can be selective.
description: SBU announcements including claimed strikes on named Russian airbases, refineries and Black Sea targets, plus detentions of artillery spotters that reveal which cities were being targeted.

title: Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) - website
reliability_notes: Live but bot-blocked (HTTP 403 from datacenter IPs); content is official and one-sided.
description: Web archive of SBU press releases, including spotter/saboteur cases that identify the settlements and facilities Russian forces were targeting.

title: State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) - Telegram
reliability_notes: Highly reliable on the fact and place of an incident because crews attend the scene; it does not describe frontline movement and avoids naming military targets.
description: DSNS operational posts and photos of fire/rescue responses to strikes, naming the settlement and often the specific facility. One of the best official feeds for confirming that a strike actually landed somewhere.

title: State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) - website
reliability_notes: Live but returns HTTP 403 to datacenter IPs; incident locations are accurate, military detail is absent.
description: Official DSNS site with daily nationwide incident digests and regional strike-response reports naming affected settlements. Also hosts the demining and hazard sections.

title: Sumy Oblast Military Administration - head Oleh Hryhorov
reliability_notes: Names hromadas and often individual villages in the border zone, which is critical because Sumy Oblast events cluster along the international border; frontline claims are absent.
description: The Sumy OVA head's reporting on cross-border shelling, glide-bomb and drone strikes by named hromada across Shostka, Krasnopillia and Bilopillia areas. Best official source for the Sumy border axis.

title: Sumy Oblast Military Administration - institutional channel
reliability_notes: Institutional feed with the same border-zone precision; evacuation lists are especially useful and are published as named-settlement enumerations.
description: Sumy OVA channel publishing daily attack digests and mandatory-evacuation settlement lists. Evacuation orders here are a leading indicator of Russian ground pressure.

title: Ukrainian Land Forces - Telegram
reliability_notes: Command-level PR channel; combat footage is genuine but locations are usually described only by direction, and geolocation must be done from the video itself.
description: Official Land Forces channel with unit announcements, brigade-level reporting and combat video from named directions. Useful as an official pointer to which formations are engaged where.

title: Ukrenergo - Telegram
reliability_notes: Deliberately vague about which substations were hit for security reasons, naming only oblasts and outage scale; useful for detecting that an energy strike occurred, not exactly where.
description: Ukraine's TSO reporting damage to generation and transmission after strikes plus emergency outage schedules by region. The outage geography is a reliable indicator of which oblasts absorbed an energy attack.

title: Unmanned Systems Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine - Telegram
reliability_notes: Publishes strike video whose stated locations are unverified official claims; the footage itself is often geolocatable by OSINT analysts.
description: Official channel of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces posting drone strike footage, "kill-zone" claims and deep-strike confirmations. Valuable because the video frequently contains terrain usable for precise geolocation.

title: Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration (ZODA)
reliability_notes: Reports on the Ukrainian-controlled part of the oblast only, naming settlements precisely; has little visibility into occupied districts and none into ZNPP.
description: Zaporizhzhia OVA channel logging strikes on Zaporizhzhia city districts and frontline villages such as Orikhiv, Stepnohirsk and Huliaipole. Key source for the southern axis civilian-impact geography.

title: EEAS - EU Delegation to Ukraine
reliability_notes: EU diplomatic channel; statements condemning strikes usually name the city but appear a day or more after the event.
description: EU Delegation statements, HR/VP declarations and EU support reporting on Ukraine. Useful for authoritative confirmation of major named-city strike events.

title: EU Advisory Mission Ukraine (EUAM Ukraine)
reliability_notes: Civilian security-sector reform mission, not a monitoring mission, so it produces no frontline or incident geography; note that "EUMM" is the separate EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia and is not a Ukraine source.
description: EU's civilian advisory mission in Ukraine, working with police and prosecutors including on war-crime documentation capacity. Indirect value via institutional context.

title: GOV.UK - Russian invasion of Ukraine: UK government response
reliability_notes: Curated UK government landing page, policy-heavy and pro-Ukraine; no incident-level geography.
description: Official UK hub linking Defence Intelligence products, sanctions and support announcements. Useful as an index into UK official Ukraine documentation.

title: NATO - support for Ukraine
reliability_notes: Alliance policy communication; no independent battlefield reporting and no coordinates, and framing is aligned with Ukraine.
description: NATO topic page on assistance to Ukraine, NSATU and related statements. Background and attribution context rather than event data.

title: UK Ministry of Defence Defence Intelligence updates (@DefenceHQ)
reliability_notes: Assessment-based, professionally hedged with probabilistic language, but explicitly pro-Ukrainian in framing and now published far less regularly than the daily 2022-2023 cadence; maps are schematic and never give coordinates.
description: UK Defence Intelligence updates on the situation in Ukraine, usually as an infographic plus short assessment naming axes and towns. Valuable as an allied-government sanity check on both sides' claims.

title: UK MoD news and publications (gov.uk, Ukraine-filtered Atom feed)
reliability_notes: Machine-readable and stable, but Ukraine content is mostly assistance announcements rather than frontline assessment; the standalone Defence Intelligence collection page no longer resolves (HTTP 404).
description: Atom feed of UK MoD publications and news filtered to Ukraine, newest first. The practical automated route to UK official Ukraine material now that the old DI update collection URL is dead.

title: US Department of Defense - news releases
reliability_notes: Live but bot-blocked (HTTP 403 from datacenter IPs); Ukraine content is assistance and policy focused and DoD stopped routine battlefield-assessment briefings, so frontline value is low.
description: US DoD releases, transcripts and PDA/USAI announcements. Mainly useful for capability and aid context rather than event locations.

title: US Department of State - Ukraine
reliability_notes: Policy and diplomatic framing, pro-Ukraine; occasional named-city condemnations but no systematic event reporting.
description: State Department statements, fact sheets and human-rights reporting on Ukraine. Useful for authoritative attribution language on major strike incidents.

title: US European Command (EUCOM)
reliability_notes: Operational-security constrained; publishes almost nothing about the Ukrainian front itself and nothing geolocated.
description: EUCOM newsroom covering European posture, exercises and Ukraine assistance coordination. Contextual only for frontline mapping.

title: Wikipedia: DeepStateMap.Live (background article)
reliability_notes: Encyclopedic background, not a data feed.
description: Reference article on the DeepStateMap project, its methodology, funding and relationship to Ukrainian forces; useful for documenting source provenance.

title: adsb.lol open ADS-B API
machine_readable: REST API + JSON (api.adsb.lol/v2/..., OpenAPI docs at /docs); ODbL-licensed community aggregation
reliability_notes: Fully free and open, no key, ODbL licence; coverage depends on volunteer receiver density, which is sparse inside Ukraine and better in NATO states. Same fundamental limit as any ADS-B source: combat aircraft and drones are not cooperative targets.
description: A genuinely open, key-free live aircraft feed usable in an aggregator to show ISR and military transport activity around Ukraine, and to derive GNSS-interference indicators from navigation-accuracy fields.

title: Airframes.io (ACARS/VDL/HFDL/SATCOM aggregation)
machine_readable: Live web feed plus community MQTT/API access for contributors; open-source tooling on GitHub
reliability_notes: Aggregates volunteer-decoded aircraft datalink messages (ACARS, VDL2, HFDL, Inmarsat/Iridium SATCOM). Coverage is receiver-dependent and message content is mostly airline operational; military use of these links is limited but occasionally revealing. Signals-intelligence-adjacent, so interpretation demands care.
description: A non-ADS-B radio-signal channel that occasionally surfaces aircraft positions and operational messages, including flights that do not appear on ADS-B, useful as corroboration for air-activity timelines.

title: AISStream.io
machine_readable: WebSocket streaming API + JSON (wss://stream.aisstream.io/v0/stream), free key with documented rate limits
reliability_notes: Free live AIS firehose filterable by bounding box and message type, sourced from community receivers, so Black Sea coverage is patchier than commercial satellite AIS. Same AIS spoofing caveats apply.
description: A free, machine-readable live vessel feed that an aggregator can filter to the Black Sea and Azov box to detect port activity, convoy movements and AIS-dark behaviour around Crimea.

title: EcoDozor (Zoi Environment Network / OSCE)
machine_readable: Interactive map with per-incident records and downloadable datasets
reliability_notes: Curated database of war-related environmental incidents in Ukraine (fires, industrial and energy-facility damage, chemical releases, mine flooding), each geolocated and sourced, combining satellite fire/imagery evidence with open reporting. Curated and therefore incomplete, with a lag of days to weeks.
description: Point-geolocated, source-cited records of strikes on industrial, energy and chemical facilities across Ukraine, giving verified coordinates and dates for infrastructure events that thermal detections alone cannot identify.

title: EUMETSAT Data Store fire products (Sentinel-3 SLSTR FRP)
machine_readable: REST/OpenSearch Data Store API + NetCDF/SAFE download
reliability_notes: Sentinel-3A/B SLSTR active-fire and FRP at ~1 km (S7 band), with a dedicated fire channel that saturates less than MODIS; two satellites give extra overpasses including night. Latency ~hours.
description: A third independent thermal sensor family for fire-based frontline mapping, useful to confirm VIIRS clusters and to catch night-time fires.

title: EUMETSAT LSA SAF Fire Radiative Power (Meteosat/SEVIRI FRP-PIXEL)
machine_readable: NetCDF/HDF products via LSA SAF data service and EUMETSAT Data Store API
reliability_notes: Geostationary Meteosat gives 15-minute (MSG) to 10-minute (MTG) refresh over Europe, but pixel size at Ukraine latitudes is ~4-6 km, so only large, intense fires are detected. Complements polar-orbiter VIIRS by catching fires that start and die between overpasses.
description: Sub-hourly detection of large fires (refineries, fuel depots, ammunition dumps) anywhere in Ukraine, giving a timestamp for the strike far tighter than VIIRS overpass gaps allow.

title: Global Fishing Watch map and API
machine_readable: REST API v3 (gateway.api.globalfishingwatch.org) with free token; vessel, event and SAR-detection endpoints
reliability_notes: Combines AIS with satellite SAR and VIIRS night-light vessel detections to find vessels that are not broadcasting AIS. Built for fisheries, so Black Sea military interpretation requires care; SAR detections have false positives on wind farms, rigs and wave clutter.
description: Its SAR and night-light vessel detections identify dark ships in the Black Sea that have switched off AIS, a method used publicly to track sanctioned oil and stolen Ukrainian grain shipments.

title: IODA (Internet Outage Detection and Analysis), Georgia Tech
machine_readable: REST API + JSON (api.ioda.inetintel.cc.gatech.edu/v2/, public, documented) with per-country/region/ASN time series
reliability_notes: Fuses three independent signals (BGP reachability, active probing, network telescope darknet traffic) at country, region and ASN level, so it is far more reproducible than single-signal claims. Regional geolocation of IP space is imperfect; small localised outages can be missed.
description: Free, API-accessible, region-level Ukrainian outage time series that let you correlate connectivity collapses with reported strikes, and detect occupied-area network changes without relying on any belligerent's statements.

title: MarineTraffic
machine_readable: Commercial REST API (services.marinetraffic.com) on paid plans; free web map with delay
reliability_notes: Largest terrestrial plus satellite AIS aggregator. Free tier is delayed and coverage-limited; bot-blocks bare HTTP clients (403). AIS is self-reported and routinely spoofed or switched off by Russian and sanctioned vessels, so absence and even positions must be treated sceptically.
description: Tracks Black Sea and Sea of Azov shipping, Russian naval auxiliaries, grain-corridor convoys and port activity at Odesa, Novorossiysk and Sevastopol, providing dated positions for maritime incidents and USV strikes.

title: NetBlocks
machine_readable: Reports and social alerts; internal measurement platform not publicly queryable
reliability_notes: Fast public alerts on connectivity collapses with named operators and timestamps, widely cited; methodology details and raw data are not fully open, so claims cannot always be independently reproduced. Attribution of cause (strike vs power vs deliberate shutdown) is often inferred.
description: Rapid, quotable confirmation that connectivity has collapsed in a specific Ukrainian city or across an operator, which in practice correlates tightly with major strikes on energy and telecom nodes.

title: OpenAerialMap
machine_readable: STAC-like catalogue API (api.openaerialmap.org) + TMS/XYZ tiles per image; openly licensed GeoTIFFs
reliability_notes: Community/NGO repository of openly licensed drone and satellite imagery, often very high resolution (cm-scale for drone flights) but sparse and event-driven. Ukraine holdings are limited and contributor-dependent.
description: Occasionally provides cm-resolution openly licensed drone orthophotos of Ukrainian damaged areas that can be used freely for damage mapping and geolocation.

title: OpenSky Network
machine_readable: REST API and Trino/Impala historical database; OpenSky Python API; free for research use
reliability_notes: Research-grade ADS-B/Mode-S archive going back years with documented coverage metadata, ideal for reproducible studies (e.g. quantifying airspace closure or ISR flight-hour trends). Rate limits are tight for anonymous users; blocks some scrapers (403 to bare curl).
description: Historical and live flight data with an academic archive, used in published work on Ukrainian airspace closure, ISR patterns and GNSS interference derived from aircraft position-quality fields.

title: Raspberry Shake citizen seismograph network
machine_readable: Open FDSN-compliant data via the Raspberry Shake data centre (fdsnws services) and StationView map; open station metadata
reliability_notes: Thousands of low-cost volunteer seismographs streaming openly; instrument quality and station density vary and there are few stations inside Ukraine, though nearby Poland, Romania and Moldova stations can record large blasts. Urban noise limits sensitivity.
description: Openly accessible waveform data from citizen sensors near Ukraine that can be used to independently detect and time large explosions, including cross-border events, at zero cost.

title: RIPEstat / RIPE Atlas
machine_readable: RIPEstat Data API (stat.ripe.net/data/{call}/data.json) and RIPE Atlas measurement API (atlas.ripe.net/api/v2/), free with account for custom measurements
reliability_notes: Authoritative BGP routing history, prefix visibility and traceroute measurements from thousands of probes. Requires networking expertise to interpret; probe density inside Ukraine, especially occupied areas, is limited.
description: BGP-level evidence of Ukrainian ISP prefixes being rerouted through Russian upstreams is one of the hardest technical indicators that a settlement or district has come under Russian administrative control.

title: UNOSAT (UN Satellite Centre) Ukraine damage assessments
machine_readable: Downloadable PDF maps plus GIS layers (SHP/GeoJSON/GeoPackage) and datasets on HDX
reliability_notes: Manual expert interpretation of very-high-resolution commercial imagery, producing damage points classified by severity for named Ukrainian cities and oblasts; the de facto ground truth used to train automated methods. Coverage is limited to tasked cities and dates; not comprehensive, and lags events by days to weeks.
description: Authoritative, individually digitised damage points for specific Ukrainian settlements, letting you say precisely which buildings in Mariupol, Bakhmut or Avdiivka were destroyed and when they were first observed damaged.

title: Yandex Maps satellite and panoramas
machine_readable: Unofficial XYZ tile access; official Yandex Maps JS API for embedding
reliability_notes: Frequently has higher-resolution and better-updated pre-war imagery and street-level panoramas of Ukrainian and Russian towns than Western providers, plus Russian-language toponyms and building numbers. Occupied-territory labelling follows Russian official positions; imagery of sensitive Russian sites is censored/blurred.
description: The reference dataset for pre-war ground truth: street panoramas and building-level imagery that let analysts match a geolocated video frame to an exact address in a Donbas town.

title: air-alarms.in.ua
machine_readable: Live web map with historical alert statistics; JSON consumed by the front end
reliability_notes: Volunteer statistics site tracking alert start/stop times, durations and totals per oblast since 2022. Derived from official alert declarations, so inherits their administrative granularity; not an impact-location source.
description: Historical air-alert statistics by oblast that quantify which regions are under sustained aerial threat, a useful long-run correlate of strike-campaign focus and of proximity to the front.

title: alerts.in.ua API (Ukrainian air-raid alerts)
machine_readable: REST API + JSON (api.alerts.in.ua/v1/alerts/active.json, /v1/iot/active_air_raid_alerts_by_oblast.json, /v1/regions/{uid}/alerts/{period}.json); Bearer token or query-param token
reliability_notes: Free volunteer-run service with a personal token; documented soft limit 8-10 requests/min per IP, hard limit 12/min, and 2/min for the historical endpoint. Granularity down to oblast, raion, hromada and city UIDs. Alerts reflect official oblast/hromada air-defence declarations, so they indicate threat axes rather than exact impact points, and are declared conservatively wide.
description: The cleanest machine-readable feed of Ukrainian air-raid alerts by administrative unit; sequences of alert onsets across oblasts trace missile and Shahed flight corridors in near real time, and historical queries let you reconstruct which districts were threatened during a given strike.

title: EOS Data Analytics LandViewer
machine_readable: REST APIs for search/processing on paid plans; free browser access to Sentinel/Landsat scenes
reliability_notes: Ukrainian-founded EO company; free tier gives Sentinel-2, Landsat and Sentinel-1 browsing with band-math and change detection, with scene-download quotas. High-resolution commercial archive is paid.
description: A convenient free viewer with built-in change-detection and index tools for comparing two dates over a Ukrainian settlement, run by a company with strong Ukraine ties.

title: Neptun live Shahed and missile tracking map
machine_readable: Web, Android and iOS apps with ~5-second refresh; no documented public API
reliability_notes: Aggregates Ukrainian monitoring-channel reports into live drone and missile track markers with direction of flight, refreshed every few seconds. Tracks are crowd-and-monitor-derived, not radar truth: positions are approximate, misattributions and duplicate tracks occur, and coverage depends on active spotters. Free.
description: One of the most granular public sources of where individual Shahed drones and missiles are at a given moment, giving point-level, timestamped indications of inbound threat axes across Ukraine.

title: Ukraine Alarm (Povitryana Tryvoha) API
machine_readable: REST API at api.ukrainealarm.com with Swagger docs and an API key issued on request; JSON alert status and region lists; @UkraineAlertBot on Telegram
reliability_notes: Long-running alert aggregator behind popular apps and siren-automation devices; the API host is behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to bare clients without an API key. Same interpretive limit as any alert feed: administrative-unit granularity, not impact coordinates.
description: A second independent Ukrainian alert API, valuable for cross-checking alerts.in.ua and for consuming the alert stream through a Telegram bot in an aggregation pipeline.

title: Ukrainian Nature Conservation Group
machine_readable: Reports and articles; no standing data API
reliability_notes: Ukrainian conservation NGO publishing assessments of war impacts on protected areas, including fire and land-cover change in and near occupied and frontline nature reserves. Output is publication-based, focused on protected-area boundaries rather than the military frontline, and largely Ukrainian-language.
description: Ukrainian-perspective analyses of fire and habitat destruction in frontline and occupied protected areas, useful for interpreting large persistent fire clusters in steppe and reserve areas that are not agricultural burning.

title: Ukrenergo (Ukrainian TSO) operational updates
machine_readable: Web publications and press releases; some consumption charts, no open API
reliability_notes: Official Ukrainian transmission system operator. Wartime disclosure is deliberately restricted (no facility-level locations) and the site is behind Cloudflare (403 to bare clients). Statements confirm that strikes hit energy infrastructure and which oblasts face restrictions, without naming substations.
description: Authoritative confirmation, by oblast, that energy infrastructure was struck and where load restrictions apply, providing the ground truth to interpret nighttime-lights and internet-outage anomalies.

title: war.ukrzen.in.ua alert monitor
machine_readable: Live alert map and downloadable/scrapable alert history tables
reliability_notes: Small volunteer project with a long alert archive; no formal API or SLA and the interface is Ukrainian-only. Useful chiefly as an independent archival cross-check.
description: An independent archive of Ukrainian air-alert timelines per region, handy for verifying whether a claimed strike time coincided with a declared alert.

title: Zvook acoustic aerial-threat detection network
machine_readable: None public (operational data goes to Ukrainian air defence, not to open channels)
reliability_notes: Grassroots Ukrainian network of parabolic-microphone acoustic sensors with on-device machine learning that detect low-flying cruise missiles and Shahed drones below radar horizon; reported coverage of a minority of Ukrainian territory concentrated near the border. Raw detections are not public; they feed military air-defence and, indirectly, public alert systems. Listed for completeness as a sensor layer whose outputs surface downstream.
description: Explains where the point-level drone and missile track data seen in Ukrainian alert apps and monitoring channels physically originates: a distributed acoustic sensor grid, not radar or satellites.

title: ADS-B Exchange (unfiltered flight tracking)
machine_readable: REST API via RapidAPI for feeders/subscribers plus historical archive downloads (see adsbexchange.com/data-products)
reliability_notes: The only major aggregator that does not filter military or blocked aircraft, making it the primary tool for tracking NATO ISR flights (RQ-4, RC-135, P-8, E-3) over the Black Sea and Poland. Ukrainian and Russian combat aircraft usually do not transmit ADS-B, so it reveals surveillance and support aviation, not the frontline itself. API access requires feeding data or a paid plan.
description: ISR orbit patterns over the Black Sea and Romania/Poland are a strong indirect indicator of where Western intelligence expects activity, and MIL/ELINT flight geometry helps corroborate the timing of large Russian strike packages.

title: Airbus Space Solutions (Pleiades Neo / OneAtlas)
machine_readable: OneAtlas REST APIs and streaming WMTS for subscribers; free sample gallery
reliability_notes: Pleiades Neo 30 cm, Pleiades 50 cm, SPOT 1.5 m, plus TerraSAR-X/PAZ SAR. Paid tasking with export-control and licence restrictions; sample imagery and press releases are the free surface.
description: The main European very-high-resolution alternative to Maxar; its imagery appears in European media geolocation of Ukrainian strike sites and in EU/UN damage assessments.

title: Alaska Satellite Facility Vertex (Sentinel-1 SAR search)
machine_readable: Search API (asf.alaska.edu/api) + bulk download python client; STAC-like GeoJSON/CSV/metalink output
