reliability_notes: NASA-funded SAR DAAC mirroring Sentinel-1 GRD/SLC/burst products plus ALOS and (from 2025) NISAR; Earthdata Login required. Sentinel-1 revisit over Ukraine degraded after the S1B failure and partially restored with S1C.
description: The easiest route to Sentinel-1 SLC pairs and burst products needed for interferometric coherence damage mapping, the technique behind most credible nationwide Ukraine building-damage estimates.

title: ASF HyP3 on-demand InSAR/RTC processing
machine_readable: REST API + Python SDK (hyp3_sdk) for job submission; outputs GeoTIFF InSAR coherence, unwrapped phase, RTC
reliability_notes: Free monthly credit allocation per Earthdata user; jobs take tens of minutes to hours. Coherence loss is caused by many things besides destruction (vegetation growth, ploughing, snow, water), so raw coherence-drop maps over Ukrainian cropland are noisy.
description: Lets a non-specialist generate Sentinel-1 interferometric coherence change products for a Ukrainian town without owning a SAR processor, the standard DIY method to detect buildings destroyed between two dates through cloud and darkness.

title: Bing Maps aerial imagery
machine_readable: Bing Maps REST/Tile API (key required); free browser viewing
reliability_notes: Independent high-resolution aerial/satellite mosaic with different acquisition dates from Google and Esri, plus Bing building footprints (open data). Vintage varies widely across Ukraine and is not exposed per tile.
description: A third independent pre-war imagery baseline; comparing Google, Bing, Esri and Yandex vintages of the same Ukrainian village often brackets when a structure was built or destroyed.

title: BlackSky
machine_readable: Spectra AI platform APIs for customers; public imagery via press and social channels
reliability_notes: ~1 m Gen-2 (and sub-metre Gen-3) optical with high revisit optimised for dawn-to-dusk monitoring; publicly known to supply imagery under Ukraine-related contracts. Not an open data source.
description: High-revisit 1 m monitoring of fixed Ukrainian targets (airbases, ports, staging areas); publicly released frames periodically document Black Sea Fleet and airfield damage.

title: Building Damage Assessment Portal (Conflict Ecology, Oregon State)
machine_readable: Web GIS with ADM3 damage counts, damage clusters and probability layers; geospatial downloads gated by authorisation
reliability_notes: Same InSAR coherent-change-detection lineage as the DDMG Ukraine work; the live portal instance rotates between active conflicts (recent deployments covered other theatres), so Ukraine layers may be archival rather than current. Download requires contacting the team.
description: District-level (ADM3) counts of damaged buildings derived automatically from Sentinel-1, a quantitative and non-partisan measure of where the heaviest destruction, and therefore the fighting, has occurred.

title: Capella Space Open Data
machine_readable: STAC catalogue + GeoTIFF/SLC in a public S3 bucket, documented on the AWS registry page
reliability_notes: Sample X-band SAR at ~50 cm to 1 m, spotlight and stripmap; a demonstration archive rather than an operational feed, so scene availability over Ukraine is incidental. Capella was acquired by IQT/IonQ-adjacent owners and its commercial offering has shifted; check current status before relying on it.
description: Free sample high-resolution SAR scenes useful for method development and for occasional Ukrainian sites, plus a reference for what tasked commercial SAR can resolve.

title: Chaos Signals Ukraine strike map
machine_readable: Web map aggregating Ukrainian official and monitoring-channel reports; refresh on the order of minutes
reliability_notes: Third-party aggregator of Ukrainian air-alert and monitoring-channel data into an English-language map of alerts, drone and missile activity. Derived and unattributed at the item level, so it should be treated as a convenience layer over primary Ukrainian feeds rather than an independent sensor.
description: English-language live map of Ukrainian air-raid alerts and reported drone/missile activity, useful as a quick orientation layer before drilling into primary Ukrainian alert APIs.

title: Cloudflare Radar Ukraine
machine_readable: REST API + JSON/CSV (api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/..., documented at developers.cloudflare.com/radar), free token
reliability_notes: Traffic-volume, ASN, protocol and outage-annotation data derived from Cloudflare's global network; granularity is country and sometimes subdivision/ASN, not settlement. Bot-protected for bare curl (403 in browser path) while the API works with a token. Traffic dips can reflect strikes, power cuts, cable damage or routing changes.
description: Sharp drops in Ukrainian internet traffic by region or ASN provide near-real-time evidence of strikes on power and telecom infrastructure, and BGP/ASN shifts expose rerouting of occupied-territory networks through Russian carriers.

title: Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS) Ukraine analyses
machine_readable: Reports and briefings, some with accompanying geospatial data and imagery analysis
reliability_notes: Specialist NGO combining remote sensing (fire detections, Sentinel imagery, plume analysis) with open-source reporting on Ukrainian industrial and environmental war damage. Analytical and episodic rather than a live feed; explicitly discusses methodological uncertainty.
description: Methodologically careful remote-sensing analyses of Ukrainian infrastructure and environmental damage, including guidance on how to distinguish combat fires from agricultural burning in FIRMS data.

title: Copernicus Browser (Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem)
machine_readable: OData, STAC, OGC WMS/WMTS and Sentinel Hub-compatible Process/Catalog APIs (documentation.dataspace.copernicus.eu)
reliability_notes: Sentinel-2 L1C/L2A at 10 m optical with 2-5 day revisit over Ukraine; Sentinel-1 C-band SAR (GRD/SLC) at ~10-20 m sees through cloud and night. Free ESA licence permits redistribution with attribution. 10 m is too coarse to count vehicles but resolves trench lines, craters in fields, destroyed buildings, bridge cuts and river crossings.
description: The workhorse free imagery source for verifying frontline changes: fresh trench networks, bridge and dam damage, burn scars, flooded terrain and destroyed built-up areas, with an archive back to 2015 for before/after comparison.

title: Copernicus Data Space OData and STAC APIs
machine_readable: OData catalogue query + S3-compatible download; STAC at catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/stac
reliability_notes: Replaced the retired scihub.copernicus.eu (now offline). Free accounts get generous but finite download quotas; S3 credentials issued per user. Sentinel-1 SLC pairs needed for coherence work are large (several GB each).
description: Programmatic discovery and download of every Sentinel-1/2/3 scene over Ukraine, the foundation for automated change-detection and SAR coherence damage pipelines.

title: Copernicus EFFIS / Global Wildfire Information System
machine_readable: Web GIS with WMS layers and downloadable burnt-area polygons; GWIS at gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu offers country stats and API-ish downloads
reliability_notes: EU JRC system: active fire points (MODIS/VIIRS ingest) plus burnt-area perimeters derived from Sentinel-2. Burnt-area products lag days-to-weeks and are tuned for wildland fire, so shelling burn scars in cropland can be missed or misclassified.
description: Burnt-area polygons (rather than points) around the contact line quantify how much land has been scorched, a durable spatial signature of sustained artillery activity that survives cloud gaps.

title: Decentralized Damage Mapping Group (Scher and Van Den Hoek, InSAR coherent change detection)
machine_readable: Peer-reviewed method with published derived damage datasets; portal downloads on request via data@conflict-ecology.org
reliability_notes: Uses 17,000+ Sentinel-1 InSAR coherence images in a coherent change detection framework across Ukrainian settlements (Mar 2022 - Oct 2023 in the published study). Coherence loss is a proxy, not a confirmation: ploughing, snow, flooding and vegetation cause false alarms, and the method is calibrated for built-up areas. Release cadence is publication-driven, not continuous.
description: The most-cited independent nationwide Ukraine building-damage estimate produced without any government or belligerent input, widely used by journalists to sanity-check both sides' claims about which towns are destroyed and where fighting has been heaviest.

title: Earth Observation Group VIIRS Nighttime Lights (Colorado School of Mines)
machine_readable: Direct HTTPS download of monthly/annual GeoTIFF composites; free EOG account for some products
reliability_notes: Independent VIIRS DNB processing chain (monthly and annual cloud-free composites, plus daily products) with careful outlier removal; monthly cadence limits event attribution. Also produces the VIIRS Nightfire (VNF) gas-flare product.
description: Monthly night-light composites give a clean, comparable time series of how much light each Ukrainian oblast and city has lost since 2022, and VIIRS Nightfire detects hot industrial sources such as burning refineries.

title: EarthScope/IRIS station map and FDSN data services
machine_readable: FDSN web services (station, dataselect, event) returning miniSEED/StationXML; standard obspy client support
reliability_notes: Federated archive of global seismic and infrasound stations with standardised FDSN access. Requires signal-processing skill; array/infrasound coverage relevant to Ukraine is limited and much CTBTO infrasound data is restricted to member-state users.
description: The gateway to raw waveform and infrasound data for anyone wanting to independently locate large explosions in Ukraine using arrival-time differences rather than relying on published catalogues.

title: Element 84 Earth Search STAC (Sentinel-2 COGs on AWS)
machine_readable: STAC API v1 (GET /search, POST /search) over sentinel-2-l2a, sentinel-2-l1c, landsat-c2-l2 COG collections
reliability_notes: No key, no registration for search; imagery served as cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs from AWS open-data buckets (requester-pays applies to some collections). Latency of a few hours to a day behind acquisition.
description: The lowest-friction machine endpoint for pulling only the pixels you need over a Ukrainian coordinate, ideal for automated daily change detection without downloading whole scenes.

title: EMSC-CSEM European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre
machine_readable: FDSN event web service and real-time feeds via seismicportal.eu (REST + WebSocket, GeoJSON/QuakeML)
reliability_notes: Denser European station coverage than the global USGS catalogue, so a lower detection threshold over Ukraine and neighbouring Russia, plus felt-report crowdsourcing. Explosion/earthquake discrimination is still imperfect and events are sometimes revised or removed.
description: The most sensitive publicly queryable seismic catalogue for the Ukraine theatre, used to independently confirm and time-stamp large ammunition-depot detonations and infrastructure blasts.

title: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform
machine_readable: REST API + XML (web-api.tp.entsoe.eu/api) with free security token; documented query types
reliability_notes: Ukraine's grid has been synchronised with continental Europe since March 2022, so Ukrainian load, generation and cross-border flow data appear in the platform. Country-level, hourly-to-quarter-hourly resolution; reporting completeness for Ukraine is weaker than for EU members and wartime data can be withheld for security reasons.
description: Sharp drops in Ukrainian generation or spikes in emergency imports from Poland, Slovakia, Hungary and Romania are a quantitative, machine-readable fingerprint of successful Russian strikes on the power system.

title: Esri World Imagery Wayback
machine_readable: Versioned XYZ/WMTS tile services per Wayback release date, usable in any web map
reliability_notes: Provides every historical version of the Esri World Imagery basemap (sub-metre in most Ukrainian settlements) back to 2014, each with a release date. Release date is not acquisition date, so imagery vintage must be inferred and can lag by months to years.
description: The best free way to obtain multiple dated pre-war high-resolution basemap versions of a Ukrainian location, essential for before/after geolocation when Google Earth has only one frame.

title: Flightradar24
machine_readable: Commercial REST API (fr24api.flightradar24.com) on paid plans; web app free
reliability_notes: Largest receiver network with MLAT and satellite ADS-B, but filters some military/blocked aircraft, so ADS-B Exchange is preferred for military work. Bot-blocks plain HTTP clients (403) while serving browsers normally. Also publishes a GPS-jamming visualisation derived from aircraft navigation accuracy.
description: Broadest live aviation picture around Ukraine, including airspace-closure effects, humanitarian and government flights, and a GNSS-interference view over the Black Sea and eastern Europe.

title: Google Earth (web) and Google Earth Pro historical imagery
reliability_notes: Sub-metre to ~50 cm commercial mosaics with irregular acquisition dates; the historical imagery slider in Earth Pro often yields several pre-war and occasionally wartime frames for Ukrainian settlements. Dates are per-tile and can be mislabelled.
description: Indispensable for geolocating a video or photo to an exact building, treeline or road junction, and for establishing the pre-war appearance of a site now claimed to be destroyed or captured.

title: Google Earth Engine
machine_readable: JavaScript Code Editor and Python API over petabyte-scale ImageCollections; REST API for registered cloud projects
reliability_notes: Free for noncommercial/research use with a registered Cloud project; commercial use is paid. Hosts Sentinel-1 GRD, Sentinel-2, Landsat, VIIRS FIRMS and Black Marble collections. Sentinel-1 SLC phase is not available, so true InSAR coherence must be done elsewhere.
description: The platform on which most published Ukraine-wide damage, fire and nighttime-lights analyses were computed, and the host for the public Ukraine Damage Explorer apps.

title: GPSJam GPS interference map
machine_readable: Daily hex-grid map with per-day URLs (gpsjam.org/?date=YYYY-MM-DD); no documented public API
reliability_notes: Built by John Wiseman from ADS-B Exchange aircraft navigation-integrity (NIC/NACp) reports, aggregated into hex cells and published daily. Only shows interference where aircraft actually fly, so coverage over active Ukrainian airspace is thin and heavily biased toward corridors around the conflict (Black Sea, Poland, Baltic, Moldova, Romania). Interference cause (jamming vs spoofing vs equipment) is not distinguished.
description: The best-known public map of GNSS jamming/spoofing, whose persistent hotspots around the Black Sea, Kaliningrad, Rostov and Moscow reveal Russian electronic-warfare posture and often flag imminent or ongoing drone/missile activity.

title: HawkEye 360 (RF geolocation from space)
machine_readable: Commercial RF analytics APIs; selected findings published publicly
reliability_notes: Clusters of formation-flying satellites geolocate emitters (marine radars, VHF/UHF, GNSS interference sources) with kilometre-scale accuracy. Data is paid and export-controlled; the public record consists of company reports and media collaborations.
description: Space-based RF geolocation has publicly identified GPS-jamming sources and AIS-dark vessels in the Black Sea, offering a physics-based fix on electronic-warfare emitters and sanctions-evading shipping.

title: ICEYE
machine_readable: Commercial tasking/analytics APIs; no open public feed
reliability_notes: Largest SAR smallsat constellation (25 cm spot mode, sub-daily revisit) and a confirmed supplier of SAR capacity to Ukraine under a government-funded contract. Data itself is not public; public value comes from published imagery and flood/damage analytics releases.
description: The dominant SAR provider actually used over Ukraine; its published frames and flood-extent products periodically enter the public record and are cited in strike-damage reporting.

title: Kentik network-analysis blog (Doug Madory internet-observability reporting)
machine_readable: Narrative analyses with charts; underlying aggregate data is commercial
reliability_notes: Widely respected BGP/NetFlow analyses of Ukrainian and Russian routing changes, occupied-territory ISP takeovers and traffic collapses. Publication is episodic (when something notable happens) and the raw data is not released.
description: Provides the expert interpretation layer on top of routing data, documenting for example when occupied Kherson or Mariupol networks were forcibly rerouted via Russian carriers, a control-change signal independent of battlefield claims.

title: Maxar Open Data on AWS Registry
machine_readable: STAC catalogue + COGs in a public S3 bucket (s3://maxar-opendata), documented on the registry page
reliability_notes: No credentials needed for anonymous S3 reads; CC BY-NC 4.0. Organised by event/collection, so you must know which collection covers your Ukrainian area of interest.
description: Machine-readable access to the free high-resolution Maxar crisis imagery, enabling automated tiling and comparison against later frames of the same Ukrainian site.

title: Microsoft Planetary Computer
machine_readable: STAC API + SAS token signing (planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1), hosted Jupyter Hub
reliability_notes: Hosts Sentinel-1 RTC, Sentinel-2 L2A, Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS and NAIP as analysis-ready COGs; free compute allocation requires an approved account request. Some collections were re-scoped over time, so verify collection availability before building on it.
description: Cloud-native access to co-located Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical archives over Ukraine, plus free notebooks, so damage and fire analyses can run next to the data instead of downloading terabytes.

title: NASA Black Marble nighttime lights
machine_readable: VNP46A1/A2/A3/A4 HDF5 products via LAADS DAAC REST/wget; GIBS layers for visual browsing
reliability_notes: VIIRS Day/Night Band at ~500 m, nightly, atmospherically and moonlight-corrected in VNP46A2. Cloud, snow cover and moon phase create artefacts; blackouts from strikes are hard to distinguish from scheduled load-shedding, curfew dimming or evacuation-driven depopulation.
description: The standard method for mapping Russian strike effects on Ukrainian electricity: night-light loss maps show which cities and districts went dark after infrastructure attacks, and light returning in occupied or liberated settlements signals population and control changes.

title: NASA CMR (Common Metadata Repository) search API
reliability_notes: Metadata-only: returns granule IDs, spatial/temporal extents and download links across all NASA DAACs. No imagery itself; some collections need Earthdata Login for the actual files.
description: Machine discovery layer for finding every NASA satellite granule covering a given Ukrainian coordinate and date range, the first step in any automated overhead-imagery pipeline.

title: NASA FIRMS Active Fire Data archive and NRT downloads
machine_readable: Bulk CSV/SHP/KML/GeoJSON archive downloads plus 24h/48h/7d NRT files
reliability_notes: Standard (science-quality) archive lags NRT by weeks-to-months but has better geolocation and fewer artifacts; NRT files refresh several times a day. Requires an Earthdata Login for custom archive requests.
description: Historical fire-point archives for Ukraine let you reconstruct how the frontline moved month by month since Feb 2022 and to build a seasonal baseline that separates agricultural burning from combat fires.

title: NASA FIRMS Fire Map (VIIRS/MODIS active fire)
machine_readable: Interactive map with WMS/WFS and CSV/SHP/KML export from the same platform (firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov)
reliability_notes: VIIRS 375 m (NOAA-20/21, S-NPP) and MODIS 1 km thermal anomalies; ~4-6 overpasses/day at Ukraine latitudes; NRT latency ~1-3 h (URT ~60 min for US/Canada only). Massive false-positive load from agricultural stubble burning (Mar-Apr and Jul-Sep), gas flares, industrial heat and wildfires; clouds/smoke suppress detections, so absence of fire is not absence of shelling.
description: The single most-used physics-based frontline proxy: dense linear clusters of VIIRS thermal anomalies along a contact line reveal artillery/MLRS impacts, burning vehicles and strike sites. Analysts overlay day-by-day fire clusters to infer where the line of contact sits and which axes are active.

title: NASA FIRMS WMS/WFS services
machine_readable: OGC WMS + WFS (GeoJSON/GML) endpoints documented on the FIRMS mapserver pages
reliability_notes: Layer-based access with MAP_KEY; useful for direct QGIS/Leaflet integration without writing a CSV parser. Same detection physics and false positives as the FIRMS point products.
description: Lets a mapping front end render live fire detections as an overlay on a Ukraine frontline map without downloading and reprojecting files.

title: NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services) WMTS/WMS
reliability_notes: No key, no rate-limit registration; 1000+ layers with daily time dimension back to 2000 for MODIS and 2012 for VIIRS. Best-available granule mosaics may include swath gaps and cloud.
description: The raw tile service behind Worldview: lets an aggregator embed dated NASA satellite basemaps, fire overlays and Black Marble nighttime lights for any Ukraine viewport programmatically.

title: NASA LAADS DAAC (VIIRS/MODIS granule archive)
machine_readable: HTTPS/REST file API plus wget/curl bulk download; Earthdata Login token required
reliability_notes: Source of VNP14IMG (375 m active fire), VNP02/VNP03 radiance and VNP46 Black Marble products; NRT collections (5000-series) available within hours, standard collections after reprocessing.
description: Where to get the underlying granules if you want to run your own fire-detection or nighttime-lights thresholding for Ukraine rather than trusting FIRMS defaults.

title: NASA Worldview
machine_readable: Backed by GIBS WMTS/WMS; snapshot API at wvs.earthdata.nasa.gov/api/v1/snapshot for georeferenced GeoTIFF/PNG export
reliability_notes: VIIRS true colour at 250-375 m, MODIS 250 m, plus thermal anomaly, aerosol, smoke and nighttime-lights layers; near-real-time layers appear within ~3 h of overpass. Resolution too coarse to see vehicles, adequate to see large smoke plumes, burn scars, dam/flood changes and city-scale blackouts.
description: Fast, no-login way to eyeball a whole Ukrainian oblast on a given date: smoke plumes from refinery/depot strikes, flood extent after the Kakhovka dam, and burn scars along the contact line, with fire points and nighttime lights toggleable on the same canvas.

title: NOAA CLASS (VIIRS Active Fires EDR archive)
machine_readable: Order-based bulk download of NetCDF granules; NCEI catalogue landing page at ncei.noaa.gov (dataset gov.noaa.ncdc:C00971)
reliability_notes: NOAA operational VIIRS Active Fire EDR/AF-EDR at 375 m nadir with fire radiative power; delivered as 10-minute aggregated NetCDF TARs. Order-queue based (not instant), clunkier than FIRMS but is the authoritative NOAA operational stream.
description: The NOAA-operational (as opposed to NASA science) VIIRS fire detection line, useful as an independent second opinion on whether a hotspot cluster in Donbas is real.

title: NOAA Hazard Mapping System Fire and Smoke Product
machine_readable: Daily fire-point shapefiles/KML and smoke-plume polygons via NOAA OSPO/satepsanone directories
reliability_notes: Analyst-quality-controlled fire points plus manually drawn smoke plume polygons; primary focus is North America, global coverage is partial, so Ukraine coverage is inconsistent. Daily cadence, not real-time.
description: Human-vetted smoke-plume polygons are a useful cross-check when trying to confirm a large fire (refinery, depot, forest) from a suspected strike, where automated hotspots alone are ambiguous.

title: Planet Disaster Data program
machine_readable: Activation-based access through Planet Explorer and the Data API
reliability_notes: Access granted per activation to responders and, in some cases, media/researchers; licence restricts redistribution. Coverage windows are limited to the activation area and period.
description: Route by which humanitarian and research users have obtained free Planet imagery of specific Ukrainian disaster events such as the Kakhovka dam breach flooding.

title: Planet Labs NICFI / Education and Research programs
machine_readable: REST Data API (api.planet.com) + Basemaps XYZ/WMTS tiles under program licences
reliability_notes: PlanetScope Dove/SuperDove: ~3-4 m daily global coverage, SkySat ~50 cm tasked. NICFI free access is geographically restricted to the tropics, so Ukraine is NOT covered by NICFI; Ukraine access comes via the Education and Research program, disaster-data activations or paid contracts. 3 m daily is the sweet spot for detecting new craters, revetments, pontoon bridges and vehicle concentrations.
description: Near-daily 3 m coverage is the highest-cadence commercial optical source; Planet frames underpin many published claims about Russian troop build-ups, new fortification lines and river-crossing attempts.

title: Rapid Damage Assessment (Sentinel-1) on-demand tool
machine_readable: Google Earth Engine app running the published inference pipeline on user-selected AOI and dates
reliability_notes: Runs the same model for any user-chosen area and time window, so freshness is limited only by Sentinel-1 availability (days). Accuracy degrades on small or lightly built settlements and outside the training distribution; outputs are probabilities, not confirmed damage.
description: Lets anyone generate a fresh SAR-based damage map for a currently contested Ukrainian town within minutes, an independent check on claims that a settlement has been levelled or captured.

title: SafeAirspace (OPSGROUP conflict-zone airspace warnings)
machine_readable: Country-by-country risk pages; no public API
reliability_notes: Aggregates NOTAMs and state aviation warnings into plain-language conflict-zone risk assessments by country and flight level. Editorially curated, aviation-safety focused, updated when states publish notices rather than continuously.
description: Documents which airspace over and around Ukraine, Russia and the Black Sea is closed or hazardous and why, a formal-record indicator of missile/drone activity zones and of how far the threat envelope extends.

title: Satellogic
machine_readable: Tasking/archive APIs for customers; an open Satellogic EarthView sample dataset is published on AWS
reliability_notes: ~70 cm to 1 m multispectral and hyperspectral with high daily capacity; comparatively low cost per km2. Not an open Ukraine feed.
description: A lower-cost tasking option for monitoring specific Ukrainian coordinates repeatedly, relevant when researchers or media buy imagery of a contested settlement.

title: Sentinel Hub custom scripts repository
machine_readable: Open evalscript (JavaScript) library usable in EO Browser and the Process API
reliability_notes: Community-contributed scripts include SAR change detection, burn-severity (NBR/dNBR), moisture and urban-damage composites. Quality varies; scripts are visualisation aids, not validated damage classifiers.
description: Ready-made band-math recipes that turn raw Sentinel bands into damage- and burn-highlighting visualisations, e.g. making artillery burn scars and destroyed built-up blocks pop out over Donbas.

title: Sentinel Hub EO Browser
machine_readable: Backed by Sentinel Hub Process/Catalog/Statistical APIs (OGC WMS/WMTS + REST); free trial and Copernicus-funded free tier
reliability_notes: Best-in-class UI for band-math visual comparison (NDVI, SWIR burn indices, SAR RGB composites) over Sentinel-1/2/3, Landsat and MODIS. Free tier has processing-unit quotas; heavy API use is paid.
description: The tool most OSINT analysts use to make a visually convincing before/after or burn-index frame of a specific Ukrainian village or bridge, and to timestamp when a change first appeared.

title: SkyFi
machine_readable: REST API and mobile/web app for tasking and archive orders across multiple providers
reliability_notes: Broker/marketplace reselling optical (down to 15-30 cm) and SAR from many constellations without an enterprise contract; per-scene pricing from tens of dollars. Licence terms vary by upstream provider; some AOIs are restricted.
description: Makes it practical for an independent OSINT researcher or newsroom to buy a fresh sub-metre or SAR image of a specific Ukrainian frontline village within days, rather than waiting for free Sentinel passes.

title: SkyWatch EarthCache
machine_readable: EarthCache REST API for archive search and tasking across multiple providers
reliability_notes: Aggregator API abstracting Airbus, Planet, Satellogic and others; free developer sandbox credits, then pay per km2. Availability and licensing inherit from each upstream supplier.
description: A single API to search and order high-resolution imagery over Ukrainian coordinates from several constellations, useful for building an automated tasking workflow.

title: Spire Global (space-based AIS/ADS-B/RF)
machine_readable: Commercial REST/streaming APIs for maritime and aviation data; some free trials
reliability_notes: Global satellite AIS and ADS-B fills the gaps where terrestrial receivers cannot see, including the central Black Sea; paid subscription, with latency from minutes to hours depending on plan.
description: Satellite AIS/ADS-B coverage of the Black Sea reveals dark shipping, Russian naval movements and grain-corridor traffic in areas with no coastal receivers.

title: Starlink availability map
reliability_notes: Shows official service/availability status by area, not live per-terminal connectivity. Coverage policy in occupied Ukrainian territory has been a documented issue; the map reflects commercial availability decisions rather than observed outages.
description: Reference for where satellite connectivity is officially available, relevant because Starlink is the primary comms layer for Ukrainian units and reported service anomalies have coincided with operations.

title: Ukraine Damage Explorer (ETH Zurich / UZH / ICRC, Sentinel-1 deep learning)
machine_readable: Google Earth Engine app; source code on GitHub (prs-eth/ukraine-damage-mapping-tool, MIT) and result rasters/footprints on Zenodo (record 15088349)
reliability_notes: Deep-learning model over Sentinel-1 SAR time series trained on UNOSAT damage labels, producing per-pixel destruction probability and building-level damage at nationwide scale, published in Communications Earth and Environment (2025). Detects destroyed/severely damaged structures well, under-detects light damage; false positives in areas of construction or heavy vegetation change. Not continuously updated in real time.
description: A nationwide, weather-independent map of destroyed buildings across Ukraine that both confirms where heavy fighting occurred and, because destruction tracks the contact line, traces the frontline's historical path settlement by settlement.

title: Umbra Space Open Data
machine_readable: STAC catalogue + GeoTIFF/CPHD in public AWS bucket (registry.opendata.aws/umbra-open-data)
reliability_notes: Genuinely open (CC BY 4.0) sub-metre to 25 cm SAR spotlight imagery, including phase history data for advanced processing. Coverage is a curated set of interesting sites, not systematic; Ukraine appears occasionally rather than continuously.
description: One of very few sources of free, commercially-licensable very-high-resolution SAR, which sees through cloud and darkness, letting analysts confirm equipment presence and damage independent of weather.

title: UP42 geospatial marketplace
machine_readable: REST API and Python SDK for catalogue search, tasking and processing blocks
reliability_notes: Airbus-owned marketplace bundling optical and SAR archives with analytics blocks; free account for catalogue search, paid for delivery. Some sensors restricted by export controls over conflict areas.
description: Programmatic route to buy and process very-high-resolution and SAR imagery of Ukrainian areas of interest, including change-detection blocks that run server-side.

title: USGS EarthExplorer
machine_readable: Machine-to-Machine (M2M) REST API at m2m.cr.usgs.gov; bulk download application
reliability_notes: Landsat 8/9 at 30 m (15 m pan) with 8-16 day revisit, Sentinel-2 mirror, plus declassified historical Corona/Hexagon imagery of Soviet-era infrastructure. 30 m is coarse for tactical work but excellent for burn scars, flooding, reservoir levels and large industrial fires.
description: Landsat thermal (TIRS) and SWIR bands detect large fires and hot industrial targets, and the long archive plus declassified Cold War imagery supports reconstruction of pre-war baseline infrastructure.

title: USGS Earthquake FDSN event web service
reliability_notes: Global catalogue with automated and reviewed solutions; detection threshold over Ukraine is roughly M2.5-3.5 given station spacing, so only very large explosions (major ammunition depots, the Nord Stream blasts, dam-scale events) register. Locations for shallow explosions carry kilometre-scale uncertainty and are often initially mislabelled as earthquakes.
description: Seismic detections give an independent, timestamped, coordinate-bearing record of the very largest explosions in and around Ukraine, immune to any party's information operations.

title: USGS LandsatLook viewer
machine_readable: STAC API (landsatlook.usgs.gov/stac-server) and COG access on AWS
reliability_notes: Cloud-optimised Landsat Collection 2 access with quick visual comparison and time slider; no login for browsing. Same 30 m/16 day limits as Landsat.
description: Quick visual and thermal-band checks of large Ukrainian sites (refineries, power plants, reservoirs) with a STAC endpoint suitable for automation.

title: Vantor (formerly Maxar) Open Data Program
machine_readable: Open data releases as COGs with STAC catalogues; also mirrored at registry.opendata.aws/maxar-open-data
reliability_notes: 30-50 cm WorldView/GeoEye imagery released free under CC BY-NC 4.0 for selected crisis events. Ukraine coverage is event-driven and sparse rather than continuous; releases are curated, so absence of an event means no release, not no imagery.
description: When activated, gives the public genuinely tactical-resolution imagery (individual vehicles, revetments, crater fields, destroyed buildings) for a specific Ukrainian area and date.

title: Vantor (Maxar) News Bureau
machine_readable: None (press-release imagery with captions and coordinates)
reliability_notes: Curated, media-licensed 30-50 cm frames with dates and place names; the source of most widely republished satellite images of Ukrainian strike damage, convoys and airbases. Selection is editorial and heavily Western-media driven.
description: Provides the annotated high-resolution before/after frames of specific Ukrainian events (airbase strikes, destroyed bridges, mass graves, Black Sea Fleet losses) that anchor many public geolocation claims.

title: ACLED API (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data)
machine_readable: REST JSON/CSV/XLSX API: GET https://acleddata.com/api/acled/read with OAuth Bearer token obtained by POST to https://acleddata.com/oauth/token (myACLED username/password grant)
reliability_notes: Verified Aug 2026: acleddata.com/api/acled/read returns 403 without a token (endpoint live); the legacy api.acleddata.com host no longer resolves. Free for non-commercial/research use under ACLED Terms of Use with attribution; commercial use requires a licence. Each event carries geo_precision 1-3 - only precision 1 is settlement-accurate. Weekly Tuesday release, ~5-10 day lag.
description: The reference geocoded conflict-event dataset for Ukraine: battles, shelling, drone/missile strikes and civilian targeting with lat/lon, actor, fatality and source fields, from 2018 onward.

title: ACLED Ukraine conflict events on HDX (no API key)
machine_readable: XLSX resources via CKAN: https://data.humdata.org/api/3/action/package_show?id=ukraine-acled-conflict-data then fetch resource download URLs
reliability_notes: Verified 200; metadata_modified 2026-08-19, coverage 2018-01-01 to present. Licence shown as 'Other' (ACLED terms). Aggregated to admin1/admin2 by month-year - not point-level, but requires no ACLED account.
description: Free, key-free mirror of ACLED's Ukraine political-violence, civilian-targeting and demonstration counts aggregated to oblast/raion by month.

title: Cline Center SPEED (Social, Political and Economic Event Database)
machine_readable: Dataset downloads via Illinois Data Bank / Illinois Experts records (CSV, Stata)
reliability_notes: Verified 200 (note: the older /project/human-conflict/SPEED path is now 404). Human-coded civil unrest and repression events, historically 1946-2005/2009 - it does NOT cover the 2022+ war. Included only as a historical baseline; the Cline Center's Phoenix machine-coded series is the more current sibling.
description: Human-coded historical civil-unrest and political-violence event data; useful for long-run Ukraine baselines, not for current frontline tracking.

title: conflict-investigations/media-search-engine
machine_readable: Self-hostable search index over Bellingcat, Cen4InfoRes and similar geolocated media databases; ingests their JSON exports
reliability_notes: Verified 200; last pushed 2026-06-13 (recently maintained). Open-source. Depends on upstream databases' availability, several of which are now frozen.
description: Search geolocated social-media evidence across multiple OSINT incident databases at once - useful for resolving what happened at a given coordinate.

title: conflict-investigations/osint-geo-extractor
machine_readable: Python library (pip) that normalises Bellingcat, Cen4InfoRes, GeoConfirmed, Texty and DeepState sources into a common geo record schema
reliability_notes: Verified 200; last pushed 2024-01-20 so endpoint drift is likely (e.g. the GeoConfirmed collection naming). Open-source licence in repo. Read it as a schema-mapping reference even where the fetchers need patching.
description: Ready-made normalisation layer that maps several Ukraine OSINT incident databases onto one geo schema - a shortcut for an aggregator's ingest design.

title: EM-DAT public interface
machine_readable: Web query builder with XLSX export; free academic account required. Ukraine country profile also mirrored on HDX (emdat-country-profiles-ukr)
reliability_notes: Verified 200. CC BY 4.0 for non-commercial use after registration. EM-DAT records natural and technological disasters, not armed conflict - relevant to Ukraine only for dam/flood and industrial events (e.g. Kakhovka). Country-level granularity, monthly refresh.
description: Disaster-loss database useful for the non-combat destructive events (floods, dam failure, industrial accidents) that overlap the Ukrainian conflict record.

title: Europe VIIRS/MODIS active fire detections on HDX
machine_readable: CSV resources refreshed daily; discoverable via https://data.humdata.org/api/3/action/package_show?id=nasa-firms-active-fire-europe-viirs
reliability_notes: Verified via CKAN search (licence other-pd-nr i.e. public domain, no restrictions; open-ended coverage from 2012 for VIIRS and 2000 for MODIS). Pre-clipped to Europe so no bounding-box maths or API key needed - convenient but coarser update cadence than the FIRMS API.
description: Key-free daily CSV of VIIRS/MODIS fire detections over Europe including all of Ukraine - the simplest way to add a thermal-anomaly layer to an aggregator.

title: GADM 4.1 Ukraine boundaries
machine_readable: Direct file downloads: https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/json/gadm41_UKR_1.json.zip (also gpkg, shp, and levels 0-3)
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Free for academic and other non-commercial use only - redistribution and commercial use require permission, which matters for an aggregator. Boundary vintage predates Ukraine's 2020 raion reform in places, so names and raion counts will not match KATOTTG.
description: Long-standing global admin-boundary set, useful as a fallback or for cross-country comparability - but licence-restricted and administratively out of date for Ukraine.

title: GDELT 2.0 raw event/GKG files
machine_readable: CSV.zip files every 15 minutes; manifest at http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/lastupdate.txt, files at data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/{YYYYMMDDHHMMSS}.{export|mentions|gkg}.CSV.zip
reliability_notes: Verified 200 - lastupdate.txt served a 2026-08-19 19:30 UTC batch while testing. Free for non-commercial and most research use (see GDELT terms); BigQuery mirror also public. Geocoding is automated from news text, so precision is coarse and false positives are common - treat as a lead-generation firehose, not ground truth.
description: A 15-minute global news event and geo-mention firehose; the fastest machine-readable signal that something is being reported at a named Ukrainian place, with CAMEO codes and lat/lon.

title: GDELT DOC 2.0 API
machine_readable: REST JSON/CSV: GET https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query=...&mode=artlist&format=json (also mode=timelinevol, geo modes)
reliability_notes: Documented endpoint; live host verified but returned HTTP 429 on test calls - the service is aggressively rate-limited and has no key, so back off and cache. No SLA; article-level only.
description: Keyword/geo search over GDELT's rolling global news index - handy for pulling the source articles behind a place-name spike without downloading raw 15-minute files.

title: geoBoundaries API (Ukraine ADM0-ADM3)
machine_readable: REST JSON metadata + GeoJSON download links: https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/UKR/ADM3/
reliability_notes: Verified 200 with a real JSON response (UKR ADM3 'Village Councils', 2021 vintage, source OSM, CC BY-SA 2.0). gbOpen release is redistributable; gbAuthoritative/gbHumanitarian have stricter terms. ADM3 vintage is pre-KATOTTG in places, so reconcile against COD-AB.
description: Stable, versioned, programmatically fetchable Ukrainian admin polygons down to village-council level - convenient when you need consistent ADM3 geometry without a portal download.

title: GeoConfirmed Ukraine API
machine_readable: REST JSON/CSV, no auth. Spec at /openapi/v1.json (NOT /swagger/). GET /api/Placemark/{conflict}/geojson -> 59,359 dated Point features (2014-03-03..2026-08-19); GET /api/Map/export/{conflict}/csv -> 59,337 rows semicolon-delimited UTF-8 BOM with Date;Name;Faction;Origin;Latitude;Longitude;PlusCode;Description;Source;Geolocation;Equipment;Units;OrbatUnits;Id; GET /api/Placemark/detail/{id}; GET /api/Conflict lists 20 conflicts (Ukraine=UKR); POST /api/Placemark/filter for server-side paging.
reliability_notes: Volunteer-verified geolocations to building precision, each row carrying a source URL plus unit/ORBAT attribution - the richest machine-readable event feed found. CAVEAT: /api/placemark/Ukraine (lowercase, no suffix) returns only the icon taxonomy, not data. Coverage is event-driven, so absence of points is not absence of fighting.
description: Volunteer-verified, building-precision geolocations of war footage and incidents across Ukraine, current to within a day - the best free source for exact event coordinates.

title: Geofabrik OSM extracts for Ukraine
machine_readable: Daily .osm.pbf, .osm.bz2 and shapefile extracts, plus daily change files (.osc.gz) for incremental updates
reliability_notes: Verified 200. ODbL. Rebuilt daily with a full internal-difference update stream, so you can maintain a local Ukraine OSM mirror cheaply instead of hammering Overpass. Includes historical snapshots on request.
description: Bulk daily OpenStreetMap extracts covering all of Ukraine - the practical foundation for self-hosted geocoding and settlement matching at aggregator scale.

title: GeoNames gazetteer (Ukraine dump + API)
machine_readable: Bulk TSV: https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/UA.zip plus alternateNames.zip; REST JSON API at http://api.geonames.org/searchJSON?q=...&username=<user>
reliability_notes: Both verified 200 (API tested with the demo username, which is rate-capped - register a free account). CC BY 4.0. Daily-rebuilt dumps; feature codes distinguish populated places from admin divisions. Alternate-names table carries Cyrillic, Latin transliterations and historical names, which is exactly what disambiguating duplicate Ukrainian toponyms requires.
description: A licence-clean, download-once gazetteer of every Ukrainian populated place with coordinates, admin codes, population and multi-script alternate names.

title: HALO Trust Ukraine mine-action programme data
machine_readable: Programme reporting and Esri-hosted survey maps; task-level contamination data is shared with national authorities rather than published as open downloads
reliability_notes: Verified 200. HALO's Ukraine survey teams feed IMSMA and publish selected ArcGIS story maps; the underlying hazardous-area polygons are not openly licensed for download. Treat the public material as indicative, and mine.dsns.gov.ua / GICHD as the data route.
description: Largest non-governmental survey effort mapping Ukrainian hazardous areas; its public maps and reports indicate where post-combat contamination has been formally surveyed.

title: HDX HAPI - conflict events REST API
machine_readable: REST JSON: GET https://hapi.humdata.org/api/v2/coordination-context/conflict-events?location_code=UKR&app_identifier=<base64 name:email>; OpenAPI at /openapi.json; identifier mintable at /api/v2/encode_app_identifier
reliability_notes: Verified 200 with a self-generated base64 app_identifier (no approval needed). v0.9.14. Returns ACLED-sourced event/fatality counts by admin1/admin2 and event_type with reference periods. CC-BY per underlying HDX datasets. Admin-unit aggregates only - no coordinates.
description: OCHA's unified humanitarian API: a single well-documented endpoint for Ukraine conflict-event and fatality counts by raion, plus IDP, population and needs endpoints for the same admin codes.

title: HDX Ukraine crisis data catalogue + CKAN API
machine_readable: CKAN v3 REST API: https://data.humdata.org/api/3/action/package_search?fq=groups:ukr&rows=... and package_show?id=<dataset>; each resource exposes a direct download URL
reliability_notes: Verified 200; the Ukraine group held 244 datasets at test time with per-dataset licences visible in the API (mostly CC BY / CC BY-IGO / CC BY-SA). Fully key-free and paginated - the single best programmatic entry point for discovering new Ukraine datasets as they appear.
description: OCHA's Ukraine data catalogue with a plain CKAN API: admin boundaries, ACLED events, WHO health attacks, IDP figures, fire detections, port activity and damage assessments all discoverable and downloadable in one query pattern.

title: HOT OSM building footprints of Ukraine (HDX)
machine_readable: SHP / GeoPackage zips plus JSON metadata from the HOT raw-data API S3 bucket
reliability_notes: Verified via CKAN package_show (metadata_modified 2026-08-08); ODC-ODbL. Coverage reflects volunteer mapping effort - urban areas dense, rural frontline areas sparser. Regenerated on a rolling schedule from live OSM.
description: Every OSM-tagged building in Ukraine as ready-to-use vectors - the denominator layer for damage-assessment joins and for resolving strike reports to specific structures.

title: Insecurity Insight - explosive weapons and sector attack datasets (Ukraine)
machine_readable: XLSX/CSV dumps on HDX; sibling datasets include ukraine-data-on-attacks-on-aid-operations-education-health-and-protection, sind-safeguarding-healthcare-monthly-news-briefs-dataset, conflict-related-incidents-affecting-water-systems
reliability_notes: Verified 200; CC BY-SA, coverage running to 2026 and updated monthly. Media-and-partner-monitoring based, so it is an incident register rather than a census; records name settlements and oblasts, coordinates are inconsistent.
description: Monthly structured registers of explosive-weapon incidents affecting health, education, water and aid operations in Ukraine - good coverage of infrastructure strikes that ACLED codes only as generic shelling.

title: IOM DTM Ukraine displacement data (API + HDX mirror)
machine_readable: IOM DTM v3 REST API (subscription key from the DTM Developer Portal, documented at dtm.iom.int/data-and-analysis/dtm-api); CKAN CSV mirror on HDX
reliability_notes: HDX mirror verified 200; dtm.iom.int itself returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients so the API portal must be reached interactively. API exposes only non-sensitive IDP figures at country/admin1/admin2. Monthly-to-quarterly rounds, several weeks lag. Attribution to IOM required.
description: IDP and returnee counts by oblast and raion - a lagging but systematic indicator of which frontline districts are emptying or being repopulated.

title: NASA FIRMS active fire API
machine_readable: REST CSV: https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/area/csv/{MAP_KEY}/{source}/{area}/{dayRange}[/{date}] where area is west,south,east,north; sources include VIIRS_SNPP_NRT, VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT, MODIS_NRT
reliability_notes: API landing page verified 200; a bare csv/ path returns 400 as expected without a MAP_KEY (free self-service key). Public domain (NASA). ~3-hour NRT latency, 375 m VIIRS pixels, several passes daily. Thermal anomalies include agricultural burning and industrial heat, so filtering is essential - but shelling, strikes and burning vehicles show up.
description: Free near-real-time geolocated thermal anomalies over Ukraine - an independent, non-OSINT signal of where intense fighting and fires are occurring, on a several-hour cadence.

title: Nominatim geocoding API
reliability_notes: Verified 200 with a live query. ODbL data; the public instance's usage policy caps you at ~1 request/second with a required identifying User-Agent and forbids bulk geocoding - self-host or use a commercial mirror for aggregator-scale volumes.
description: Turns Ukrainian place names from Telegram and press reports into coordinates and admin hierarchy; the default free geocoder for OSM-based pipelines.

title: OpenStreetMap Overpass API
machine_readable: Overpass QL over HTTP POST/GET to https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter (JSON or XML out); mirrors at kumi.systems and overpass.private.coffee
reliability_notes: Verified with a live Overpass QL POST returning valid JSON (timestamp_osm_base 2026-08-19). ODbL - share-alike attribution obligations apply to derived databases. Public instances are rate-limited/quota'd; run your own for bulk work. HEAD requests return 406, so probe with a real query.
description: Query any Ukrainian settlement, road, bridge, railway or building by name/tag and get its geometry - including name:uk, name:ru and old_name tags that make transliteration and renaming matches tractable.

title: ReliefWeb API v2
reliability_notes: Verified Aug 2026: v1 is retired (HTTP 410) and v2 rejects unregistered appnames with HTTP 403 pointing to apidoc.reliefweb.int/parameters#appname - you must request an approved appname. Free, no cost. Full-text situation reports, not coordinates.
description: Machine-readable index of every UN/NGO Ukraine situation report and humanitarian snapshot - the text layer behind oblast-level incident and displacement claims.

title: tak-feeder-deepstate (sgofferj)
machine_readable: Code: polls DeepStateMap API, emits CoT to a TAK server
reliability_notes: Integration glue, not a data source; documents the DeepStateMap API contract in code.
description: Feeder that pulls deepstatemap.live data and pushes it into a TAK (Team Awareness Kit) server; a concrete working example of consuming the DeepState API.

title: UCDP Candidate Events Dataset (monthly, ~1 month lag)
machine_readable: Monthly CSV/XLSX candidate-GED dumps; codebook at ucdp.uu.se/downloads/candidateged/ucdp-candidate-codebook1.3.pdf
reliability_notes: Verified 200. CC BY 4.0. Same coding as GED but released monthly with under a month's lag; events may be revised or dropped in the annual GED. Useful when GED's annual cadence is too slow.
description: Near-current monthly instalments of UCDP GED, keeping the georeferenced fatal-event series within about a month of real time.

title: UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED) download centre
machine_readable: Bulk CSV / XLSX / Stata / R dumps per dataset version; Ukraine filtered by country id 369
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Free under CC BY 4.0 with citation. Strictest verification standard of the event datasets (only incidents with >=1 confirmed direct death, conservative sourcing), so it systematically undercounts Ukraine relative to ACLED. Annual GED release plus monthly Candidate releases; where_prec field flags coordinate quality.
description: Uppsala's academically peer-reviewed geocoded lethal-violence events - the highest-precision, lowest-recall point dataset for cross-validating other Ukraine event feeds.

title: Ukraine subnational administrative boundaries (OCHA COD-AB) on HDX
machine_readable: GeoJSON / SHP / Geodatabase / XLSX downloads; discoverable via https://data.humdata.org/api/3/action/package_show?id=cod-ab-ukr
reliability_notes: Verified 200; metadata_modified 2026-08-14, boundary vintage Sept 2025, sourced from SSPE Kartographia via OCHA FISS. CC BY-IGO. Carries the official post-2020 KATOTTG hromada/raion codes, so it is the join key for almost every UN/NGO Ukraine dataset.
description: The authoritative, licence-clean oblast/raion/hromada polygon set with official codes - the base layer for aggregating any point-level event feed to Ukrainian admin units.

title: UNESCO monitoring of damaged cultural sites in Ukraine
machine_readable: Verified-site counts and lists published as HTML/PDF by oblast and heritage category; no public API or bulk geodata
reliability_notes: Verified 200 (the /en/articles/damaged-cultural-sites... path blocks non-browser clients with 403). UNESCO verifies each site before listing, so figures are a conservative floor and lag by weeks. Oblast and site-name granularity only - you must geocode names yourself.
description: Officially verified inventory of damaged Ukrainian religious buildings, museums, monuments and libraries by oblast - a distinct damage stratum absent from most conflict datasets.

title: UNOSAT / UNITAR Ukraine damage assessments
machine_readable: Per-product PDF maps plus shapefile/geodatabase exports; many products also mirrored as HDX datasets with SHP/CSV resources (searchable via the HDX CKAN API)
reliability_notes: Verified 200 (country filter also 200). Free with UNITAR/UNOSAT attribution. Analyst-reviewed manual vector digitisation of damaged structures - very high precision, but city-by-city and event-driven with weeks of lag; HDX mirrors are the machine-readable route (e.g. Mariupol, Kharkiv, Sumy, Kremenchuk, Kherson, Nova Kakhovka assessments).
description: UN satellite-imagery damage analyses giving per-building damage points/polygons for specific Ukrainian cities - the reference standard for verified destruction geometry.

title: WHO Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care - Ukraine
machine_readable: CSV resource (Google-Sheets-published CSV) plus methodological note PDF; discoverable via https://data.humdata.org/api/3/action/package_show?id=ukraine-who-ssa
reliability_notes: Verified via CKAN: CC BY licence, metadata_modified 2026-08-18, coverage from 2022-02-24 with no end date (ongoing). WHO applies a formal verification standard, so counts are conservative and lag incidents by days to weeks. Attack records carry admin unit and facility type rather than precise coordinates. Live dashboard at extranet.who.int/ssa (verified 200).
description: Systematically verified attacks on Ukrainian health facilities, transport and personnel with dates, oblasts and impact types - a high-credibility proxy for where strikes are landing on populated areas.

title: Wikidata SPARQL query service
machine_readable: SPARQL over HTTP: GET/POST https://query.wikidata.org/sparql with Accept: application/sparql-results+json
reliability_notes: Verified 200 with a live SPARQL query returning JSON bindings. CC0 data. Requires a descriptive User-Agent; queries time out at 60 s so paginate. Coverage of small Ukrainian villages is uneven and KATOTTG/KOATUU properties are not universally populated.
description: Query Ukrainian settlements by admin parent, coordinates, KATOTTG/KOATUU code, historical and Russian-language names, and renaming events - the best single source for linking a reported toponym to a stable identifier.

title: Wikipedia: List of Ukrainian place names affected by decommunization
machine_readable: Wikitables parseable via the MediaWiki API (action=parse / action=query&prop=revisions) or Wikidata SPARQL for the same rename events
reliability_notes: Verified 200. CC BY-SA. Community-maintained and incomplete relative to the ~1,000 settlements and 51,000+ toponyms renamed since 2014 (and the further wave of derussification renames after 2022), but it is the only consolidated free old-name/new-name table in English. Cross-check against Wikidata and OSM old_name tags.
description: Old-name to new-name pairs for renamed Ukrainian settlements - directly addresses the matching failures caused by decommunization and derussification when older sources use pre-rename toponyms.

title: Lostarmour.info (Russian-side loss and strike catalogue)
machine_readable: No public data API (probed /api paths -> 404; only a third-party comments API is exposed). Server-rendered catalogue pages plus /map and /map_la interactive loss maps; scraping required
reliability_notes: Verified 200 for /, /map, /map_la, /armour, /articles. Russian-perspective mirror-image of Oryx: catalogues claimed Ukrainian equipment, vehicle, artillery, aviation and personnel losses with photo evidence, plus dedicated Kursk and Kharkiv sections. Partisan sourcing - treat as claims requiring cross-checking; no licence, expect anti-bot friction.
description: Essential counterpart for Ukrainian-side attrition claims with an accompanying loss map; the only large structured Russian-perspective equipment catalogue.

title: Mediazona / BBC Russian confirmed Russian military deaths
machine_readable: No official API or CSV release; figures published as regularly updated articles with embedded charts, so extraction requires scraping the article or its chart payloads
reliability_notes: Verified: the canonical /casualties_eng URL redirects to the current instalment (2026-08-14 at test time), so it self-updates. Names confirmed from obituaries, local media and official statements jointly with BBC News Russian; the authors state it is a floor, not a total (~233k named by mid-2026). No public repo despite the mediazona GitHub org existing.
description: The most rigorous named-death count for the Russian side, broken down by region and time - a demand-side indicator of offensive intensity rather than a geolocated event feed.

title: cyterat/deepstate-map-data (daily DeepState GeoJSON archive)
machine_readable: GeoJSON files per date in /data plus consolidated deepstate-map-data.geojson.gz; raw download via raw.githubusercontent.com
reliability_notes: Verified 200 and last commit 2026-08-19 03:45 UTC - GitHub Action runs daily at 03:00 UTC. MIT-style repo LICENSE covers code; underlying geometry is DeepState's. Ready-made archive avoids hitting the DeepState API for history.
description: Occupied-territory MultiPolygon GeoJSON snapshots of DeepStateMap, one file per day, plus a single gzipped file holding all historical geometries with their dates.

title: data.gov.ua open data portal (CKAN)
machine_readable: CKAN v3 REST API: https://data.gov.ua/api/3/action/package_search?q=... and package_show; resources as CSV/XLSX/JSON
reliability_notes: Verified 200 for both the portal and a live CKAN query. Ukrainian government open data under the national open-data terms. Wartime publication of security-relevant registers has been curtailed and many datasets are stale or withdrawn; Ukrainian-language metadata only.
description: Ukraine's national open-data portal with a standard CKAN API - the source for official administrative registers, the KATOTTG codifier and infrastructure inventories used to resolve place names.

title: deepstate-map-data-analytics (lazar-bit)
reliability_notes: Analysis code rather than a maintained feed; verify freshness before relying on it.
description: Analytics layer over DeepStateMap data computing occupied-area change over time; useful reference for turning polygons into territorial-change metrics.

title: DeepStateMap.Live public history API
machine_readable: REST JSON: GET /api/history/public returns every historical snapshot id + timestamp + change description; GET /api/history/{id}/geojson returns that snapshot's control polygons; GET /api/history/last returns current FeatureCollection
reliability_notes: Verified Aug 2026: /api/history/public (200, full snapshot index back to 2022-04-03), /api/history/last (200, GeoJSON FeatureCollection), /api/history/{id}/geojson (200). Bare /api/history returns 401. No documented licence - site terms only; heavy scraping discouraged. Ukrainian-perspective assessment, updated several times per day, ~hours lag behind Telegram claims.
description: The single most valuable free frontline-geometry time series: a queryable archive of every DeepState map snapshot since April 2022 as GeoJSON control polygons, plus a change note per snapshot.

title: Kaggle: Massive Missile Attacks on Ukraine (piterfm)
machine_readable: CSV dumps via Kaggle dataset API (kaggle datasets download -d piterfm/massive-missile-attacks-on-ukraine) or browser download
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Requires a free Kaggle account for API/download. Compiled from Ukrainian Air Force daily reports - launch/target descriptions are textual place and oblast names rather than coordinates, and shot-down figures are Ukrainian claims. Frequent updates by the same maintainer as the General Staff losses repo.
description: Per-attack records of missile and Shahed strike waves (model, launched, destroyed, launch place, target region) - the best structured series for strike-wave geography at oblast level.

title: KATOTTG / KOATUU administrative code reference (Zenodo)
machine_readable: CSV download (katottg.csv, ~32k hierarchical records) via the Zenodo record and REST API at https://zenodo.org/api/records/18863103
reliability_notes: Zenodo record and API verified reachable (Zenodo returns 403 to bare curl HEAD but serves normally to browsers/WebFetch). DOI-citable with an open CC licence. Contains both the legacy KOATUU codes and the current KATOTTG codes with hierarchy - the crosswalk you need because older Ukrainian datasets use KOATUU and newer ones use KATOTTG.
description: A frozen, citable dump of Ukraine's administrative-territorial codifier including the KOATUU-to-KATOTTG mapping - the key to joining pre- and post-2020 Ukrainian administrative data.

title: KSE Institute - Russia Will Pay / Damages assessment
machine_readable: Periodic PDF/XLSX damage reports with oblast-level and sector-level tables; no public API
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Run with Ukraine's Ministry of Economy, Ministry for Development of Communities and Territories and the NBU using World Bank RDNA methodology; latest published figure $197.5bn direct damage as of Feb 2026 (released Aug 2026). Semi-annual cadence, so months of lag; aggregate monetary values by sector/oblast rather than per-object geometry.
description: The authoritative monetary damage assessment for Ukrainian civilian infrastructure by oblast and sector - the economic layer over the geospatial damage record.

title: mine.dsns.gov.ua - Ukrainian interactive map of mine-contaminated territories
machine_readable: Interactive web map (no public JSON/API endpoint discoverable in the page source); contamination polygons served to the client only
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Operated by Ukraine's State Emergency Service and fed from the GICHD-built IMSMA national mine-action database. Official but deliberately generalised for public release; occupied and active-combat areas are unsurveyed by definition, so absence of contamination is not evidence of safety.
description: Official Ukrainian mine and explosive-ordnance contamination mapping - the best public indicator of where the fighting has been, since contamination polygons trace former frontlines.

title: PetroIvaniuk/2022-Ukraine-Russia-War-Dataset (Ukrainian General Staff daily losses)
machine_readable: JSON dumps: data/russia_losses_equipment.json, russia_losses_personnel.json, russia_losses_equipment_oryx.json, plus a corrections file
reliability_notes: Verified 200; last commit 2026-08-19 (updated daily). Mirrors the Ukrainian General Staff's official daily claims, which are unverified belligerent figures - useful as a claim series, not as ground truth, and explicitly contrasted with the Oryx column in the same repo. Repo carries an open licence.
description: Machine-readable daily Ukrainian General Staff claimed Russian personnel and equipment losses since 24 Feb 2022, aligned side-by-side with Oryx visual confirmations.

title: saveschools.in.ua (education infrastructure damage)
machine_readable: Web dashboard with oblast and institution-level damage counts; no documented public API or CSV export found
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Ukrainian Ministry of Education-linked monitoring of damaged and destroyed educational institutions. Official Ukrainian figures - authoritative for the Ukrainian-controlled area, with no coverage of occupied territory. Extraction requires scraping.
description: Running national tally of damaged and destroyed Ukrainian schools and universities by region - a dense, geographically spread indicator of strike impact on civilian areas.

title: testapiw/kodifikator (KATOTTG parser/importer)
machine_readable: Python tooling that downloads and parses the official Minregion KATOTTG spreadsheet into a relational/CSV structure
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Open-source. Useful because the official source (minregion.gov.ua) blocks non-browser clients (HTTP 403 observed), so a maintained scraper is the practical path to the current codifier.
description: Keeps the official Ukrainian administrative codifier ingestible: automates fetching and parsing KATOTTG so settlement codes stay current as hromadas change.

title: UALosses (named Ukrainian military dead and missing)
machine_readable: No public API or bulk export found (tested /api/, /en/api/soldiers/ -> 404); paginated HTML tables with per-soldier detail pages, so scraping is required
reliability_notes: Verified 200 (root redirects to /en/soldiers/). Built from obituaries, social media and official records by OSINT volunteers; over 90k named Ukrainian dead recorded as of 2026. Coverage is a lower bound and per-record locations are home/burial oblasts, not death locations. No stated open licence - scrape politely.
description: The largest named-casualty register for the Ukrainian side; useful for regional loss intensity over time but not for pinpointing where fighting occurred.

title: WarSpotting API (documented Russian equipment losses)
machine_readable: REST JSON, no auth (verified 2026-08-19): /api/losses/{russia|ukraine}/recent/ returns 100 items; /api/losses/russia/<YYYY-MM-DD>/[status]/; /api/losses/russia/<limit>/; /api/stats/russia/. Item fields: id,type,model,status,lost_by,date,nearest_location,geo("lat,lon"),unit,tags.
reliability_notes: Photo-verified losses with real coordinates, but per-date results backfill with a lag (2026-08-15 returned 0 while /recent/ held 2026-08-19 items), so poll /recent/ AND re-poll past dates. Docs page is 200 to curl, 403 to headless fetchers. Russian-side coverage is far more complete than Ukrainian.
description: Photo-verified Russian equipment losses with per-item status and, where determined, coordinates and nearest settlement - the cleanest free JSON API for point-geolocated attrition.

title: Bellingcat Civilian Harm in Ukraine (TimeMap) dataset
machine_readable: JSON dump: https://bellingcat-embeds.ams3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/production/ukr/timemap/api.json (also CSV/JSON export buttons in the UI)
reliability_notes: Verified 200, 1.1 MB, 2517 incidents spanning 2022-02-24 to 2025-07-09 - i.e. the dataset has stopped being extended and is effectively archived as of Aug 2026. Each record has lat/lon, date, description, impact type, weapon system and source URLs, all researcher-verified. Bellingcat licence terms require attribution.
description: A closed but high-quality corpus of ~2.5k verified civilian-harm incidents with coordinates, impact category and source links - excellent training/validation data even though it no longer updates.

title: Centre for Information Resilience Russia-Ukraine Monitor Map
machine_readable: MapHub-hosted point layer; MapHub offers GeoJSON/KML export of public maps (no documented dedicated API)
reliability_notes: Verified 200. Volunteer-verified, geolocated incident points with source links, curated by CIR. Update cadence has slowed markedly since 2023; treat as a large historical archive. Attribution to CIR required.
description: Thousands of verified, source-linked geolocated incidents from the CIR monitor map - a strong historical complement to GeoConfirmed.

title: conflict-investigations/nzz-maps (NZZ territorial control archive)
machine_readable: Raw CSV + per-day JSON geometry from GitHub, no auth (verified 2026-08-19): territory.csv has 1,638 daily "date,area" rows 2022-02-24..2026-08-19. Default branch is master, not main.
reliability_notes: Verified 200; territory.csv current through 2026-08-19 and /data holds daily JSON from 2022-02-24 onward (2000+ files). Scrapes Neue Zuercher Zeitung's war map; derived data so NZZ copyright applies to the geometry. Note default branch is master, not main.
description: A second independent daily frontline-geometry time series (from NZZ's cartography) plus a clean daily occupied-area km2 series - useful as a cross-check against DeepState.

title: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (Sentinel-1/2 archive and APIs)
machine_readable: OData and STAC catalogue APIs plus Sentinel Hub OGC/Process APIs and an S3 archive; browser UI at dataspace.copernicus.eu/browser/
reliability_notes: Verified 200 (browser UI also 200). Free registration; Copernicus open data licence with attribution, generous but quota'd processing units. Sentinel-1 SAR gives all-weather revisit useful for damage/coherence work; Sentinel-2 optical is cloud-dependent. Ukraine Sentinel-1 acquisition coverage has varied over the war.
description: The primary free source of the satellite imagery underlying independent damage and frontline analysis, with catalogue APIs suitable for automated Ukraine AOI monitoring.

title: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping API and activations
machine_readable: REST JSON: https://rapidmapping.emergency.copernicus.eu/backend/dashboard-api/public-activations-info/ (paginated list) and .../public-activations/?code=EMSRxxx; vector products (grading/delineation) downloadable per AOI
reliability_notes: Both endpoints verified 200 Aug 2026 - the list endpoint returned 257 activations with codes, centroids, categories and lastUpdate timestamps (freshest entry 2026-08-19). Free and open under Copernicus data policy with attribution. Activation-driven, so Ukraine coverage is episodic (specific cities/events) rather than continuous.
description: Machine-readable index of every EU rapid-mapping activation with downloadable damage-grading and flood-delineation vectors - authoritative satellite-derived damage polygons for specific Ukrainian events.

title: ETH Zurich Sentinel-1 war-destruction dataset for Ukraine (Zenodo)
machine_readable: Zenodo downloads: buildings_preds.parquet (4.8 GB), n_buildings_damaged_adm3_t0_655.geojson, ukraine_final_preds_22_23_masked.tif, unosat_aois.geojson, unosat_labels.geojson; REST metadata at https://zenodo.org/api/records/15088349
reliability_notes: Verified via WebFetch (Zenodo blocks bare curl HEAD with 403). CC BY 4.0, v2 published 2025-03-19, accompanying paper in Nature Communications Earth & Environment. Covers Feb 2022 - Feb 2024 only; predictions are model output validated against UNOSAT labels, not ground truth. Archived, not updated.
description: Nationwide, model-inferred building-damage predictions from Sentinel-1 InSAR coherence, aggregated to ADM3 and per-building - the only free country-wide damage layer for Ukraine's first two war years.

title: ISW / CTP 'Assessed Control of Terrain in Ukraine' ArcGIS FeatureServer
machine_readable: ArcGIS REST, no auth (verified 2026-08-19): base ?f=json enumerates 324 services; append /query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&returnGeometry=true&f=geojson. Supports resultRecordCount/resultOffset paging, geometry filters, f=geojson|json|pbf.
handle_or_feed: VIEW_RussiaCoTinUkraine_V3/FeatureServer/49 (Polygon, has EditDate for diffing); Assessed_Russian_Gains_in_the_Past_24_Hours_view/FeatureServer/0 (Polygon); RUAF_Field_Fortifications_Polylines/FeatureServer/0 (LineString); also VIEW_ClaimedRussianTerritoryinUkraine_V2, AssessedRussianAdvanceInUkraine_V2_view, Claimed_Limit_of_Ukrainian_Advance_VIEW.
reliability_notes: Verified 200, ~2.1 MB GeoJSON, fields include EditDate. Publicly readable with no key; ISW asks for attribution and its maps are for non-commercial reference. Layer URLs are discoverable from ArcGIS webmap item 9f04944a2fe84edab9da31750c2b15eb - note ISW renames services occasionally (the old Ukraine_Front_Line_NEW service is gone).
description: ISW/AEI Critical Threats assessed Russian-controlled area polygons, refreshed daily - the canonical Western frontline assessment in queryable GeoJSON form.

title: ISW / CTP companion ArcGIS layers (24h gains, advances, infiltration, fortifications, settlements)
machine_readable: ArcGIS REST FeatureServers under services5.arcgis.com/SaBe5HMtmnbqSWlu; each layer supports /query?where=1=1&f=geojson. Layer list obtainable from arcgis.com/sharing/rest/content/items/9f04944a2fe84edab9da31750c2b15eb/data?f=json
reliability_notes: Verified 200 for the 24h-gains layer and for Ukrainian_Settlements_Updated_view (29,655 features). ~24 named operational layers including Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas, Claimed Ukrainian Counteroffensives, Russian Field Fortifications (incl. Nathan Ruser/ASPI lines), Kakhovka flood extent. ISW attribution required; service names change without notice.
description: The rest of ISW's daily map stack as machine-readable layers: last-24h gains, claimed advances, infiltration areas, fortification lines, and a 29.6k-feature Ukrainian settlement-boundary polygon layer for name-to-polygon matching.

title: leedrake5/Russia-Ukraine (Oryx + Naalsio geolocated losses + FIRMS archive)
machine_readable: CSV dumps in /data: Naalsio/{avdiivka,kharkiv,krynky,kursk,zaporizhizhia}.csv (Andrew Perpetua's geolocated equipment losses), FIRMS/{YYYY-MM-DD}.csv daily fire detections from 2022-02-23, plus bySystem/ and byType/ Oryx series
reliability_notes: Verified 200; last commit 2026-08-19 (actively maintained). Bundles Andrew Perpetua's (Naalsio26) per-battle geolocated loss spreadsheets, which are otherwise scattered across Google Sheets, and a complete daily NASA FIRMS archive for Ukraine. Repo LICENSE covers the code; source data retains its own terms.
description: The most convenient single repo for geolocated equipment losses by battle plus a pre-downloaded daily thermal-anomaly archive - both directly usable to place events on the map.

title: MilitaryLand.net deployment and frontline maps
machine_readable: Interactive web maps (unit deployments, frontline) with no documented public API or export; underlying layers are not published as downloadable geodata
reliability_notes: Verified 200; no JSON/GeoJSON endpoints found in the page source. Detailed order-of-battle mapping of Ukrainian and Russian units by sector, maintained daily; some content and map detail sit behind supporter tiers. Unit placements are OSINT inference, not confirmed positions.
description: The most granular free unit-deployment mapping for the Ukrainian front - valuable for attributing an event location to a sector and formation, though it must be read visually rather than ingested.

title: Oryx - Attack On Europe: Documenting Russian Equipment Losses
machine_readable: No API: a single very large HTML page (23k+ anchor tags) of per-item links to image evidence; requires scraping or use of a third-party CSV mirror
reliability_notes: Verified 200. The de facto citation standard for visually confirmed attrition, but deliberately conservative (visual proof only) and NOT geolocated - entries carry no coordinates. Update cadence has become irregular. No explicit licence; attribution expected. Companion Ukrainian-losses page exists separately.
description: The benchmark visually-confirmed equipment-loss tally for both sides; valuable as a denominator for loss analytics, but it must be joined to WarSpotting/Naalsio data to obtain locations.

title: scarnecchia/oryx_data (Oryx parsed to CSV)
machine_readable: CSV dumps: daily_count.csv, totals_by_system.csv, totals_by_type.csv, event_{destroyed,damaged,captured,abandoned}.csv via raw.githubusercontent.com
reliability_notes: Verified 200 but last commit 2025-08-21 - effectively stale as of Aug 2026, so use for historical series only. MIT/CC licence in repo; underlying counts are Oryx's. No coordinates.
description: Tidy CSV time series of the Oryx tallies (daily counts, per-system totals, per-event status) - saves scraping the HTML, but frozen in Aug 2025.

title: simonhuwiler/russo-ukrainian-data-ressources (catalogue of war data sources)
machine_readable: Curated markdown catalogue in a Git repo, listing dataset URLs, formats and update cadence
reliability_notes: Verified 200; last commit 2026-07-10, so reasonably current. Maintained by an NZZ data journalist. A meta-resource, not data itself - links do rot, so re-verify before ingesting anything from it.
description: A maintained index of Russo-Ukrainian war data sources with notes on formats and access - the fastest way to discover feeds not covered elsewhere in this catalogue.

title: Carnegie Politika (Carnegie Endowment - Russia/Eurasia)
reliability_notes: Written substantially by exiled Russian analysts, so it is unusually good on Russian decision-making but deliberately does not do tactical mapping.
description: Explains the Russian political and military-industrial drivers behind offensive pushes. Context layer rather than a locator, but essential for interpreting why particular axes are prioritised.

title: ETH Zurich Center for Security Studies (CSS Analyses)
reliability_notes: Swiss academic neutrality is a strength for balance but the publication cycle is far slower than the frontline.
description: Short analytical briefs on the war's military-technological dynamics; also runs the ISN resource collection useful for background sourcing.

title: IISS - Strategic Comments and Military Balance Ukraine coverage
reliability_notes: Authoritative order-of-battle and force-strength data but much of the Military Balance is paywalled and its cadence is far slower than the frontline changes.
