description: Provides the force-structure and attrition baseline (units, equipment holdings) that frontline assessments depend on, plus periodic operational commentary on Ukrainian and Russian offensives.

title: CAST - Center for Analysis of Strategies and Technologies (Moscow)
reliability_notes: Moscow-based defence-industry-linked think tank operating under Russian wartime censorship; treat all claims as reflecting a Russian institutional line, though its arms-transfer data has historically been credible.
description: Russian-perspective analysis of the war, Russian defence production and equipment; valuable specifically as a counter-perspective input when cross-checking Western frontline claims.

title: RIAC - Russian International Affairs Council
reliability_notes: State-founded Russian body; content is constrained by Russian law on war reporting and functions partly as external messaging.
description: Russian institutional commentary on the war and its diplomacy. Use only as a perspective sample - it does not provide independently verifiable positional information.

title: Centre for Defence Strategies (Ukraine) - Daily Brief
reliability_notes: Ukrainian think tank staffed by former defence officials; the operational section largely restates Ukrainian General Staff reporting, so Ukrainian framing should be assumed.
description: A daily English-language brief listing fighting by operational direction with named settlements, plus political and economic sections. One of the few structured Ukrainian daily texts.

title: Come Back Alive Foundation - analytics
reliability_notes: A fundraising foundation supplying Ukrainian forces, so its analytical output is advocacy-adjacent and not an independent assessment.
description: Publishes analytical explainers and situation digests on Ukrainian defence needs and frontline dynamics; context and equipment-attrition insight rather than positional data.

title: National Institute for Strategic Studies (NISS, Ukraine)
reliability_notes: Reports to the Ukrainian President's Office, so it is an official-perspective institution and should be read as Ukrainian state analysis.
description: Ukrainian state strategic research institute publishing assessments of the war's military and security dimensions; valuable as authoritative Ukrainian framing of frontline developments.

title: Ukrainian Institute for the Future
reliability_notes: Independent Ukrainian think tank with mixed private funding; military analysis is a secondary line of work alongside economics and much content is Ukrainian-only.
description: Ukrainian analytical commentary on the war including periodic military-political forecasts. Useful as domestic Ukrainian expert opinion on frontline trajectory.

title: Atlantic Council - UkraineAlert
reliability_notes: High volume, commentary-driven and openly pro-Ukraine advocacy; individual posts vary widely in analytic rigour and are not independently verified.
description: Fast-turnaround commentary on frontline and strike developments with frequent Ukrainian-authored pieces. Good for narrative and reaction, weak as a positional source.

title: Black Bird Group (Finland)
reliability_notes: Small Finnish analyst team (Kastehelmi et al.) that publishes its geolocation reasoning; cadence dropped to irregular long-form pieces and there is no RSS.
description: Situation updates and axis assessments on the Ukraine war built from geolocated footage and satellite imagery, notable for measured square-kilometre gain estimates and clear map graphics.

title: CEPA (Center for European Policy Analysis)
reliability_notes: Transatlantic-advocacy think tank with government and defence-industry funding; commentary format, no independent verification.
description: High-frequency short analyses on Russia's war, drone and strike campaigns, and Ukrainian resilience. Interpretive layer around the frontline rather than a locator.

title: Chatham House - Russia's war on Ukraine
reliability_notes: Strong Ukraine Forum network of Ukrainian experts; output is strategic/policy rather than operational, and it does no independent geolocation.
description: Tracks the geopolitical and negotiation dimension of the war alongside periodic military assessments. Useful for interpreting frontline events politically, not for coordinates.

title: CNA Russia Studies Program
reliability_notes: US federally funded research centre; reports are rigorous and heavily sourced to Russian-language military literature but slow and rarely map-based.
description: Translates and analyses Russian military thinking and lessons-learned from Ukraine, including how UAV saturation shapes the character of the contact line.

title: Critical Threats Project (AEI) - Russia-Ukraine crisis coverage
reliability_notes: CTP co-authors the ROCA with ISW, so its Ukraine output largely duplicates ISW's; AEI's policy-advocacy orientation is openly hawkish.
description: AEI's co-publication hub for the daily ISW/CTP campaign assessments plus its own Iran/Russia interaction analysis. Duplicate of ISW text but a second, independently reachable mirror if ISW is down.

title: CSIS - Ukraine programme and conflict monitoring
reliability_notes: US government-adjacent funding; strong on quantified rate-of-advance analysis (Jones/Futures Lab) but occasional data products lag and methodology annexes are sparse.
description: Publishes quantitative assessments of Russian monthly territorial gains in square kilometres per casualty, plus geospatial briefs, giving a numeric check on qualitative frontline narratives.

title: DFRLab (Digital Forensic Research Lab)
reliability_notes: Publishes method sections and archives its evidence, but Atlantic Council funding gives it a Western policy orientation and it prioritises information-operations over kinetic mapping.
description: Combines OSINT verification with think-tank publishing: geolocates strike footage, satellite-verifies damage, and documents Russian information operations around frontline claims.

title: ECFR - Ukraine coverage
reliability_notes: Pan-European advocacy think tank; commentary-driven, EU-policy focused, no independent verification.
description: Commentary and polling-based research on European support for Ukraine and negotiation scenarios that shape frontline expectations.

title: FIIA - Finnish Institute of International Affairs
reliability_notes: Parliament-funded Finnish institute; strong Russia expertise, low frequency, no tactical detail.
description: Briefing papers on Russian strategy and the war's trajectory, with Nordic-Baltic threat-perception framing.

title: FOI - Swedish Defence Research Agency, Russia and Eurasia (RUFS)
reliability_notes: Commissioned by the Swedish Ministry of Defence; methodologically explicit multi-year capability assessments but very low publication frequency and no operational tracking. Site was unreachable from some networks during checking.
description: Produces landmark reports on Russian military capability at war and force regeneration, providing the analytic baseline for judging whether Russia can sustain offensive pressure.

title: FPRI - Eurasia Program (BEAR Network)
reliability_notes: Hosts named military analysts (Kofman, Muzyka contributions) whose individual reliability is high; institutional output is irregular and essay-form.
description: Analytical essays on Russian and Ukrainian force generation, drone warfare and offensive potential, frequently the venue where leading frontline analysts publish long-form assessments.

title: ICDS - International Centre for Defence and Security (Estonia)
reliability_notes: Estonian defence-ministry-supported institute; frontline-region expertise is strong but output is commentary and it does not geolocate.
description: Baltic-perspective analyses of Russian operations, force posture and the implications of frontline changes for NATO's eastern flank.

title: IFRI - French Institute of International Relations (Russia/Eurasia Center)
reliability_notes: Independent French institute; its Russie.Nei.Visions series is well regarded but Ukraine military output is occasional and long-form.
description: Publishes detailed studies of Russian military adaptation and the war's operational lessons, including French-language analysis not available elsewhere.

title: Institute for the Study of War - Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment (ROCA)
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML only - NO RSS exists (verified: /feed/ and /?feed=rss2 return 200 but redirect to homepage with 0 items; /rss.xml 403; /publications/feed/ 404). Use the ArcGIS layers for machine-readable geometry.
reliability_notes: Compiles geolocated social-media and Russian/Ukrainian MoD claims into an explicitly caveated assessed-control narrative; US-centric framing, historically cautious about confirming Russian advances, and each claim is labelled by confidence level.
description: The single most-cited daily text assessment of the Ukraine front, naming specific settlements where Russian or Ukrainian forces advanced in the past 24 hours. The narrative accompanies ISW's control-of-terrain maps and cites the underlying geolocated footage.

title: ISW Russia and Ukraine campaign assessment archive
machine_readable: Scrapeable HTML only - NO RSS exists (verified: /feed/ and /?feed=rss2 return 200 but redirect to homepage with 0 items; /rss.xml 403; /publications/feed/ 404). Use the ArcGIS layers for machine-readable geometry.
reliability_notes: Same methodology as the daily ROCA; the archive is complete back to Feb 2022 which makes it usable as a longitudinal corpus of assessed control changes.
description: Landing page and searchable archive for every ROCA plus supplemental products (Russian mobilization, Ukrainian deep strikes). Useful for backfilling a settlement-by-settlement timeline of frontline movement.

title: Jamestown Foundation - Eurasia Daily Monitor
reliability_notes: Long-running daily briefing relying heavily on Russian-language open sources; individual article sourcing quality varies and the editorial line is consistently anti-Kremlin.
description: Daily analytical articles on Russian military operations in Ukraine, often summarising Russian-language reporting on specific axes and units.

title: Lawfare - Ukraine coverage
reliability_notes: Legal and policy focus; military-operational content is secondary and it performs no independent geolocation.
description: Analysis of the legal, cyber and accountability dimensions of the war, including OSINT-evidence admissibility questions relevant to verifying frontline incidents.

title: Modern War Institute at West Point
reliability_notes: US Army-affiliated, so framing is doctrinal and lessons-focused rather than current-intelligence; no verification function.
description: Practitioner-oriented articles on how the Ukraine frontline actually functions (drone kill webs, assault-group tactics, the transparent battlefield), explaining why the line is shaped as it is.

title: NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence (Riga)
reliability_notes: NATO-accredited but not NATO command; work is information-environment focused and does not assess ground control.
description: Studies of Russian information operations, Telegram ecosystems and social-media manipulation, directly relevant to judging the reliability of frontline claims circulating online.

title: NUPI - Norwegian Institute of International Affairs
reliability_notes: Academic institute; Ukraine military content is limited relative to its Russia politics and Arctic work.
description: Research and podcasts on Russian military and political behaviour in the war, useful as northern-European analytic context.

title: OSW - Centre for Eastern Studies (Poland)
reliability_notes: Polish state research institute; the daily war analyses are concise, well sourced and explicitly dated by day-of-war, though framing is Polish-security-policy oriented.
description: Publishes a numbered daily 'day N of the war' analysis naming specific axes, settlements and strike targets - one of the most consistent non-ISW daily written frontline products.

title: PISM - Polish Institute of International Affairs
reliability_notes: Polish MFA-affiliated; bulletins are short policy notes rather than operational assessments.
description: Regular bulletins on Russian military and political developments affecting the frontline and on Western support decisions.

title: RAND Corporation - Ukraine research
reliability_notes: US federally funded; methodologically transparent but publishes on strategy and war termination rather than current frontline status.
description: Rigorous studies on attrition dynamics, war termination scenarios and force planning that frame long-run frontline stability or collapse.

title: Rochan Consulting - Ukraine Conflict Monitor (Konrad Muzyka)
reliability_notes: Single-analyst product with repeated Ukraine field visits; explicitly separates confirmed from claimed advances but the detailed weekly report sits behind a paid tier.
description: Weekly axis-by-axis operational review of Russian and Ukrainian advances with maps, widely regarded as the most disciplined commercial frontline monitor. Company site: https://rochan-consulting.com/

title: Royal Danish Defence College
reliability_notes: Military-academic institution; Ukraine analysis appears as occasional briefs and much of the best material is Danish-language.
description: Publishes military-professional assessments of the Russo-Ukrainian war, including operational-art critiques of both sides' offensives.

title: RUSI - Ukraine research
reliability_notes: Draws on repeated in-country fieldwork and interviews with Ukrainian units (Watling/Reynolds), so tactical detail is strong but publication is episodic and locations are often deliberately generalised.
description: Deep tactical and operational studies of how both armies actually fight (drone-artillery kill chains, defensive belts), which explains why the line moves where it does rather than pinpointing it.

title: Silverado Policy Accelerator
reliability_notes: Small policy accelerator whose Ukraine work is project-based (sanctions, supply chains, geospatial pilots); cadence is unpredictable.
description: Occasional data-driven Ukraine projects including geospatial and economic-warfare analysis; useful for supply-line and logistics context behind frontline sustainment.

title: SWP - German Institute for International and Security Affairs
reliability_notes: Funded by the German Chancellery; rigorous, peer-reviewed and slow, with no tactical mapping and a policy-advice framing.
description: Authoritative German assessments of the war's military and diplomatic course, including analyses of Russian force regeneration and European support capacity.

title: War on the Rocks
reliability_notes: Curated commentary platform; authors range from senior practitioners to academics with no uniform verification standard.
description: Frequent expert essays and podcasts on the Ukraine war's operational and strategic dynamics, including recurring assessments of offensive prospects.

title: Wilson Center - Kennan Institute
reliability_notes: Congressionally chartered, scholarly and regional-studies oriented; not a military-tracking source.
description: Regional expertise on Russia and Ukraine including occupied-territory governance, useful for interpreting events behind the line of contact.

title: archive.today
reliability_notes: Captures on-demand single-page snapshots including many pages the Wayback Machine cannot, but it is anonymously operated with no formal preservation guarantee and often demands CAPTCHAs.
description: On-demand snapshot service for preserving individual frontline claims, Telegram web previews and news pages at a specific moment.

title: Bellingcat Auto Archiver
reliability_notes: Open-source and actively maintained; requires self-hosting and API credentials for some platforms, and Telegram/X changes periodically break extractors.
description: Automates archiving of Telegram, X and YouTube posts with hashes and metadata into spreadsheets - the standard way to preserve frontline footage before it is deleted.

title: Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit
reliability_notes: Community-maintained and mostly current, but individual listed tools die without notice and entries are not systematically re-tested.
description: The canonical curated catalogue of verification tools, with a dedicated geolocation category covering reverse image search, satellite imagery, shadow analysis and map resources.

title: Internet Archive Wayback Machine
reliability_notes: Free and API-accessible with excellent longevity, but captures are incomplete for dynamic pages and it does not capture Telegram media reliably.
description: Preserves and timestamps frontline claims, official statements and maps so that a later-edited or deleted source can still be cited and dated.

title: OpenTopoMap
reliability_notes: Rendered from OSM plus SRTM elevation; contour accuracy is limited by SRTM resolution and OSM completeness in Ukraine.
description: Free topographic rendering with contour lines and relief, used to match terrain shape, treelines and elevation cues visible in frontline video.

title: OSINT Framework
reliability_notes: Broad tree-structured directory but noticeably stale in places, with dead links and no Ukraine-specific curation.
description: A general directory of OSINT tools including geolocation, imagery and social-media sections; useful as a breadth check against the more curated Bellingcat toolkit.

title: Overpass Turbo (OpenStreetMap query engine)
reliability_notes: Extremely powerful for feature-based search but entirely dependent on OSM completeness, which varies sharply across Ukrainian oblasts; heavy queries get rate-limited.
description: Lets you search Ukraine for structures matching features seen in footage (water towers, grain silos, level crossings, church types) and export candidate coordinates - the core needle-in-haystack geolocation tool.

title: PeakVisor
reliability_notes: Designed for mountains, so it is of limited use across Ukraine's steppe but valuable for horizon matching where relief exists.
description: Identifies terrain skylines and viewsheds from a candidate viewpoint, allowing horizon profiles in footage to be matched against a proposed location.

title: SunCalc
reliability_notes: Astronomically accurate but only as good as the shadow measurement fed into it; overcast footage and short shadows give wide error bands.
description: Computes sun azimuth and elevation for any coordinate and time, letting you chronolocate frontline footage from shadow direction and length, or confirm a candidate location's orientation.

title: Telegago (Telegram search via Google CSE)
reliability_notes: A community-built Google custom search over t.me and related mirrors; it only reaches Google-indexed pages, so recent or low-traffic posts are frequently missed.
description: Free keyword search across public Telegram content, useful for finding all channels that posted a given frontline claim or settlement name.

title: yt-dlp
reliability_notes: Actively maintained open source supporting Telegram, YouTube and X; extractors break when platforms change and some sources need cookies.
description: Downloads frontline videos at source quality with metadata so frames can be extracted for geolocation and the file hashed and archived before deletion.

title: Telemetr
reliability_notes: Telegram channel analytics and post search with a free tier; coverage of small or private channels is limited and the sibling domain telemetr.io was unreachable from some networks during checking.
description: Alternative Telegram archive and search platform for locating original posts of frontline footage, tracking channel reach, and preserving posts that are later deleted.

title: Yandex Images reverse image search
reliability_notes: Best-in-class for Eastern European and Russian-language visual matches, which is why the OSINT community relies on it; it is a Russian service, so operational-security caution applies and coverage varies unpredictably.
description: The single most effective reverse image search for matching frontline photos and video stills to prior imagery of the same location in Russia and Ukraine.

title: Bing Visual Search
reliability_notes: Useful as a third opinion because its index differs from Google's, but results are inconsistent for rural Ukrainian scenes.
description: A complementary reverse image search engine; running the same still through Yandex, Google and Bing materially raises the chance of a location match.

title: FotoForensics
reliability_notes: Error-level analysis is easily misread and cannot prove manipulation on its own; uploads are public by default, which is a real operational-security issue.
description: Image forensics (ELA, metadata, thumbnail analysis) for testing whether a purported frontline photo has been edited before you invest in geolocating it.

title: Google Earth Pro (desktop, historical imagery)
reliability_notes: Free desktop client with the historical-imagery slider and measurement tools; Ukrainian rural base imagery can be years old and update timing is opaque.
description: The workhorse for confirming geolocations against pre-war satellite imagery, measuring distances between landmarks, and comparing terrain across dates.

title: Google Lens
reliability_notes: Strong at object and text recognition (road signs, unit markings) but weaker than Yandex at exact-place matching in the post-Soviet space.
description: Reverse image and visual search used to identify landmarks, signage and vehicles in frontline footage as a first step in geolocation.

title: InVID / WeVerify Verification Plugin
reliability_notes: EU-funded browser plugin bundling keyframe extraction, multi-engine reverse search, metadata and magnifier tools; project funding has ended so some services degrade over time.
description: One-stop browser toolkit for verifying frontline video: splits a clip into keyframes and pushes them to several reverse image engines at once, plus metadata and forensic filters.

title: Mapillary
reliability_notes: Crowdsourced street-level imagery with an API; Ukrainian coverage is patchy and mostly pre-2022, and Meta ownership means terms can change.
description: Provides pre-war ground-level imagery of Ukrainian roads and villages for matching buildings, fences and poles seen in frontline footage.

title: Mapy.com (formerly Mapy.cz)
reliability_notes: Its aerial and hiking layers are unusually detailed for Central and Eastern Europe; coverage quality drops the further east you go in Ukraine.
description: Alternative satellite and topographic basemap with different imagery vintages from Google, frequently decisive when a Google tile is too old or cloudy.

title: Picarta.ai image geolocation
reliability_notes: AI predictions are probabilistic and frequently wrong at village scale; must be treated as a hypothesis generator that still requires manual confirmation, and uploading sensitive imagery to a third party carries risk.
description: AI-based image geolocation that proposes candidate coordinates for a photo, useful for narrowing the search area before manual terrain matching.

title: ShadeMap
reliability_notes: Models terrain and building shadows globally from elevation data; building footprints in rural Ukraine are incomplete, limiting fine-grained matching.
description: Simulates shadows cast at a given place, date and time over real terrain - a strong cross-check when confirming a candidate geolocation from shadow patterns in video.

title: TinEye
reliability_notes: Excellent at finding the earliest known appearance of an exact image but poor at near-duplicate or scene matching; API access is paid.
description: Establishes whether a purportedly new frontline image is actually recycled from an earlier date - the fastest check against chronologically false claims.
